Promoting Gender Equality and Inclusion Promoting Gender Equality and Inclusion by ending Sexual and Gender Based Violence in South Sudan Gender inequality gaps in South Sudan continue to widen as Gender Based Violence cases increase. According to Protection Analysis Update, Jan-Mar 2022, It notes that the situation of women and girls in South Sudan is daunting: conflict-related sexual violence is widespread and systematic and it is seen as a form to disrupt the fabric of communities, lack of accountability is exacerbated by conflict with poor socio-economic conditions of women and girls contributing to harmful social and gender norms practices.
This project will work to tackle the unequal power relations and harmful social and gender norms that contribute to GBV using Plan's gender transformative approach.
These will be done  through our gender transformative programming and influencing and Community engagement approach that addresses the root cause of power imbalance. Plan mainstreams GBV, safeguarding and PSEA in all its programs by mitigating risk to the people that we work with and ensuring that they feel safe while working with us. Interventions shall be tailored to have the involvement and participation of men, women, girls and boys in diversity including persons with disabilities.

The project will involve key actors in GBV response and prevention through taking leadership of the Protection Cluster or GBV sub Cluster at the state and county level. Currently, Plan International leads the protection Cluster in Nimule and Co-chair the protection Cluster in Yei. Also, in the rest of the states Plan International has been an active member in the cluster meetings and activities as a member. Plan will build on this to support the initiative of the cluster in coordinating GBV prevention and response interventions. 

Plan International will create, engage and maintain linkages/ relationships with  the key stakeholders and partners, such as Government including Ministry of Gender, police, judiciary including the ABC Court (A- the grassroots traditional court system at the Boma level headed by the Boma Chief;  B- middle traditional court headed by the Payam Head chief; and C- Last Traditional Court system headed by the Paramount chief at County level), religious institutions, cultural and community leaders, etc.

While building on the projects like Action Research on Violence against Women and Girls; Youth Voices in Eastern Equatoria, Integrated response to conflict-affected at-risk boys, girls, women and men in Central Equatoria State, South Sudan, Improving the quality and access in provision of life-saving integrated Health, Protection, Education and Nutrition services for vulnerable children and targeted communities in Pibor county, Jonglei State and Humanitarian protection measure for children and young people affected by South Sudan Crisis(GFFO) in Lakes state, among other Protection/ GBV projects that Plan International implements.

The project will be implemented in collaboration with the State Ministry of Gender, GBV cluster/partners, community leaders and women and youth groups at different levels. Plan International will ensure that these life-saving interventions eg PSS and referrals are provided to critically needed GBV survivors including vulnerable groups and other special cases such as Persons with disabilities. Cases with compounding medical conditions will be supported through CVA and referred for clinical management.
The project will mobilize communities to form drama groups that will will be trained and supported to conduct awareness raising on GBV in communities through radio, community mobilization and sensitization, participating in advocacy events such as 16 days of activism, etc. Youth will be mobilized into groups/ clubs as Champions of Change(CoC) plays a pivotal role in peer to peer mobilization of young people to challenge negative and discriminatory social norms that contribute to GBV. 
COVID-19 mitigation measures will especially those affecting public gatherings will be strengthened with COVID SOPs and items to effect COVID.

Multisectoral and coordinated emergency response directed to the most vulnerable population affected by the complex crisis in Venezuela Respuesta integral en seguridad alimentaria y nutricional de emergencia para la población más vulnerable afectada por la crisis en Venezuela.  Acción Contra el Hambre (ACH) en Venezuela atiende las necesidades humanitarias de los grupos más vulnerables en riesgo de desnutrición aguda: < de 5 años, 5 – 14 años, mujeres embarazadas y lactantes (MEL), personas con discapacidades o con problemas de salud, en particular adultos mayores. Son agravantes las situaciones de pobreza y necesidades básicas no satisfechas como la falta de acceso a: alimentos, condiciones higiénico-sanitarias adecuadas, servicios de salud, y medios de vida. La desnutrición y el deterioro de la salud repercuten en una mayor exposición a factores agravantes como la violencia de género, embarazos adolescentes y criminalidad. A través del HRP, ACH brindará una respuesta humanitaria para la reducción del sufrimiento y ayudar a salvar vidas, identificando casos de desnutrición aguda y severa en las familias más a riesgo. Se trabajará a nivel comunitario y se coordinará con instituciones locales, en particular con escuelas y centros de salud. ACH trabaja con un enfoque de programa país y dentro de una estrategia regional, con intervenciones complementarias e integrales en: 1) Nutrición: sensibilización y consejerías; detección, tratamiento de la desnutrición aguda, y derivación de los casos con complicaciones médicas; capacitación en el manejo preventivo de la desnutrición aguda; 2) Salud: atención primaria, equipos, insumos, medicamentos, métodos anticonceptivos; 3) Seguridad Alimentaria y medios de vida: distribución de alimentos y apoyo para la producción de alimentos; 4) ASH: acceso a servicios de agua, saneamiento, e higiene, en escuelas y centros comunitarios; distribución de kits de higiene, y rehabilitación/reparación de sistemas de abastecimiento de agua y de saneamiento en comunidades. El sector de Protección y género, de manera transversal, trabajará en prevención de VBG, nuevas masculinidades y DSSR; establecimiento y/o fortalecimiento de espacios seguros para mujeres y niñas; atención psico-social, distribución de kits de higiene menstrual y protección para mujeres en riesgo. La respuesta actual de ACH se concentra en Caracas DC, Guárico, Carabobo, Miranda, Zulia, Bolívar, y próximamente en Falcón, Amazonas y Sucre.

Enhancing access to learning opportunities and protection outcomes for children through provision of quality integrated education and child protection services and strengthening community level mechanisms resulting in a safer environment for children and their families in targeted LGAs Borno state Addressing urgent protection and psychosocial needs of children and adolescents through mobile response in Northeast Nigeria Plan International’s mobile programming has been effectively used in its German Federal Foreign Office (GFFO) funded project in 6 LGAs of Borno State. Plan proposes using the mobile unit approach in the four targeted LGAs of Borno. The mobile response ensures the deployment of the mobile team within 72 hours of a specific request, or of a report from relevant humanitarian clusters groups of acute needs. In cases of first response, the mobile unit will be deployed for a period of 6 and up to 12 weeks to provide urgent lifesaving assistance including provision of cash transfer. The mobile team currently is based in Maiduguri and serves LGAs within Borno state. They are being deployed in Kaga, Damboa, Bama, and four different locations of Maiduguri Metropolitan City-Jere, Madinatu, Bolori and Teachers village camp. The team can also be stationed in other field locations like Mubi, Dikwa, Pulka or Gwoza and be deployed from there. The mobile protection team will conduct a participatory rapid needs assessment, engaging the affected population to identify immediate needs. The outcome of the rapid assessment will be used to determine the line of response and also to identify existing community based services. Based on the findings of the assessment a rapid referral pathway will be developed to guide the provision of protection services to the children and adolescents. The referral pathway will be disseminated among stakeholders and will be used to coordinate actors providing services on the ground especially during the first line of response which will include provision of direct case management services. 
In addition, the mobile team will set up rapid complaints and feedback response mechanism to address issues of protection of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) as well as advocate for services that are needed and not available. Communities will be engaged to identify the most suitable and safe mechanisms to raise complaints and provide feedback on both services and operations of the mobile team and other available community services. The mobile team will provide targeted response for high-risk children including children with no suitable caregivers, children at risk of abuse in their current care arrangements, and UASC

Fortalecimiento de la Red de Atención Primaria de Salud y Comunitaria en la atención materno-infantil, mujeres en edades reproductivas y adolescentes, estado Miranda, municipio Sucre, parroquia Petare FORTALECIMIENTO DE LA RUTA MATERNA A NIVEL DE LA RED DE ATENCIÓN PRIMARIA EN SALUD/ ÁREAS DE SALUD INTEGRAL COMUNITARIAS EN LOS ESTADOS MIRANDA Y ZULIA Este Proyecto está orientado a la inclusión de grupos poblacionales constituidos por mujeres gestantes, puérperas, niños, niñas y adolescentes, en las que barreras geográficas, institucionales y culturales les impide tener acceso a servicios de salud, en este caso a salud sexual y reproductiva.
La Asociación Civil Redes Integrales de salud desde 2018 ha mantenido un trabajo permanente en los estados: Aragua, Carabobo, Falcón, Lara, La Guaira, Mérida, Miranda, Táchira, Trujillo, Zulia y el Distrito Capital, a través del monitoreo de indicadores, que dan cuenta de la implementación de la Ruta Materna, en cuanto a: número de referencias oportunas de las gestantes de control prenatal para la atención del parto en hospitales de referencia, número de partos, prevención de la transmisión vertical de sífilis y VIH, seguimiento nutricional de las gestantes y enfermedades prevalentes de la infancia, particularmente diarreicas y respiratorias agudas,  control postnatal e inmunizaciones; los cuales evidencian la situación de la salud materno/infantil en centros de salud priorizados en los estados mencionados y, sirve de base para el conocimiento de las necesidades de poblaciones que son responsabilidad de esos  centros de salud.
La propuesta de fortalecer la Ruta Materna, como una ruta que permite articular en cada territorio social acciones institucionales a través de una unidad básica territorial denominada Área de Salud Integral Comunitaria (ASIC), orientada a garantizar respuestas bajo un modelo de atención con enfoque familiar y comunitario en los cuales se encuentran ubicados  los Ambulatorios que fueron priorizados en los Planes de Salud Estadales bajo los criterios de  presencia de equipos básicos de salud, comunidad organizada y alta frecuencia  de embarazos no controlados y, que para el caso de esta propuesta fueron seleccionados en el estado Miranda son, según sus Ejes Territoriales: Mirandinos: Puerta Morocha, Montaña Alta, Francisco de Miranda y Camatagua. Metropolitano: Araguaney, Bloque 1, Medicentro, La Urbina, San Miguel Arcángel, Los Dos Caminos, La Suiza y Joaquín Blanco. Guarenas-Guatire: Care 1, Casa Amiga de la Salud, Bellard, El Mirador, Menca de Leoni y en el estado Zulia: Encontrados (Mcpio. Catatumbo), La Laguna (Mcpio. Guajira), Campo Lara (Mcpio. Lagunillas) Cuatro Bocas y Santa Cruz (Mcpio. Mara), El Tokuko, Toromo y Las Piedras (Mcpio. Machiques de Perijá), Cuatricentenario, San Jacinto, Cujicito, Los Claveles, Centro de Atención al Indígena y La Victoria (Mcpio. Maracaibo) y EL Silencio, Sierra Maestra y San Felipe (Mcpio San Francisco). Cuya finalidad es dotarlos de equipos médicos (tensiómetro. estetoscopio, infantometro, balanza, tallímetro, equipos de otorrino, cinta métrica, gestometro, doppler fetal)  y no médicos (escritorio, sillas) y formación a los equipos básicos de salud y comunidades, para el desarrollo de capacidades en: factores protectores de la vida, control prenatal, prevención y control de la transmisión vertical de sífilis y VIH,  gestantes de bajo peso, inmunizaciones, implementación de formato de la tarjeta de vacunación, referencia oportuna de gestantes, identificación de los síntomas y signos de alarma en la emergencia obstétrica y violencia obstétrica. Asimismo se trabajará con promotoras comunitarias para que conjuntamente con equipos de salud y comunidades faciliten la concepción de un Parto Humanizado para proteger los derechos de las mujeres durante la gestación, parto, postparto, lactancia y crianza bajo el enfoque de los cuidados cariñosos y sensibles de la primera infancia (OPS/UNICEF) y así, contribuir al mejoramiento de las condiciones para alcanzar una maternidad segura.

Comunidades Waraos protectoras, resilientes y empoderadas – Abeje para los Waraos Programa Nutrifamilias FUNDANA FUNDANA desde hace 30 años, a través de su entidad de atención, ha brindado un hogar protector a más de 32.000 niños, niñas y adolescentes (NNA) víctimas de maltrato, abuso o negligencia. Producto de la crisis social y económica, en nuestra organización hemos evidenciado un aumento significativo de niños y niñas con desnutrición infantil, motivado a una situación económica precaria, impactando negativamente en su alimentación y salud.

En respuesta a esta problemática en 2017 se decide inaugurar el Programa de Atención y Recuperación Nutricional ¨Nutrifamilias¨, que tiene como objetivo promover la recuperación nutricional de los niños, niñas con riesgo o desnutrición aguda sin complicaciones, mujeres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia (MEL), que además se encuentren en situación de vulnerabilidad social, facilitando su rehabilitación y posterior reinserción a la comunidad.

Para el 2023 el Programa espera atender 6.200 NN menores de 5 años y 2054 Mujeres embarazadas y lactantes a través de tamizaje nutricional, 7500 NNA de 2 a 14 años desparasitados, 375 NN y 375 NN de 6 a 59 meses reciben tratamiento para la desnutrición aguda y suplementos para la vulnerabilidad nutricional respectivamente. Asimismo, 8.254 personas reciben consejería en prácticas claves en temas de Nutrición, WASH y Protección NNA. También, 1.875 personas acceden a productos de higiene y tienen acceso a agua segura. Además, 50 profesionales de salud de la red ambulatoria aliada se ven fortalecidos a través de la capacitación en temas de nutrición y WASH. Finalmente, 120 familias donde uno de sus miembros cursa con desnutrición aguda y tiene una alta vulnerabilidad psicosocial reciben acompañamiento por promotores de convivencia familiar. 

Por otra parte, el Programa contempla la conformación de grupos estables de padres y cuidadora para sensibilizaciones en temas relacionados a la alimentación del lactante y niño pequeño ALNP-E, a fin de fomentar el desarrollo de capacidades y promover estrategias EDC. 
El programa Nutrifamilias se ejecuta en 6 Centros de Protección ubicados en los estados Miranda; municipio Sucre y Baruta  y Distrito Capital; municipio Libertador. Asimismo, se establecerán alianzas con 5 Centros de Salud en comunidades periféricas a los Centros de Protección de FUNDANA a fin de acortar las brechas de acceso a los servicios de nutrición, WASH y Protección. 

Adicionalmente, la estrategia intersectorial de Nutrición, WASH y Protección es una respuesta integral que busca centrar los servicios en el individuo, por medio de una visión integradora y respaldada que responda a sus distintas necesidades y enfocada en la sostenibilidad y la resiliencia.

Finalmente, la participación de los beneficiarios durante todas las fases del proyecto permite medir necesidades sentidas, tener retroalimentación de las acciones y mejorar los servicios constantemente. Para ello, todos los datos estarán desagregados por género, edad, discapacidad y  diversidad, a fin de tener in enfoque inclusivo y adaptado al contexto.

Asistencia multisectorial para la disminución de la vulnerabilidad y el acceso a servicios de protección, seguridad alimentaria, medios de vida y salud de la población vulnerable en Delta Amacuro Protección de Niños, Niñas y Adolescentes en riesgo, y fortalecimiento de las capacidades de cuidado de sus familias  El proyecto tiene como objetivo promover la protección integral y el ejercicio de derechos de los Niños, Niñas y Adolescentes (NNA) con riesgos de protección y en mayor vulnerabilidad, así como, atender a sus familias para la sostenibilidad de la protección y el alcance del bienestar. Incorpora un componente de desarrollo de medios de vida de las familias de las que hacen parte los NNA, así como, del fortalecimiento de su capacidad de crianza positiva, cuidado adecuado a la edad de los NNA y de la prevención de violencia y otros importantes que pueden impactar a las familias, particularmente a los NNA. 

El proyecto está dirigido principal y prioritariamente a NNA en movilidad, NNA separados de sus progenitores y al cuidado de familiares o terceros, NNA de comunidades indígenas y afrodescendientes, NNA de madres adolescentes y adultas jóvenes, NNA víctimas o en riesgo de violencia, reclutamiento a actividades delictivas, violentas o de explotación, NNA en riesgo de protección y que no ejercen o acceden a sus derechos por no poseer documentos de identidad (acta de nacimiento, cédula, otros), al estar fuera de la escuela, no acceder a la nutrición/alimentación adecuada, no recibir la asistencia en salud que requiere, entre otros, que los exponen a riesgos y deterioran el adecuado desarrollo. 
Desde un enfoque de protección integral, se identificarán los NNA con riesgos de protección en y con las comunidades, se evaluará su situación y necesidades, se proveerán servicios psicosociales, en protección legal y social, así como serán refridos y acompañados para acceder a serviciso complementarios brindados por el sistema de protección público y por otros actores no gubernamentales.  Se establecerán las vías de derivación seguras a través del trabajo articulado con organismos competentes como el CPNNA, CMDNNA, Ministerio Público, DdP entre otras.
 Adicionalmente, la intervención incluye procesos de prevención, formación psicosociales y vinculación con los NNA en las comunidades, que incluirá el entrenamiento en habilidades para la vida, sociales, importancia de la diversidad, la protección personal,  y primeros auxilios psicológicos y cooperación, para que aprendan a identificar situaciones en sí mismos y cuándo un amigo o compañero experimenta estrés, angustia o sentimientos de tristeza, cómo expresar sus emocionas y cómo brindar apoyo. Estos procesos apuntan a fortalecer la experiencia colectiva propiedad de la edad de los NNA, a fortalecer capacidades afectivas, cognitiva y sociales personales que le permitan mitigar y retardar el acercamiento a riesgos del contexto, y a estar en mejores condiciones para enfrentarlos. 

El componente de desarrollo de los medios de vida y fortalecimiento de la capacidad de cuidado y protección de los NNA de las familias se llevará a cabo: 
(i)Actividades de información, orientación y psicoeducación de las personas cuidadoras de los NNA: madres, abuelos u otras familias en condición de vulnerabilidad cabezas de hogar, hombres solos cabeza de hogar y con NNA de los perfiles descritos antes. Las actividades coadyuvarán a su resiliencia, estabilidad emocional y fortalecimiento de capacidades de crianza positiva y para la protección y cuidado de los NNA ante un contexto retador de violencia, separación, movilidad, entre otras. Esto se desplegará mediante la aplicación de metodologías escalables.
(ii)Formación, orientación, acompañamiento y entrega de asistencia en especie y mediante servicios para el desarrollo o fortalecimiento de medios de vida o de generación de ingreso que le permitan a las familias mitigar la difícil situación económica que atraviesan y responder a necesidades básicas, de modo que puedan facilitarse acciones de protección y cuidados de los NNA que las integran.  
El proyecto plantea una mirada multisectorial y promueve el nexo entre lo humanitario con respuesta a necesidades y el desarrollo, trabajando en fortalecimiento de las familias y la protección de NNA en las comunidades

Education in Emergency support in Duk County	Provision of Inclusive Quality Education for Out-of-School Children in Duk County - Jonglei  State Provision of Inclusive, Protective & Effective Education Services to Conflict-affected Children & Youth in Jonglei & Upper Nile States. This CMD’s Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) for 2022 seeks to provide inclusive, protective and effective education services to accelerate learning recovery and make schools more equitable, efficient and resilient for 7, 339 (3, 302 girls) school-aged children, 250 (50 female) teachers, 275 (82 female) PTA members and 60 (10 female) local education officials in 6 Counties of Jonglei & Upper Nile States by building on investments made during the Pandemic and previous years of EiE programming in South Sudan.

The expected results are equalised participation and improved learning outcomes across gender and disability for 7, 339 (45% female) children and youth through provision of essential school facilities and supplies, psychosocial support, gender-sensitive delivery of curriculum, classroom management, teacher conduct and schoolyard dynamics in 25 target schools (5 ECD centers, 15 primary schools, and 5 secondary schools) in Ayod, Uror & Duk Counties of Jonglei State and Ulang, Nasir and Longechuk Counties of Upper Nile State respectively. These 7, 339 children (5-17) and 250 teachers will be provided with teaching and learning materials in the form of 10 ECD learner kits, 250 learner kits for primary and 10 learner kits for secondary schools. 250 recreational kits will be provided to enhance learning and play and psychosocial wellbeing during schooling.

For their protective and safe school environment, 30 temporary learning spaces will be established in line with Inter-INEE's Minimum Standards for Education in Emergencies and Standards in Education Cluster Strategy 2019; and 30 gender segregated latrines and 30 water points in line with INEE and sphere standards. (unit of measurement: 1:60 for boys, 1:30 for girls). CMD will distribute 95 (500-litre) plastic water tanks with taps, 95 (50-litre) hand-washing tanks with taps and on their metal stands; 285 (1-litre) liquid sanitisers, 190 cartons of toilet soap, 95 bags (20 kgs) of detergent/powder soap, 95, 000 face masks, and 375 pairs of gumboots to provide sanitation and PPE for students and teachers. 2, 000 adolescent girls will receive dignity kits and undergo MHM sessions to better enhance their self-esteem and school attendance.

The plan targets 2, 339 (935 girls & 1, 404 boys) children in Ayod; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Uror; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Duk; 1, 000(400 girls & 600 boys) in Ulang; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Nasir; and 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Longechuk. 50 (10 female) teachers in Ayod; 40 (10 female) in Uror; 40 (10 female) in Duk; 40 (10 female) in Ulang; 40 (5 female) in Nasir; and 40 (5 female) in Longechuk will benefit from active EiE pedagogy that is centered on children and adolescents and their full development, and that responds to school needs and favours the equitable achievement of learning goals. These teachers will Improve the quality of gender and disability-inclusive education services and teachers' capacity to protect the wellbeing of all children and prevent the negative impact of the emergencies on learning environments.

Equally important, 75 (27 female) PTA members in Ayod; 40 (11 female) in Uror; 40 (11 female) in Duk; 40(11female) in Ulang; 40(11 female) in Nasir; and 40 (11 female) in Longechuk and 10 (1 female) education officials in Ayod, 10 (1) in Uror; 10 (1) in Duk; 10(1) in Ulang; 10(1) in Nassir; and 10 (1 female) in Longechuk will be trained in School Management, Psychosocial Support (PSS) and Disaster Risk Reduction in Education (DRR).

CMD will also conduct 12 Back to Learning (BTL) campaigns through public information campaigns intended for the entire affected population and/or awareness raising activities aimed at specific segments of the out-of-schoolchildren (OOSC) as well as current learners identified as most at-risk.

Provision of lifesaving General Protection and GBV prevention, mitigation and response services to 14,813 floods at risk women, girls, boys and men in Malakal, Upper Nile State Provision of comprehensive, lifesaving SGBV prevention and response interventions to the floods and conflict affected communities in Ayod, Duk, Fangak and Malakal Counties in Jonglei  and Upper Nile states. SAADO's proposed project will provide comprehensive, lifesaving SGBV prevention and response interventions to the floods and conflict affected communities in Ayod, Duk, Fangak and Malakal Counties in Jonglei and Upper Nile states respectively. The proposal will target 4,000 beneficiaries (1000 boys;1000 men;1000 women;1000 girls) in Malakal County and 10,672 beneficiaries (1974 boys, 2436 girls,2852 men and 3410 women) in Ayod, Duk and Fangak Counties of Jonglei state. SAADO proposes to implement comprehensive, lifesaving SGBV prevention and response activities by providing quality and timely, age appropriate, case management and psychosocial support to GBV survivors. 
The proposed project seeks to implement GBV prevention, response and risk mitigation activities by providing quality and timely, age appropriate, case management and psychosocial support to GBV survivors. Further, the proposed project will provide cash assistance to the most vulnerable women and girls visiting WGFSs who are facing financial challenges to facilitate them in accessing multi-sectoral GBV services. Priority will be given to survivors who require clinical management of rape (CMR) and survivors of Intimate Partner Violence (IPV) so that they can continue to visit health facilities, access for legal aid and they can also access the nearest available centers and safe spaces that provide PSS. 
This proposed project is designed to improve responses to cases of GBV and enhance the ability of survivors to recover from GBV incidences. SAADO will provide individual psychosocial support for women and girls in established women and girls' safe spaces in the targeted locations. The project's proposed activities will also include Strengthening Psychosocial Support services and collaboration with MHPSS working group, GBV awareness and risk mitigation measures, Strengthening the implementation of primary GBV preventions  interventions, Strengthening coverage of dignity kit distribution and programming as part of risk mitigation, GBV preparedness and contingency planning and provision of livelihood support, through the provision of need based capacity building trainings to GBV actors and frontline service providers and strengthening GBV case management and referral pathways. The activities in the established WGFS will be conducted using the guidelines from the ministry of health and World Health Organization (WHO) on COVID-19 prevention and will include maintaining social distance, wearing of masks and washing hands with soap. SAADO also intends to strengthen gender-based violence prevention through EMAP and community care programs to reduce GBV risks on men, women, boys and girls.
The targeted locations have been selected because of the prevalent needs stated in the HNO 2023 and appearing in category 5 and 4 in the severity mapping as well as SAADO's long standing presence  and GBV programming in Duk, Ayod, Fangak and Malakal Counties through implementation of CERF funded GBV Prevention & Response in Ayod including management of two (2) WGFS in Jiech and Mogok payams; GBV violence risk mitigation in Schools in Duk including management of (2) WGFS in Duk Pajut and Duk Pagak and four (4) WGFS established in Duk Poktap and Padiet and implementation of the South Sudan Humanitarian Funded (SSHF) GBV Prevention and Response project in Fangak since August 2022. 
The proposed project will build upon and complement SAADO's currently ongoing GBV prevention and response projects in the targeted locations. SAADO will coordinate this proposed response with the GBV sub cluster to ensure that the proposed activities are not duplicated and there is no overlap of activities and will work with health partners such as HRSS, CARE and John Dau Foundation to refer survivors for Post Rape services.

Provision of essential nutrition services for crisis affected people in Akobo Provision of Integrated lifesaving Nutrition interventions to conflict affected populations in Jonglei, Eastern Equatoria states and Abyei administrative area in South Sudan. Through the proposed response, Save the Children International will provide integrated lifesaving nutrition service to the population in Akobo West, Budi , Bor, Kapoeta, Lopa Lafon, Magwi, Nyirol, Torit Counties, and Abyei administrative area. The aim of this is to reduce suffering, morbidity, and mortality related to malnutrition among vulnerable populations, SCI's proposed response will focus both treatment and preventative approaches, using community-based management of acute malnutrition (CMAM) and infant and young child feeding (IYCF) approaches. SCI Emergency nutrition programs will include. i) Community mobilization to increase access and coverage of CMAM services, ii) Treatment of children and PWLs with acute malnutrition through inpatient and Outpatient therapeutic programs. iii) blanket Supplementary feeding program. iv) Institutional feeding program (IFP), v) Maternal dietary supplementation, vi) Promotion of optimal IYCF through mother-to-mother support groups. vii) Improving Dietary Diversity through household kitchen gardening, viii) Strengthen nutrition information systems and operations research to ensure an evidence-based response, ix) Building capacity for frontline nutrition workers and institutions at all levels. SCI will work through communities to promote, protect and support recommended IYCF practices through one-on-one counselling and group message and counselling. Besides the CMAM and behaviour change interventions, SCI will implement cash transfer intervention in selected areas targeting families of severely malnourished children and SAM PLW to maximize the program's nutrition outcomes and reduce the relapse of acute malnutrition among under-five children and PLW. Through this response, SCI will support 104 static OTP/TSFPs and eight stabilization centres integrated with health facilities. The service will be delivered through static and outreach/mobile facilities for remote and hard-to-reach areas in the targeted project locations. SCI will work with MOH, UNICEF and WFP to secure timely provision of Nutrition supplies necessary for Nutrition Service Delivery. SCI will reach 73,683 under-five Children and 66,992 PLW. 
SCI will make deliberate efforts to enhance coordination and integration with the Health, WASH, FSL, Protection and Education clusters to address the causes of malnutrition through a multi-sectoral approach that aims to reduce vulnerabilities, prevent malnutrition and build resilience among the vulnerable people. Specific multi-sectoral activities are to increase access to safe water and sanitation, promote critical WASH messages, and integrate early childhood development strategies in nutrition treatment sites. Kitchen gardening, screening and treating of malaria, managing diarrhea, and mainstreaming child protection and gender-based violence risk mitigation will also be promoted at the nutrition sites.y. SCI will also support hygiene interventions to improve nutrition outcomes and reduce risk of hygiene-related morbidities
SCI will monitor the nutrition situation and the needs of the affected people through KAP survey, SMART surveys, monthly nutrition programme data collection and analysis, and joint field monitoring visits. Spot checks, supportive supervision and monitoring visits will monitor service delivery and engage with the community and other stakeholders to gauge evolving needs. Community nutrition volunteers will be supported to undertake household visits, conduct regular screening of malnourished children and women to ensure timely detection and treatment, and report on a monthly basis. Data collection tools and analysis will be strengthened to enhance monitoring of integrated services

Scale up Life Saving Emergency Response in Shelter/NFIs for South Sudanese Returnees in Renk Emergency S/NFIs response to IDPs, Returnees and Host Community affected by disasters in South Sudan The project aims to provide Survival Kits /Emergency shelter/Non Food items both in-kind and in cash modalities to the most vulnerable persons, newly displaced/host communities and returnees. The project will focus on the life saving shelter/NFIs needs, as identified through assessment to protect the affected displaced people from harsh weather conditions and protection risks targeting all states of South Sudan. The intervention will be implemented through mobile response as well as using its static teams based in Kajo Keji, Juba, Koch, Mayom, Leer, Bor, Duk, Twic East, Akobo, Aweil, Wau and Alek. However the major focus areas will be Jonglei, Unity, Northern Bahrel Ghazal, Central, Western and Eastern Equatoria states. Cash programming will also be considered in areas where markets are fully or semi-functional and shelter/NFI items are available and accessible by the community. When blanket targeting is not applicable, the intervention will target mainly lactating and pregnant women, households with malnourished children, and households with members who have certain health complications. Besides unaccompanied children, unaccompanied elderly and persons with no community linkages will also be targeted.
The project will promote timely delivery of assistance through deployment of rapid response teams in line with humanitarian priorities for 2022 HRP's. NRC’s mobile response teams will be ready for deployment within 8 days to conduct assessments and within 22 days for full-fledged delivery of NFIs and emergency shelters and other activities per location. The project will also support returnees in settlement as part of the local integration or as they settle into their areas of origin. The project will benefit 120,000 individuals directly.

Life saving Protection assistances to Returnees, Refugees, and other vulnerable host communities in Renk and Melut Counties affected by the conflict in Sudan. Provision of emergency shelter and non-food items and solutions to vulnerable internally displaced persons, returnees and host community in Jonglei, Unity, Central and Eastern Equatoria States South Sudan, generally is still a tough place to live especially for the most vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host community. The intercommunal violence spread almost across the entire country, common in Jonglei, other areas in Upper Nile and Bar-el-ghazel regions. It is mostly the women and children who are often at most risk plus the youth who are mobilized to fight inappropriate wars.
The impact of COVID-19 and failing economy continue to bite, affecting mostly the locals who lost their casual jobs, businesses. The greatest impact is on land tenure linked with returns. Though there is no data collected to prove this, but as a local NGO, many vulnerable South Sudanese are being evicted from time to time; landlords increase their rents at will or evict their tenants for their returning families. It seems many are returning due to inability to sustain their living standards in the neighbouring countries of Uganda and Kenya for those living in the suburbs. This is also the case with refugees in the camps; unavailability of cultivation land, decreasing food rations, long COVID-19 lock down are some of the reasons fostering returns apart from the struggling and holding peace.
In Jonglei and Unity States, subnational violence that results in child abductions, cattle raids, loss of lives and displacements, destruction of property including shelters razed down, continue to severely affect the two states. Currently Bentiu in Unity is the only County rated by IPC in the HNO 2022 at the catastrophic level in South Sudan. The rest of the counties in Unity and Jonglei are just at level 4 which is still extreme for human conditions.

Floods have also caused displacements, increased animal diseases which is wiping out the livelihoods and exacerbating shelter and non-food items needs among the internally displaced persons.
Floods and chronic insecurity have made these two states inaccessible making it difficult for humanitarian aid to reach. This makes delivery of aid more expensive.
Central and Eastern Equatoria have recently been impacted much by conflicts especially with the cattle keepers from Jonglei who seek pasture for their cattle and often drive cattle to the farms of the host community. These conflicts continue to cause further displacements at a small but well spread scale. The destruction of crops and other livelihoods including the cattle that are finding no pasture due to severe impact of extremities of climate change is having its toll on South Sudanese. 
Ebola virus disease is also a looming threat to lives of the impoverished South Sudanese. WHO and IOM have supported the South Sudan Ministry of Health in early preparations in case of an outbreak.

Central and Eastern Equatoria have high number of anticipated returns as reported by REACH monitoring team. This means huge needs for shelter and non-food items. However in order to build the local economy through the local markets, HDC will respond through cash and voucher assistance since the markets are highly functional in these areas.
CVA is highly recommended by the cluster in the year 2023. HDC has implemented cash programming in the past years and is well positioned to implement the project with experience.
Though all areas in Central and Eastern Equatoria have functional markets, parts of the areas in Jonglei; Twic East, Pibor and Duk have limited functionality in the markets if not functional. In-kind response will be prioritized in these areas.
HDC is capitalizing on its static presence to promote integrated response by responding in target locations through both SNFI and Protection. This will embed the strategic objective 2 of ensuring centrality of protection in all emergency responses. This will ensure dignity and protection of the most vulnerable groups among the internally displaced, host community and returnees
The project will target 40,643 vulnerable individuals; 16,250 women, 8,143 men, 16,250 children, 6,000 older persons and PWDs.

Réponse multisectorielle et intégrée aux besoins humanitaires d'urgence des nouveaux déplacés et populations hôtes dans la Région du Nord Assistance humanitaire en WASH à 20 000 PDIs et 12 000 populations hôtes et vulnérables dans 6 communes des régions de la Boucle du Mouhoun, du Centre-Nord et du Nord du Burkina Faso La situation sécuritaire au Burkina Faso s’est détériorée depuis 2015 entrainant près de 1 719 332 déplacés Internes selon les données du CONASUR du 30 Septembre 2022. La violence quasi quotidienne est généralisée sur 77% du territoire (10 sur 13 régions), affectant principalement les populations civiles, notamment les femmes et les enfants. 
Dans les zones d’accueil, les ressources naturelles déjà limitées sont insuffisantes pour couvrir les besoins des ménages hôtes et des PDIs. Sur les sites de PDIs et au sein des communautés hôtes, les besoins de première nécessité comme l’approvisionnement en eau salubre, l’assainissement et les notions de base en bonnes pratiques sont insuffisants voire inexistants, ce qui engendre et/ou aggrave la situation nutritionnelle des personnes vulnérables en générales et des enfants de moins de cinq ans en particulier.
Selon l’enquête SMART nutritionnelle réalisée en Août 2022 par le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de l’hygiène (avec le concours de l’UNICEF, d’IRC, du PAM et de DAVYCAS International), les regions du Sahel, de l’Est, du Nord, du Centre-Nord et de la Boucle du Mouhoun sont les plus affectées par la crise nutritionnelle notamment les communes de Nouna, Tougan (dans la boucle du Mouhoun), Barsalogho et Pissila (dans le centre Nord). 
 En tant qu'acteur du Cluster WaSH, avec une présence dans ces communes particulièrement touches ainsi que dans celles de Titao et Ouahigouya où des projets sont déjà en cours, APADE dispose des capacités et de l'acceptance communautaire dans ces zones pour mettre en œuvre une réponse d’urgence WASH dans ces communes en vue de contribuer à l’appui de la prise nutritionnelle dans ces zones vulnérables, APADE en 2023 prévoit d’intégrer la WASH in Nut dans ses projets et d’en faire une priorité. Le paquet minimum Wash pour le couple/mère enfant sera assuré dans différents centre de santé notamment de la région du Nord, ainsi qu’un suivi des bénéficiaires en matière de bonnes pratiques d’hygiène jusque dans les ménages. Early action intervention to the expected floods through Health, Nutrition and Gender Based Violence interventions in Malakal, Upper Nile State Gender-based Violence (GBV) Prevention and Response for Conflict-Affected Population in South Sudan The GBV prevention and response program of International Medical Corps (IMC) in South Sudan aims to empower communities and build resilience through promoting social and behavioral change to address the root causes of GBV in the country. The project targets key population to create a sustainable change in attitude and practices through male engagement, working with community leaders and building capacity of local stakeholders. Leveraging on the vast experiences, gains, and successes of IMC in implementing GBV prevention and response interventions through the FCDO-HARISS program, ECHO, SSHF and UNFPA . This project will be continued to implement in the states of Western Bahr el Ghazal (Wau IDP Camp and County), Upper Nile and Malakal PoC and County), Unity (Nyal County), and in Canal/Pigi County. This project  will directly benefit about 27495 vulnerable women and girls across the target locations. One of the project’s key priorities is to further strengthen core services to survivors of GBV and other vulnerable women and girls in the aforesaid intervention sites. These services include quality case management using a survivor-centered approach, along with psychosocial support to enhance healing and recovery. IMC UK works to ensure that survivors’ holistic needs are met by providing multi-sectoral services, referring to health centers for clinical management of rape, to legal justice services and to other kinds of support based on the needs of survivors. In addition to individual Psychososcia support (PSS ) for survivors, IMC UK will continue with PSS group activities for all vulnerable women and girls in the women girls’ safe spaces (WGSS). To ensure sustainability of the project and ownership by the community, especially of the WGSSs, in Wau, Nyal Malakal, and Canal Pigi . IMC already established, leadership committee comprise of 8 members from the community selected by their fellow women with the responsibility to give support, information, feedback, and suggestions that will foster empowerment and ownership of the space and the overall wellbeing of their members. The women committee members will be further empowered with knowledge and skills through hands-on management of the spaces and co-leading with them on the daily functioning of the WGSS. The women committee will be continuously mentored and trained on GBV basic concepts, safe referral, and referral pathways, and on leadership and conflict management and facilitation techniques and on various psychosocial support activities using IMC’s and IRC’s global WGSS toolkit. IMC UK will implement holistic community engagement strategies on the promotion of long-term positive change in the targeted communities. IMC will use the GBV community mobilization tool called SASA! - Phase-based strategy to help communities rethink about “power” and the positive use of power. “Preventing Violence against Women and Girls: Engaging Men in Accountable Practice (EMAP)” is also another tool that will be used to ensure men engagement with accountability to prevent GBV in the targeted community in Nyal, Wau and Malakal. In addition, IMC trains and collaborates with GBV Taskforce members in Wau, Malakal and Nyal. These will be supported by staff IMC UK staff to do awareness raising, and safe confidential referral of any survivors who disclose to them. IMC UK will provide emergency cash assistance for case management to the vulnerable women and girls. Cash assistance is one of the interagency minimum standards in GBV programming in emergency. Additionally, IMC UK opts to implement cash assistance based on lesson learnt and feedback from women and girls on importance of cash assistance as lifesaving. IMC will procure and distribute dignity for the conflict-affected women and girls. The dignity kits will include sanitary items, as well as other items explicitly tailored towards the local needs of women and girls of reproductive age affected by the conflict.

Food security in South Sudan	Vulnerable populations protected against hunger and malnutrition. Improved food security and livelihoods of IDPs, Returnees and Vulnerable host communities in South Sudan The purpose of the project is to improve food consumption, food security, dietary diversity and coping strategies and enhance emergency food production of vulnerable populations in the targeted counties. This will be achieved through provision of Cash-Based Transfers (CBT) to address food needs of vulnerable communities during the lean season and provision of timely and appropriate complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs and fishing kits coupled with training in improved agronomic and fishing practices.
In line with the South Sudan FSL cluster HRP objectives and priorities, NPA will support vulnerable populations in IPC 4 and 5 locations as well as some IPC 3 locations. Specifically, NPA will target Canal/Pigi, Fangak, Pochalla and Bor South Counties of Jonglei State, Rumbek East, Rumbek Centre, Cueibet, Yirol East, Yirol West and Awerial Counties of Lakes State, Terekeka County of Central Equatoria State and Kapoeta North County of Eastern Equatoria State.

NPA seeks to support 86,200 HHs (517,200 individuals) through provision of complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs and fishing kits across the target counties. Some of the kits will be provided by FAO (core pipeline) while the rest will be procured and distributed directly by NPA to enhance food production.  NPA will build the capacity of the HHs supported with the kits through training on improved agronomic and fishing practices, marketing and group dynamics. A Training of Trainers (ToT) approach will be utilized whereby lead farmers and fisher folk will be trained by NPA. They will then train/share the knowledge and skills with other farmers and fisher folk in their communities. The kits provided through this project and the knowledge gained from the trainings is expected to improve the agricultural and fishing practices of the target HHs thus enhancing and sustaining food production. CBT interventions will target 1,000 HHs (6,000 individuals ) in Rumbek East, Rumbek Centre and Cuiebet Counties in Lakes State to improve their access to food, diversify and improve their food consumption and dietary diversity scores and promote the adoption of positive coping strategies. The planned interventions are aligned to the FSL cluster objectives 1 and 2 and will provide emergency assistance and livelihoods support to save lives and avert total collapse of livelihoods in the target counties.

NPA will integrate development-oriented and conflict-sensitivity activities in this project to enhance the resilience of  vulnerable HHs in line with the Triple Nexus. Therefore, 1,200 vulnerable HHs will be supported with small-scale cash grants to establish IGAs. The target HHs will be mobilized and sensitized to transition to and establish VSLA’s to ease access to financial services and encourage the spirit of saving among the VSLA group members. The IGAs will contribute to increasing and diversifying income and building the resilience of the target HHs at the same time improving functionality of local markets and boosting the local value chains.

NPA will employ a community-based beneficiary selection approach which will entail establishing Project Management Committees (PMCs) to lead the selection of eligible beneficiaries based on the beneficiary selection criteria. Vulnerable HHs with severe food insecurity including female, child, disabled/chronically ill headed HHs; persons living with or at risk of HIV/AIDS and the elderly will be targeted in this project. 
NPA will ensure meaningful engagement of the target communities throughout the project life-cycle through holding regular meetings with the PMCs and community members and Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) to get their feedback on the project. NPA will ensure that the feedback is incorporated in the implementation of this project and design of future projects. Further, NPA will use a community-based complaints and feedback mechanism to provide a platform for beneficiaries to voice any issues or concerns.

Area-Based Response: Provision of life-saving Health, Nutrition, WASH, and Protection services for the displaced people affected by crises and fighting in Gezira state Comprehensive humanitarian nutrition services for IDPs, returnees and vulnerable residents  The humanitarian nutritional needs in Sudan are expected to remain at high levels or worsen further in 2023, making Sudan one of the countries in the World with highest estimated acute malnutrition caseload.  While the overall Global acute malnutrition (GAM) remains at 13.6%, the prevalence of GAM varies significantly across the localities with very high situation (GAM above 15% and above as per WHO classification) reported in 64 localities. The proposed nutrition project aim is to improve equitable access to quality life-saving curative and preventive services through the systematic provision of nutrition services in South Kordofan, North Kordofan, Central Darfur, North Darfur, West Darfur, Sennar, Blue Nile and Red Sea states in which 29 localities will be covered. Vulnerable children under-five and PLWs are the main target of the project. Through SC -Nutrition interventions, a total of 362,874 beneficiaries will benefit from the services provided, among them (87,131 boys, 90,680 girls, 184,383 women, 680 men). Save the children will implement lifesaving, preventative interventions, treatment of severe and moderate acute malnutrition among children under five years and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLWs), referral of SAM children with medical complications and minor rehabilitation to nutrition sites. To reach the estimated targets and planned response scale up, the nutrition sector will deploy integrated response modalities with health sector, WASH, FSL, protection, education at facility and community levels. SC will deliver nutrition services through existing health facilities, mobile and outreach teams and at community such as mother-to mother support groups activities including IDPs and hard to reach areas, use of cash-based interventions to increase access and utilization of nutrition services through FSL will be used for most cases in need. In term of emergency response, rapid response mechanisms for timely delivery of nutrition interventions in the onset emergencies will applied.

Specific nutrition response strategies will include scaling up the minimum preventive and protection lifesaving intervention package for prevention of malnutrition, treatment, and geographical coverage of severe and moderate acute malnutrition among the under-fives, strengthening referrals for children suffering from SAM with medical complication through provision of transportation costs to and from the SC, nutrition system capacity strengthening (capacity and infrastructure) will be done to facilitate provision of quality and people centered life-saving nutrition responses, timely procurement and delivery of core nutrition supplies. Additionally, infant young child feeding (IYCF) and social behavior change, and communications (SBCC) will be strengthened to promote good feeding and access to services. SC will strengthen national and sub national partnership with all stockholders to deliver nutrition services. SC will ensure monthly and quarterly monitoring of the evolving nutrition situation through an early warning and early actions and implementation of SMART surveys in prioritized localities with GAM 20% and above as well as supporting other assessment initiatives such S3M and MICS.

Réponse communautaire de Protection de l’Enfant , de prise en charge sanitaire et de la fourniture des ABNA dans les régions de Tahoua et Tillabéri Prevention et Reponse aux VSGB   dans les Régions de Tillabéri, Diffa et Tahoua.  Plan International favorisera l'accès à des services adaptés à l'âge et au sexe des enfants et des familles touchés par le conflit du Centre Tahoua , Tillaberi et Diffa (au Niger ) et renforcera le cadre de vie protégé des personnes concernées. Cet objectif sera atteint grâce à la fourniture de conseils, à la gestion des cas et au soutien psychosocial, ainsi qu'à la réintégration et à la réhabilitation sociales en favorisant l'accès aux opportunités éducatives et aux activités génératrices de revenus. En outre, un soutien psychosocial communautaire sera fourni ainsi qu'une éducation parentale et nutritionnelle (y compris des groupes de pairs, un dialogue communautaire et le renforcement des réseaux de protection de l'enfance) afin d'ancrer le travail sur la violence sexuelle et sexiste dans la communauté et d'accroître son acceptation. La fourniture de biens de première nécessité permettra également de répondre aux besoins les plus urgents des bénéficiaires ciblés afin d'améliorer leur bien-être physique et de renforcer leur dispositif de protection. Ce projet appliquera l'approche des unités mobiles équipées de personnel qualifié pour atteindre les survivants de la VBG dans les zones difficiles d'accès du Centre Sahel. Les unités mobiles visiteront les communautés et fourniront des conseils psychosociaux aux victimes de VBG, une éducation parentale et nutritionnelle et des soins aux enfants par le biais d'espaces mobiles adaptés aux enfants et aux Jeunes (CFS). Les bénéficiaires recevront des connaissances leur permettant d'améliorer la prévention et le suivi des VBG et d'accroître la résilience des populations vulnérables. En outre, ils recevront des informations sur la santé et l'hygiène (et des articles si nécessaire) et seront orientés vers des établissements de santé (c'est-à-dire des cliniques locales) si nécessaire.

Réponse multisectorielle d'urgence aux besoins des enfants vulnérables dans les communes de Ouallam et Téra dans la Rregionse Tillabéri Améliorer l'accès aux services WASH pour les populations affectées par mouvement de population, épidémies et inondation de la région de Tahoua Malgré les efforts du Gouvernement dans l’amélioration de l’accès à l’eau potable et aux infrastructures d’assainissement de base pour les populations locales ainsi que les déplacées internes, refugiées et retournées, beaucoup de défit restent encore à relever notamment dans la réalisation et ou la réhabilitation des services sociaux de base. 

Le projet proposé se veut résiliant et vise à assister 18,000 personnes déplacées et communautés hautes vulnérables dans les départements affectés ainsi que les personnes affectées par les catastrophes et les épidémies. Il sera délivré la réhabilitation/réalisation des infrastructures d'eau et d'assainissement, la promotion de l'hygiène en milieu communautaire et dans les écoles y compris la GHM, la mobilisation communautaire ainsi que le renforcement de leur résilience. Notre stratégie d'intervention reposera sur celle du cluster WASH. Les aspects de protection transversale, de PSEA, des 5 engagements minimum ainsi que l'implication des bénéficiaires et le suivi/accompagnement des autorités locales seront au centre de la stratégie de mise en œuvre.
En termes d'innovation, VISION PLUS renforcera les capacités les communes à une auto-évaluation communautaire afin de permettre à la communauté d'avoir le sentiment que le projet leurs appartient. Nos expériences antérieures ont montré que quand la communauté a l'impression que le projet leur appartient, elle participera plus davantage dans la mise œuvre et le succès du projet est garantie.

Réponse multisectorielle d’urgence aux populations (hommes, femmes, filles et garçons ) affectées par l'insécurité alimentaire et besoin EHA dans la Commune Guéskerou, Région de Diffa Préparation et Interventions d'urgence EHA pour personnes victimes des inondations dans le département de Diffa Depuis plusieurs années, les catastrophes d’origine naturelle, auxquelles s’ajoutent les déplacements forcés des populations et les épidémies sont devenus récurrents. Elles perturbent les systèmes économiques, politiques, environnementaux et sociaux, menacent aussi la sécurité alimentaire et humaine et entravent les progrès dans le processus de développement du pays. Elles engendrent aussi des crises humanitaires d’ampleurs graves au niveau de nos populations qui se trouvent très souvent face à des besoins humanitaires multiples et multiformes. Parmi ces crises, les inondations qui sont de nos jours récurrentes causent beaucoup plus de dégâts. Une analyse rétrospective des pertes subies sur 40 ans (1973-2013) réalisée au Niger (DesInventar, 2016) a estimé à plus de 40 milliards de francs CFA de pertes annuelles dues aux inondations. Face à ces situations de crises et catastrophes, plusieurs actions d’atténuation et de protection de populations en général et de couches les plus vulnérables en particulier sont menées. Le département de Diffa reste confrontée à des catastrophes naturelles, dont la principale reste les inondations, suite à des pluies persistantes, le débordement de Komondougou  .
L’inondation dans le département de Diffa cette année a affecté 26.943 personnes (3.814 ménages) sinistrées et 108 maisons effondrées. Des familles ont perdu des proches, leurs biens, cultures et animaux. Ces inondations touchent aussi bien les zones urbaines que rurales. Dans les zones périurbaines de la région, les inondations sont devenues une réalité omniprésente qui affecte directement les populations pauvres.
Lors des inondations, des points d'eau potable sont souvent contaminées et leur structure est atteinte ou même détruite. Des installations d'assainissement comme latrines privées, publiques et dans les institutions sont également rendues inaccessible ou leur structure atteinte ou détruite. Le risque et incidences de maladies hydriques monte donc fortement, si des interventions d'urgence rapide ne sont pas entreprises.

Des groupes mixtes de gestion des points d’eau seront également mis en place ou redynamisés, et outillés, en incluant les femmes, les minorités communautaires et les personnes en situation de handicap. Palestine: Reaching vulnerable children and their caregivers	Child Protection Integrated psychosocial support and child protection services for the most affected boys and girls in the Gaza Strip Strip This project will support the delivery of quality, integrated child protection and psychosocial support (PSS) services to the most vulnerable boys and girls aged 6-18 in the Gaza Strip, especially those affected by the 2021/2022 escalations. The escalation has affected all aspects of life in the Gaza Strip, including child protection needs and services.

The project will ensure that 12 family centres and 30 outreach sites in Gaza are fully operational, responding to the pressing mental health and psychosocial and child protection needs of 11,900 children (50% girls) and 4,300 caregivers (20% males). Additionally, 9,900 children and adults will be reached with Explosive Remnants of War (ERW) awareness messages, while 300 non-child protection professionals and community members will benefit from training and coaching opportunities on child protection, detection, identification and referral. 

Service delivery will be directed to the most affected locations and the most vulnerable children through a coordinated continuum of services in Gaza. Each family centre will be connected to a community-based child protection committee that identify the child protection concerns and refer identified children to the family centre within that community. Family centres will operate through established Community-Based Organisations (CBOs) and outreach sites and will assess/screen and refer children for further specialised services through:
1) a case management approach for the most affected;
2) referral of severe and complicated child protection cases to child protection services (managed by relevant stakeholders and Civil Society Organizations (CSOs); and
3) referral of children with further psychosocial support needs to more specialized psychological support services.

Services will also strengthen outreach capacities to detect and link children in need with service providers while providing mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) through the family centres. A total of 11,900 children (50% girls) and 4,300 caregivers (20% males), as well as 300 community members will be reached through the project.

This project aligns with and contributes to the Protection Cluster Objective no. 2, which calls for putting in place protection response mechanisms to prevent and mitigate occupation and conflict-related violence.

Ensuring compliance with the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) principles and procedures, project beneficiaries will be oriented on prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse. They will receive information on UNICEF and other interagency channels, including SAWA Free toll number, social media platforms, and WhatsApp to report on PSEA.

At least 70% of the project budget will support the two project implementing partners to ensure that timely services are provided to children with protection and MHPSS needs. The funds will be transferred in line with UNICEF Harmonised Approach to Cash Transfer (HACT), which ensures close follow-up on expenditures. Partners are normally micro-assessed and spot checks are regularly conducted to ensure compliance with UNICEF regulations.

Fostering Resilience through Early Recovery response for the most Crisis impacted Communities in Syria The Integrated Response for Resilience Programme aims at providing a comprehensive response through Early Recovery support in 80 communities impacted by the crisis. Communities, particularly  those most dramatically affected – and under additional stress because of IDPs returns and other displacements - need  assistance in reinforcing their resilience to address these shocks as well as the consequences of the protracted crisis, and to address their needs on seriously depleted infrastructures and service capacities.
The essence of the Programme is about providing Syrian communities with – still limited - support to regain  control  over their basic needs (livelihoods, access to essential services) and reduce their dependency on humanitarian assistance. Prioritization of locations, is the outcome of a context analysis and needs assessment conducted on more than  5,000
Syrian communities, based on the following three criteria:
1) Hard to Reach  Areas
2) Areas of major IDPs presence and IDPs returns
3) Highest scoring in the Severity Scale
The integrated response consists of the following components: strengthening of social services-related capacities (access and coverage), livelihoods creation and rural recovery, PWDs support, social cohesion/community safety, reducing gender inequality  and youth marginality, women empowerment, tensions reduction and rehabilitation of basic infrastructure and public services.
The program is built in a modular manner both in terms of geographical and sectoral/thematic interventions and foresees the allotment of average 1 Million US$ per community. Hence, donors willing to support this approach will be able to pre-select certain location(s) and/or area(s) of intervention of their preference, within the 200 prioritized  communities.
The programme relates directly to the sector objectives:
1. Living conditions
2. Livelihoods
3. Access to social services
4. Access to productive and market infrastructure
5.social protection
6. Strengthening of local public services delivery capacity
7. Reinforcing  opportunities and capacities for civic engagement

Community -based protection, P&M of SGBV, Child Protection and economic empowerment for women and youth in Derbat, Jawa and Suni, South Darfur (Consortium) Provision of Lifesaving Protection services for IDPs, returnees and host community in East, South Darfur and Khartoum states. The purpose of the project is improving the lifesaving assistance and equitable access to essential protection services for IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities in South Darfur and East Darfur. Vulnerable women, girls, people with disabilities, UASC and elderly will be prioritized among the PSNs identified. ALIGHT strategy intends to increase and strengthen the community-based structures (CBPNs, Women and Youth Safe Spaces) in ED and SD to have a leading role in the protection monitoring, prevention and response. 4 Women Centers (2 in SD and 2 in ED) and 1 Child Safe Space in SD As Salam will be constructed and child protection activities will focus in this locality. Awareness and capacity building on protection issues will reinforce the intervention of staff, community-based structures, local justice system and health workers. PSNs and in particular survivors of GBV and child abuse, children with disabilities and unaccompanied minors will be sustained with case management, PSS, legal aid, recreational activities and cash support based on their needs. Children will be targeted with a campaign for civil documentation and birth registration to ensure they can claim their rights and access the different services. Vulnerable women will receive dignity kits and will be supported to develop income generating activities to increase their living conditions. Community-protection projects will be developed to mitigate protection risks for example connected to access resources. Indeed, the complexity of protection’s causes and consequences requires collaboration and coordination among sectors. Therefore, ALIGHT will be present with protection, wash, shelter/NFI, health and nutrition interventions in the target localities. The synergic vision consents ALIGHT to look beyond the emergency approach to build pathways of behavioral and value change with IDPs, returnees and host communities to enable a protective environment. Due to the conflict started the 15th of April, the protection needs increased and therefore Nyala, Khartoum and Gezira State are considered as hotposts localities for specific life-saving interventions, in addition to the previous localities in ED and SD. Alight will set up mobile GBV and PSS teams to provide mobile protection services to outpost locations where static services do not exist. The mobile team will consist of case workers and community mobilizers for GBV sector and health, and nutrition staff for health and nutrition sector deployed on a weekly or bi-weekly basis as the situation may demand. Once mobile coordination mechanisms are established and security clearance obtained, mobile teams travel to target communities on a set interval. The number and composition of mobile team members and necessities needed will depend on displacement density, context and population per site, the distance between sites with static services and assessed needs for direct program support. In case staff deployment is not possible, Alight will provide remote support for case management and PSS, in collaboration with local partners. At the same time, Alight will build the capacity of existing service providers in the community, which will be able to identify and appropriate support survivors (the capacity building will include PSEAH). Capacity building and awareness raising will ultimately increase direct access to services for the affected population, whether they are offered by Alight, other partners, government, or local authorities. Alight will also distribute dignity kits and provide FTR services or alternative accommodation for UASC in collaboration with the Clusters and partners.

---- USA / BPRM Community Engagement and Women’s Empowerment & Sexual and Gender Based Violence in the East, Adamawa and North regions  The project titled ‘‘Community Engagement and Women’s Empowerment & Sexual and Gender Based Violence in the East, Adamawa and North regions” aims to empower communities and achieve gender equality by ensuring that People of concern to UNHCR receive proper assistance, including livelihood opportunities, cash-based interventions and inclusion initiatives that will ensure a dignified life and the respect of beneficiary rights. Activities planned to be implemented in 2023 seek to improve the protection and living conditions of 60,450 direct beneficiaries (42,315 refugees and 18,135 Cameroonians) and 181,350 indirect beneficiaries during lifetime of project. The project targets East, Adamawa and northern regions focusing on the most vulnerable groups, with 52.33% representing female (women & girls) and 53.63% of children (girls & boys) respectively. Based on IMC-UK October 2022 statistics, these regions host 327,976 Central African Refugees (CAR) in both developed sites (74,503 refugees) and off-sites (253,473 refugees).2 In addition, among these Central African refugees, 57,726 are people with specific needs, including 12,103 women at risk and 6,474 persons living with physical disability.  
As part of this project, it is necessary to strengthen community anchoring, thus facilitating the exit and sustainability strategy, which are based on the full participation of all stakeholders. Sustainability therefore aims at a transfer of competence to the government and its decentralized structures, including the communities. In other words, it is about preparing them to take charge of the protection of refugees and vulnerable populations. To do this, the proposed project will be implemented through four main strategic axes: 
Capacity building of community-based organizations for self-ownership of all activities carried out for their benefit, in particular protection activities. In doing so, it will be able to identify its problems and provide solutions based on resources that can be mobilized locally. This involves revitalizing all the protection committees (School for Husbands, Women's Committees, Youth Committees, Gender Club, Girl Shine, etc.) within refugee sites, building the capacity of Local Protection Committees (LPC) by providing them with working materials, the strengthening of community mechanisms for the identification, reporting and care at community level of people with specific needs, in particular survivors of GBV, abandoned children or children living alone, the elderly, people living with disabilities, the chronically ill and large families (under the lead of the CLPs). 
Capacity building of decentralized State structures (MINAS, MINPROFF, MINSANTE, MINJUSTICE, MINJEC, FMO, etc.) so that they are better equipped to take care of vulnerable people. The sectors seem to consider community-based protection activities as the competence of humanitarian actors. When they are called upon to be involved, they sometimes make their participation conditional on financial motivation. At both the operational and strategic levels, there is a lack of knowledge of subjects such as GBV by all sectors. This does not facilitate better appropriation of interventions and weakens coordination. 
Safe spaces for women and girls will be converted into centers of wealth production. To do so, the beneficiaries of the services (skills building and informational activities) offered by these centers will be trained and organized in such a way as to ensure proper management of the center and of the products resulting from their work. These structures will be technically supported by the MINPROFF with financial support from the Councill of the locality. 
A multi-sectoral approach that is psychosocial, medical, security and legal assistance will be necessary to ensure the success of our main objective. IMC-UK will focus on the services most crucial to ensure maximum impact on the target populations (refugee and vulnerable host community).

Vulnerable children under-five and PLWs are the main target of the project. Through SC -Nutrition interventions, a total of 362,874 beneficiaries will benefit from the services provided, among them (87,131 boys, 90,680 girls, 184,383 women, 680 men). Save the children will implement lifesaving, preventative interventions, treatment of severe and moderate acute malnutrition among children under five years and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLWs), referral of SAM children with medical complications and minor rehabilitation to nutrition sites. To reach the estimated targets and planned response scale up, the nutrition sector will deploy integrated response modalities with health sector, WASH, FSL, protection, education at facility and community levels. SC will deliver nutrition services through existing health facilities, mobile and outreach teams and at community such as mother-to mother support groups activities including IDPs and hard to reach areas, use of cash-based interventions to increase access and utilization of nutrition services through FSL will be used for most cases in need. The proposed nutrition project aim is to improve equitable access to quality life-saving curative and preventive services through the systematic provision of nutrition services in South Kordofan, North Kordofan, Central Darfur, North Darfur, West Darfur, Sennar, Blue Nile and Red Sea states in which 29 localities will be covered. Vulnerable children under-five and PLWs are the main target of the project. Through SC -Nutrition interventions, a total of 362,874 beneficiaries will benefit from the services provided, among them (87,131 boys, 90,680 girls, 184,383 women, 680 men). Save the children will implement lifesaving, preventative interventions, treatment of severe and moderate acute malnutrition among children under five years and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLWs), referral of SAM children with medical complications and minor rehabilitation to nutrition sites. To reach the estimated targets and planned response scale up, the nutrition sector will deploy integrated response modalities with health sector, WASH, FSL, protection, education at facility and community levels. SC will deliver nutrition services through existing health facilities, mobile and outreach teams and at community such as mother-to mother support groups activities including IDPs and hard to reach areas, use of cash-based interventions to increase access and utilization of nutrition services through FSL will be used for most cases in need. In term of emergency response, rapid response mechanisms for timely delivery of nutrition interventions in the onset emergencies will applied.
