Humanitarian initial allocation 2023 Supported integrated basic life-saving services to vulnerable populations in Darfur, Sudan The Darfur states remain one of the areas worst-affected  by the ongoing conflict which erupted in April 2023 between the Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which is heavily impacting civilians and has triggered in Sudan the world's largest displacement crisis. The project's overall objective is to provide emergency health, nutrition, and pss services to crisis-affected populations in Central and West Darfur, IDPs, and host communities, by ensuring i) basic lifesaving integrated health services are supported and provided to IDPs and host communities; ii) significant access to essential integrated prevention and management of acute malnutrition for the targeted population at HF and community level and iii) communities are involved in the improvement of their health, nutrition and psychosocial status, selecting and training community volunteers, providing health, nutrition and pss awareness to targeted communities and providing protection training and service mapping.
PUI will continue to support the already supported Mother and Child Centre (MCC) in Geneina as the main primary care service for mothers, conducting maternity care, such as ante-natal care (ANC), post-natal care (PNC) and Family Planning. Given the context evolutions in the whole Darfur states, with increasing health, nutrition and MHPSS needs while access is improved, PUI will also start supporting one additional HF in Zalingei, Central Darfur. Zalingei’s PHC will provide free primary healthcare, including Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) services, to its catchment population area, while Geneina MCC will more specifically target women of reproductive age, PLWs and children under 5, providing SRH minimum essential package and integrated management of childhood illness (IMCI).
PUI will ensure the provision of  essential pharmaceutical commodities following standard quality process for purchase, storage, distribution and management, and non-medical equipment and supplies to health facilities, their financial support and necessary rehabilitation. PUI will continue to coordinate with UNFPA and WHO for the provision of SRH and IEH kits. PUI will provide support on outbreak preparedness and routine immunization program, ensure the training and capacity building of health staff, support access to quality healthcare services, including (SRH), and referral systems, provide PSS services. As per MISP recommendation, Clean Delivery Kits will be distributed to PLWs in communities where access to HF and skilled birth attendants is not ensured to reduce risk of maternal and neonatal mortality. As per SOPs and safe and dignified programming principles, menstrual hygiene kits will be provided to displaced teenagers (14 – 25) and women under 25 coming to the HFs seeking care. 
2 OTPs will be set inside the supported HFs to provide treatment to children under 5 suffering from SAM without complications, and will be accessible by both IDPs and host communities. PUI will liaise with UNICEF and WFP for nutrition commodities provision. SAM with complications cases will be referred to Geneina’s Stabilization Centre (SC), set in Geneina Hospital and supported by MSF, and to Zalingei SC, set in Zalingei’s hospital, which World relief is planning to support. PUI will support SAM with complications referral to higher level of care with cash for transportation, as well as health and SRH referrals. Two Mother Support Groups of 10 mothers each will be established. Under the supervision of PUI health and nutrition officer, they will be provided with sensitization on Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) best practices, including exclusive breastfeeding, and cooking demonstrations on how to prepare nutritious food from locally available ingredients.
PUI will provide Psychosocial Support Services, at HF and community levels.

Explosive hazard contamination not only poses severe socioeconomic implications for families and communities by depriving them of livelihoods and sources of income but also increases vulnerabilities. Insecurity and economic hardship persist, exacerbating child protection concerns and leading to harmful coping mechanisms such as the worst forms of labor and child marriage. Additionally, high levels of psychosocial distress prevail among children and caregivers due to multiple stresses, including the continued escalation of conflict, poverty, earthquakes, and restrictions on movement that limit access to social services.

In line with the CP AOR Strategy, UNICEF will enhance equitable access to quality CP services with a resilience focus, for prevention and response to CP risks, including for survivors of abuse, violence, neglect and exploitation, CWD, unaccompanied and separated children, targeting high severity sub-districts.

UNICEF will focus the intervention under this proposal on the following activities:
• The provision of structured MHPSS activities for 234,500 girls and boys through child-friendly spaces, mobile teams, and community structures.
• Engagement of 50,000 parents and caregivers in structured and sustained parenting programmes to facilitate the creation of a safe and enabling environment in families and communities free from violence against children.
• Implement EORE sessions for 653,600 children and parents/caregivers in communities including through using mobile teams.
• Provide integrated specialized child protection services, through case management, to 16,920 children, including family tracing and reunification for separated and unaccompanied children, children in contact with the law, violence against children, child marriage, child labour, and children with disabilities.
• Build technical capacity of 3,000 implementing partners' social workers on child protection/GBV services delivery and ensure regular monitoring of activities. In coordination with the GBV AoR UNICEF will build capacities on GBV risk mitigation.
• Elimination of VAC, including GBV prevention and empowerment for 120,550 girls, boys, and women, and prevention of violence in schools, homes, and communities through awareness-raising sessions.
• Awareness-raising on CP risks and SBC interventions on child protection issues for 200,000 girls, boys, women and men.

UNICEF will generate evidence to inform the humanitarian response and advocacy, including setting up an information management system for case management. UNICEF will also continue to support the Monitoring and Reporting Mechanism on grave violations against children.

Violence prevention is a key priority. UNICEF will work to protect children from violence and abuse through prevention activities in schools, homes, and communities and by providing survivors of violence with child-friendly and gender-sensitive services. Support will be provided for PSEA mechanisms to protect beneficiaries and build the capacity of humanitarian actors.

PSEA by humanitarian workers and service providers is high on the UNICEF agenda to ensure that no violations and abuse happen during implementation. UNICEF, as co-lead for the ICN on PSEA, will continue to support and work closely with other agencies to enhance the PSEA portfolio by building continuous capacity for humanitarian workers with zero tolerance for SEA. As a pre-condition for contracting implementing partners, PSEA assurance and capacity-building plans are guaranteed.

---- Education Education support for Syria’s children and youth affected by crisis As per HNO 2024, the sector PIN indicates a 4% increase from the previous year for children and teachers in need of education assistance. Access to education remains a challenge for many children, as the numbers of Out of School Children remain high. The main barriers are related to the deteriorating economic situation and the ongoing protracted crisis. Even for children in school, learning spaces continue to be unconducive with overcrowded classrooms, limited number of teachers and limited availability of teaching and learning materials.
UNICEF proposes to provide 3,182,074 children and teachers with education services in areas of severity 3-5. This includes children from preprimary, primary and secondary school-aged girls and boys to enable them to develop foundational numeracy and literacy skills, as well as life and citizenship skills, in order to strengthen child, family and community resilience. Additionally, support to enhance the physical learning spaces as well as provision of psychosocial support for children and teachers. 
UNICEF will contribute to: 
A. Providing equitable access to education 
B. Supporting quality education in protective environment
C. Strengthening education systems 
Access will be promoted through Back-to-Learning Campaigns, Vouchers-for-Education, provision of non-formal education programs, school textbooks and school supplies, support to national exams to enhance access to accredited education as part of a multi-sector approach, rehabilitation of schools (formal and nonformal) and provision of temporary classrooms. Rehabilitation is also needed in lower severity areas, where displaced children and returnees as well as large numbers of host community children reside, to contribute to resilience and social cohesion. 
For school rehabilitation UNICEF coordinates with relevant authorities to identify schools in need. UNICEF conducts an assessment to confirm needs and works through vetted independent contractors to commence rehabilitation, including the improvement of WASH facilities, enhancing accessibility for children with disabilities. This is complemented by the provision of school furniture and supplies.
UNICEF will support the Self-learning program to ensure that OOSC have an opportunity to learn, this includes provision of materials, establishment of learning spaces, provision of supplies and support to teacher training. To improve the quality of education services, UNICEF will ensure schools are child-friendly, with teachers trained in child-centered pedagogy, and where children develop academic, cognitive, life and psychosocial skills that empower them to engage, relate, cope and contribute to community and family life. Due to the large number of children at different learning levels within grades, children will be provided with remedial learning support. To support system resilience, UNICEF will establish Parent Teacher Associations that cooperate with Headmasters, and train education staff on monitoring schools, staff performance and children’s learning. UNICEF monitors ongoing activities through staff and implementing partner visits, Third Partner Monitoring and through established feedback mechanisms. In NWS, TPMs provide on-site verification and beneficiary interviews. 
PROTECTION RISK ANALYSIS
1. Attack on education and safety of children on their way to school 2.Increased risks of GBV if latrines are not separated or there are no locks on the doors and light. 3.Increased risk of host-community tension due to assistance packages given to IDPs, 4. Risk of sexual exploitation by Teacher education personnel, NGO staff (risk of harassment) of boys and girls 5. Teachers or other education personnel participate in physical punishment or bullying of students Or Students participate in bullying of students
PSEA policy will be respected as per UNICEF rules and mandate.
RISKS, ASSUMPTIONS AND MITIGATION MEASURES Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation Children working with contractors Zero tolerance

Accès à une Education de qualité, sûre et inclusive des enfants affectés par la crise sécuritaire dans la région de Tillabéri au Niger (AccED) Projet d’Accès à une Education de qualité, sûre et inclusive des enfants affectés par la crise sécuritaire dans la région de Tillabéry au Niger (AccED) AccED contribuera à la réinsertion et la continuité de l'accès à une éducation inclusive, sûre et de qualité des filles, garçons et adolescent/es les plus vulnérables affectés par la crise humanitaire dans la région de Tillabéri en réduisant les obstacles à l'éducation. Dans les zones où l'accès à l'éducation est possible, l'action i) augmentera l'offre d'éducation dans les zones de forte présence de PDI et réfugiés à travers le renforcement de la capacité d'accueil et qualité de l'apprentissage et ii) promouvra des programmes d'éducation accélérés pour faciliter le rattrapage et passerelles avec le système formel d'éducation. Dans les zones de conflit où les écoles sont fermées, l'action prévoit des approches innovantes et/ou alternatives d'éducation à travers le transfert d'élèves du secondaire vers les écoles des zones sécurisées, éducation par la radio, Espaces d'apprentissage Communautaires Ouverts. En matière de protection de l’enfant le projet implémentera des activités relatives aux audiences foraines pour la délivrance des actes d’état civil au profit de 600 enfants affectés par la crise sécuritaires, formation des enseignants sur les premiers secours psychologiques, prise en charge au niveau éducatif de 420 élèves en situation de Handicap, séparés et non accompagnés et/ou victimes de VBG. Toutes ces activités viennent compléter les activités d’éducation pour un meilleurs rendement scolaire et donc le bien-être des enfants touchés par la crise.

Niger 2024	EHA (Water Sanitation Hygiene) Réponse multisectorielle d'urgence aux populations affectées par l'insécurité alimentaire et les conflits dans les régions de Tillabéri, Diffa et Tahoua, et soutien aux services d'information humanitaire au Niger  Ce projet fournira une réponse d'urgence multisectorielle pour les individus les plus vulnérables affectés par la crise de sécurité alimentaire et la crise de protection/conflit. L'intervention se concentrera sur les zones difficiles d'accès dans les régions de Tillabéry, Diffa et Tahoua. 
i) Une aide alimentaire d'urgence flexible, répondant aux besoins immédiats des communautés touchées par les déplacements et l'insécurité alimentaire, dans les zones difficiles d'accès. Le projet adaptera l'assistance au contexte et aux besoins, en combinant des actions soudaines et des actions en période de soudure. Une approche à 2 piliers sera mise en œuvre : i) en fournissant une aide alimentaire d'urgence pendant la période de soudure via du cash ; et ii) en fournissant une aide alimentaire d'urgence pendant 3 mois aux personnes qui sont tombées plus tôt dans l'insécurité alimentaire en raison d'une très faible production alimentaire avant la période de soudure, en particulier lorsqu'elles sont victimes d'un choc. 
ii) Complété par des activités multisectorielles, renforçant la capacité de production alimentaire, les moyens de subsistance et la cohésion sociale, grâce à une intervention dans deux secteurs. Pour soutenir les capacités agricoles et les mécanismes d'adaptation, dans les zones où l'assistance alimentaire sera fournie, le projet soutiendra la production agricole et alimentaire au niveau des ménages, en intégrant les ménages les plus vulnérables dans des systèmes de résilience communautaires. En tenant compte du calendrier agricole, pendant la période de soudure, les bénéficiaires recevront des intrants agricoles pour les cultures pluviales et les cultures maraîchères. En outre, la diversification des ressources économiques au-delà de l'agriculture est essentielle pour assurer un accès inclusif, en particulier pour les personnes déplacées et les femmes (non-agriculteurs), aux activités économiques et couvrir la sécurité alimentaire et les besoins nutritionnels. D'autres personnes vulnérables bénéficieront d'un soutien aux AGR et à l'élevage par le biais i) d'un soutien aux éleveurs, ii) de la vaccination du bétail et des moyens de subsistance, et iii) des AGR.  
iii) Et en tenant compte de la nécessité de mesures de protection au niveau communautaire, notamment en raison de la crise accrue en matière de protection et de déplacement, afin d'améliorer la qualité, la responsabilité et l'efficacité de la réponse tout en garantissant l'accès à la protection de base et aux services WASH pour les personnes les plus vulnérables touchées par le déplacement. Grâce à des activités de type CCCM en dehors des camps, la troisième ligne d'intervention vise à prendre en compte le lien intersectoriel entre le déplacement et la sécurité alimentaire et à fournir un cadre de protection amélioré pour la population touchée par le déplacement, y compris les communautés d'accueil. Selon le CH, les départements ciblés affectés par les déplacements et les conflits sont en phase IPC3+ ; et l'impact de la crise de la sécurité alimentaire sur la protection des plus vulnérables ne fera que s'aggraver. La qualité et l'impact de la réponse doivent s'améliorer avec i) le renforcement de la coordination des déplacements au niveau de la crise, ii) une meilleure participation des communautés affectées, iii) des mesures de protection communautaires améliorées, iv) et une meilleure responsabilisation de la réponse humanitaire. --- WASH Gender sensitive and life-saving integrated WASH response for multi-shock affected vulnerable communities in Syria Leading the fight against malnutrition, ACF implements gender-sensitive and life-saving WASH interventions and provides communities with access to safe water and sanitation as sustainable mitigation for the causes of hunger. After 13 years of hostilities and persistent economic crisis, people in Syria saw their living conditions worsen when a series of earthquakes hit northern Syria and Türkiye. The erosion of basic service capacity has continued steadily, with water and sanitation systems, and public health services under immense strain, in a context of little development investment.
ACF operates through four offices in Damascus, Aleppo, Hama, and Al-Hassakeh. ACF has MoUs with the Ministries of Water Resources, Local Administration and Environment, Education, and Health. ACF actively engages with the WASH, Health and Nutrition, Food Security and Agriculture, and Early Recovery and Livelihoods, and Protection Sectors, as well as other sub-sectors and technical working groups such as Cash and AAP. ACF maintains close coordination with SARC, as well as with Governors’ offices and local administrations, and Line Ministries with which it has MoUs in place, including MoH, MoE, MoWR, MAAR, and MoSAL. In NES, ACF coordinates with UNICEF and the NES WWG for its interventions in Al-Hassakeh. 
ACF conducts integrated assessments to understand the needs and interlinkages of WASH, FSL, and Health and Nutrition. After conducting assessments in Aleppo, Hama, Latakia, and Al-Hassakeh, it was identified that community members have access to less than 30 l/p/d of water. Al-Hassakeh city relies on humanitarian agencies for water trucking, with no sustainable and complete exit strategy in sight (not least due to the condition of water resources in the governorate, and the lacking political solutions to ensure the permanent functioning of Allouk pumping station), and all targeted governorates need rehabilitation of the water systems, and the water pipelines as well as the sewage systems.
Under Sector Objectives 1 and 4, emergency WASH services provided by ACF include life-saving water trucking, distribution of water tanks, water quality testing and light maintenance of boreholes. ACF also undertakes the rehabilitation of damaged and malfunctioning water systems, which includes repairing boreholes, upgrading to solar energy, connecting water stations to the electric grid, repairing elevated tower tanks, repairing water networks at the community level, and providing equipment for water testing facilities. By providing water through public networks, ACF ensures greater control over quality and quantity, making it an affordable service. ACF also repairs sanitation systems at different levels, including pipelines, manholes and septic tanks, and provides support for solid waste management. This includes providing garbage bins for safe disposal in coordination with municipalities, as well as technical capacity building for technicians, PPE, tools and spare parts provision for sustained service provision after handing over to the local authorities. To improve public health, ACF engages in risk communication and community engagement activities that are tailored according to age and gender. 

Gender sensitive approaches and safeguarding of beneficiaries are integral to ACF programming, with dedicated staff upholding gender minimum standards and mainstreaming safeguarding processes. ACF recognizes the right of everyone to be treated with dignity and respect and protected from sexual exploitation and abuse. ACF’s policy on PSEA complies with the IASC six principles relating to sexual exploitation and abuse. ACF provides compulsory training to each new staff member and refresher sessions to existing staff on organizational ethical policies. Internal policies relating to fraud, anti-corruption and abuse of power and whistleblowing/reporting mechanisms are followed with employees receiving instruction on these internal policies.

---- USA / BPRM Community Engagement and Women’s Empowerment & Sexual and Gender Based Violence in the East, Adamawa and North regions  The project titled ‘‘Community Engagement and Women’s Empowerment & Sexual and Gender Based Violence in the East, Adamawa and North regions” aims to empower communities and achieve gender equality by ensuring that People of concern to UNHCR receive proper assistance, including livelihood opportunities, cash-based interventions and inclusion initiatives that will ensure a dignified life and the respect of beneficiary rights. Activities planned to be implemented in 2023 seek to improve the protection and living conditions of 60,450 direct beneficiaries (42,315 refugees and 18,135 Cameroonians) and 181,350 indirect beneficiaries during lifetime of project. The project targets East, Adamawa and northern regions focusing on the most vulnerable groups, with 52.33% representing female (women & girls) and 53.63% of children (girls & boys) respectively. Based on IMC-UK October 2022 statistics, these regions host 327,976 Central African Refugees (CAR) in both developed sites (74,503 refugees) and off-sites (253,473 refugees).2 In addition, among these Central African refugees, 57,726 are people with specific needs, including 12,103 women at risk and 6,474 persons living with physical disability.  
As part of this project, it is necessary to strengthen community anchoring, thus facilitating the exit and sustainability strategy, which are based on the full participation of all stakeholders. Sustainability therefore aims at a transfer of competence to the government and its decentralized structures, including the communities. In other words, it is about preparing them to take charge of the protection of refugees and vulnerable populations. To do this, the proposed project will be implemented through four main strategic axes: 
Capacity building of community-based organizations for self-ownership of all activities carried out for their benefit, in particular protection activities. In doing so, it will be able to identify its problems and provide solutions based on resources that can be mobilized locally. This involves revitalizing all the protection committees (School for Husbands, Women's Committees, Youth Committees, Gender Club, Girl Shine, etc.) within refugee sites, building the capacity of Local Protection Committees (LPC) by providing them with working materials, the strengthening of community mechanisms for the identification, reporting and care at community level of people with specific needs, in particular survivors of GBV, abandoned children or children living alone, the elderly, people living with disabilities, the chronically ill and large families (under the lead of the CLPs). 
Capacity building of decentralized State structures (MINAS, MINPROFF, MINSANTE, MINJUSTICE, MINJEC, FMO, etc.) so that they are better equipped to take care of vulnerable people. The sectors seem to consider community-based protection activities as the competence of humanitarian actors. When they are called upon to be involved, they sometimes make their participation conditional on financial motivation. At both the operational and strategic levels, there is a lack of knowledge of subjects such as GBV by all sectors. This does not facilitate better appropriation of interventions and weakens coordination. 
Safe spaces for women and girls will be converted into centers of wealth production. To do so, the beneficiaries of the services (skills building and informational activities) offered by these centers will be trained and organized in such a way as to ensure proper management of the center and of the products resulting from their work. These structures will be technically supported by the MINPROFF with financial support from the Councill of the locality. 
A multi-sectoral approach that is psychosocial, medical, security and legal assistance will be necessary to ensure the success of our main objective. IMC-UK will focus on the services most crucial to ensure maximum impact on the target populations (refugee and vulnerable host community).

Improving access to and utilization of integrated, life-saving health, nutrition, disaster preparedness, protection, basic needs and livelihoods services for the most vulnerable IDPs, refugees and host communities in South Kordofan, West and Central Darfur, Blue Nile and Khartoum Comprehensive humanitarian nutrition services for IDPs, returnees and vulnerable residents Sudan is among the top four countries globally with the highest prevalence of global acute malnutrition (GAM) estimated at 13.6 percent. Following the conflict in May 2023, the acute malnutrition People in Need (PIN) increased by over 13% from 4.0 M in January to over 4.5M in May.  The nutrition situation is projected to continue worsening in 2024 aggravated by the conflict, deterioration in food security, health and WASH services and the continuing displacement. As a result, the 2024 PIN is estimated to increase by between 10% and 30% in non-IDP and frontline localities respectively; with an overall additional 4.1% increase from 2023 PIN levels reaching over 4.7M in 2024, the highest PIN ever estimated in Sudan. 

 About, 76% acutely malnourished under-five children, pregnant and Lactating women in host and IDP settings live in 103 localities (54% of the total localities in Sudan). These localities are most affected, classified with severity scale 3-5 for WASH, Health, and Food Security; above national average acute malnutrition PIN and very high GAM prevalence of 15% and above- the WHO emergency threshold.  Micronutrient malnutrition among children is also very high with 48% of under-five children suffering from anaemia most of which is due to iron deficiency.  Minimum dietary diversity among under-five is one of the lowest trailing at 25% which is projected have deteriorated further following the ongoing massive displacement that has disrupted feeding and caring practices.  
The proposed nutrition project aim is to improve equitable access to quality lifesaving curative and preventive services through the systematic provision of nutrition services  that includes; Preventive nutrition interventions focusing on  Maternal and Young child Nutrition (MYCN) & Infant and young child feeding practices, detection, referral and treatment of severe acute malnutrition  with and without medical complications as well as supplementation of moderate acute malnutrition among under-fives, Pregnant and lactating women and girls , Management of Small and Nutritionally at risk infants under-six months and their mothers (MAMI) and Nutrition Impact and Positive Practice (NIPP).The action will implemented in South Kordofan, Central Darfur, North Darfur, Sennar, Blue Nile, River Nile and Al Gezira states in which 25 localities with severity scale 3-5 will be covered. Vulnerable children under-five and PLWs are the main target of the project. Through SC -Nutrition interventions, a total of 323,298beneficiaries will benefit from the services provided, among them (71,287boys, 87,129girls, 163,233 women, 1,649 men. To reach the estimated targets and planned response scale up, the nutrition sector will deploy integrated response modalities with health sector, WASH, FSL, protection, education at facility and community levels. SC will deliver nutrition services through existing health facilities and outreach teams and at community such as mother-to mother support groups activities including IDPs and hard to reach areas, use of cash based interventions in one prioritized location in SK  to increase access and utilization of nutrition services through FSL will be used for most cases in need. In term of emergency response, rapid response mechanisms for timely delivery of nutrition interventions in the onset emergencies will applied. Specific nutrition response strategies will include scaling up the minimum preventive and protection lifesaving intervention package for prevention of malnutrition, treatment, and geographical coverage of severe and moderate acute malnutrition among the under-fives, strengthening referrals for children suffering from SAM with medical complication through provision of transportation costs to and from the SC, nutrition system capacity strengthening (capacity and infrastructure) will be done to facilitate provision of quality and people centered life-saving nutrition responses, timely delivery of core nutrition supplies.

Flexible humanitarian funding from Save the Children International's Humanitarian Fund Protection - Child Protection Protection des enfants vulnérables affectés par les conflits dans les régions de Diffa et Tillabéry Ce projet vise à améliorer l'environnement protecteur des filles et garçons affectés par les conflits par les biais des mésures préventives, de l'accès inclusif aux services de prise en charge adapaté à leur besoins, ainsi que par le renforcement du système formel et informel de la protection de l'enfant dans les régions de Diffa et Tilabéry. A travers cette intervention, SCI va continuer à se concentrer à promouvoir le cadre politique de la centralité de la protection pour atteindre les enfants les plus touchés et leurs communautés afin que les risques de protection auxquels ils sont confrontés soient identifiés, signalés et prise en charge. Nous nous concentrerons également, sur les dommages causés par les violations des droits et leur impact sur les filles différemment des garçons en tenant compte de leur capacité pour une réponse individualisée de la gestion de cas intégrant le soutien psychosocial et la réintégration socioéconomique. Pour renforcer le système de protection, une cartographie des services et un circuit  de référencement harmonisé seront regulièment actualisés pour promouvoir l’accès aux services essentiels assurant un environnement protecteur. En outre, Les acteurs communautaires seront mobilisés et formés aux outils et approches d'information et de sensibilisation adaptés aux enfants, afin d'assurer un changement de comportement positif et l'adoption de mesures préventives contre les risques et les violations des droits dans les contextes humanitaires.  Les interventions seront orientées vers les enfants les plus vulnérables parmi les populations déplacées internes et les communautés hôtes avec un focus sur ceux difficilement accessible ou en mobilité fréquente en raison de la crise à travers l’approche mobile. Les enfants affectés directement par la crise humanitaire, notamment, les enfants non accompagnés /séparés, associés aux forces et groupes armés et les enfants à risque d’autres violations ou de violences physiques et sexuelles, bénéficieront d’un appui psychosociale individuel et de groupe dans les espaces amis d’enfants, qui soutiennent la protection, le bien-être et l'apprentissage des enfants dans les crises par le renforcement du système, de la qualité et des méthodologies des activités de SMSPS, garantissant l'amélioration du bien-être des enfants et de leur résilience. Le système de protection sera renforcé à travers les approches intégrée  du modèle socio-écologique et des approches communes de SCI. Notamment, le renforcement des capacités sur la manière dont l'assistance sous forme de transfert monétaire et de bons sera utilisée pour atténuer les risques pour les enfants et soutenir une réponse à leurs besoins.  Les familles les plus vulnérables et les familles d’accueil seront soutenus par le Cash à l'aide d'un plan d’action individuel « PAI » participatif afin de réduire les vulnérabilités et renforcer la capacité des familles. Pour les enfants touchés par les conflits armés, l'aide comprendra des services destinés aux enfants qui ont besoin d'une aide à la réunification familial, à la réintégration communautaire comme les EAFGA, une aide aux enfants survivants des VBG liées aux conflits, aux victimes d'engins explosifs, ainsi qu'une aide connexe. Afin de renforcer la gestion des cas individualisée pour tous les enfants ayant besoin des multiples services et ayant des risques élevés. Nous allons faire recours à l' approche commune ""Steps to Protect"" de SCI, pour assurer une réponse multisectorielle. Il sera aussi question de déployer le CPIMS+ pour renforcer  la mise en œuvre d'un système de gestion de l'information inter-agences. De monitoring de la situation de protection seront organisées. La collaboration avec les autre secteurs (éducation, santé…VBG) sera envisagée pour mettre en place une intervention multisectorielle et multi acteurs. ceci répondra aux sévérités liées aux incidents de protections aux quels un grand nombre des enfants IDP sont exposés

Promotion of the rights and protection of persons affected by displacement and displacement and human mobility
Increasing safety, mitigating risk, and meeting humanitarian needs for the vulnerable populations affected by other
situations of violence, forced displacement, and food insecurity in the North of Central America Promoción de los derechos y protección de las personas afectadas por desplazamiento y la movilidad humana  NRC fortalecerá los mecanismos de protección de las personas afectadas por desplazamiento, entendidas para esta propuesta como personas en situación de desplazamiento, solicitantes de asilo y personas con necesidades de protección internacional, deportadas con necesidades de protección y personas en tránsito con necesidades de protección. NRC ofrecerá tres tipos de servicios:  
El primero, centrado en asistencia legal, la gestión de casos y atención humanitaria inmediata. El segundo es enfocado en la instalación de capacidades de las instituciones locales, especialmente en la respuesta al desplazamiento y la seguridad en la tenencia de la vivienda, tierra y propiedad (VTP). También se contempla el monitoreo de protección con la finalidad de expedir documentos situacionales que sean de utilidad a las instituciones, las organizaciones civiles y humanitarias. El tercero centrado en contribuir al enfoque comunitario de autoprotección y resiliencia.
En el proyecto se contemplan las siguientes actividades: 
Manejo de casos: La gestión de casos de protección es un servicio estructurado para una persona en situación de alto riesgo de violencia. Lo presta un gestor de casos formado que trabaja con la persona para evaluar su situación de protección, desarrollar y aplicar conjuntamente un plan de acción completo, suele durar entre 3 y 10 meses, desde la admisión hasta el cierre. La gestión de casos de protección tendrá como objetivo mitigar y responder al daño causado por la OSV a partir del análisis de riesgos de protección. NRC adoptará un enfoque centrado en el cliente en la implementación de la gestión de casos, basado la centralidad de la protección en principios clave de confidencialidad y consentimiento informado, acceso significativo sin discriminación, no hacer daño, participación y empoderamiento, responsabilidad y autodeterminación. 

Asistencia de Protección Individual, IPA: Es una ayuda puntual o limitada en el tiempo, con un seguimiento limitado. Es específica, intencionada y diseñada para lograr un resultado de protección para el participante. La asistencia es tanto una acción de respuesta como de reparación.  Está vinculada a la prevención, reducción o mitigación de la exposición a los riesgos de protección, limitando los efectos de las violaciones en las víctimas. No es una intervención a largo plazo que busque soluciones duraderas, ni está diseñada para ayudar a la vulnerabilidad generalizada y a las necesidades básicas. La IPA abordará un riesgo de protección específico a través de una asistencia puntual con un seguimiento estrictamente limitado y por un período no superior a un mes desde la admisión hasta el cierre. 
 
Servicios legales: NRC, a través de un equipo legal especializado local, brindará información y asistencia legal para acceder a mecanismos de protección internacional, reconocimiento de estatus legal y obtención de documentación, incluida la identidad legal. Para solicitantes de asilo y refugiados, se ofrecerá información sobre el proceso, derechos y deberes, con acompañamiento durante la determinación de la condición de refugiado y obtención de documentación. En casos pertinentes, se proporcionará orientación sobre naturalización. Para personas desplazadas internamente o deportadas con necesidades de protección, NRC ofrecerá información sobre el derecho a la identidad legal, con orientación para obtener documentación civil e identidad. La identificación de casos se realizará mediante remisiones y jornadas en zonas fronterizas, abordando temas de protección internacional y riesgos. NRC cuenta con capacidad para servicios nacionales mediante atención telefónica y jornadas. En cuanto a la presencia en frontera, NRC mantiene relaciones con la Dirección de Migración y Extranjería, promoviendo el fortalecimiento de capacidades desde 2023. Los servicios tendrán alcance nacional, priorizando jornadas en zonas como La Hachadura, El Poy, Las Chinamas, San Cristóbal y El Amatillo.

Appui multisectoriel en sécurité alimentaire et eau, hygiène, assainissement dans la région de Tillabéry, auprès des populations affectées par les déplacements. Réponse multisectorielle d'urgence aux populations affectées par l'insécurité alimentaire et les conflits dans les régions de Tillabéri, Diffa et Tahoua, et soutien aux services d'information humanitaire au Niger  Ce projet fournira une réponse d'urgence multisectorielle pour les individus les plus vulnérables affectés par la crise de sécurité alimentaire et la crise de protection/conflit. L'intervention se concentrera sur les zones difficiles d'accès dans les régions de Tillabéry, Diffa et Tahoua. 
i) Une aide alimentaire d'urgence flexible, répondant aux besoins immédiats des communautés touchées par les déplacements et l'insécurité alimentaire, dans les zones difficiles d'accès. Le projet adaptera l'assistance au contexte et aux besoins, en combinant des actions soudaines et des actions en période de soudure. Une approche à 2 piliers sera mise en œuvre : i) en fournissant une aide alimentaire d'urgence pendant la période de soudure via du cash ; et ii) en fournissant une aide alimentaire d'urgence pendant 3 mois aux personnes qui sont tombées plus tôt dans l'insécurité alimentaire en raison d'une très faible production alimentaire avant la période de soudure, en particulier lorsqu'elles sont victimes d'un choc. 
ii) Complété par des activités multisectorielles, renforçant la capacité de production alimentaire, les moyens de subsistance et la cohésion sociale, grâce à une intervention dans deux secteurs. Pour soutenir les capacités agricoles et les mécanismes d'adaptation, dans les zones où l'assistance alimentaire sera fournie, le projet soutiendra la production agricole et alimentaire au niveau des ménages, en intégrant les ménages les plus vulnérables dans des systèmes de résilience communautaires. En tenant compte du calendrier agricole, pendant la période de soudure, les bénéficiaires recevront des intrants agricoles pour les cultures pluviales et les cultures maraîchères. En outre, la diversification des ressources économiques au-delà de l'agriculture est essentielle pour assurer un accès inclusif, en particulier pour les personnes déplacées et les femmes (non-agriculteurs), aux activités économiques et couvrir la sécurité alimentaire et les besoins nutritionnels. D'autres personnes vulnérables bénéficieront d'un soutien aux AGR et à l'élevage par le biais i) d'un soutien aux éleveurs, ii) de la vaccination du bétail et des moyens de subsistance, et iii) des AGR.  
iii) Et en tenant compte de la nécessité de mesures de protection au niveau communautaire, notamment en raison de la crise accrue en matière de protection et de déplacement, afin d'améliorer la qualité, la responsabilité et l'efficacité de la réponse tout en garantissant l'accès à la protection de base et aux services WASH pour les personnes les plus vulnérables touchées par le déplacement. Grâce à des activités de type CCCM en dehors des camps, la troisième ligne d'intervention vise à prendre en compte le lien intersectoriel entre le déplacement et la sécurité alimentaire et à fournir un cadre de protection amélioré pour la population touchée par le déplacement, y compris les communautés d'accueil. Selon le CH, les départements ciblés affectés par les déplacements et les conflits sont en phase IPC3+ ; et l'impact de la crise de la sécurité alimentaire sur la protection des plus vulnérables ne fera que s'aggraver. La qualité et l'impact de la réponse doivent s'améliorer avec i) le renforcement de la coordination des déplacements au niveau de la crise, ii) une meilleure participation des communautés affectées, iii) des mesures de protection communautaires améliorées, iv) et une meilleure responsabilisation de la réponse humanitaire. La coordination et la diffusion de l'information seront renforcées et un mécanisme de protection mis en place pour améliorer la qualité de la réponse apportée aux PDIs. En outre, compte tenu de l'impact évident de la crise des déplacements sur l'accès aux services WASH et le lien avec la sécurité alimentaire et la nutrition, l'accès aux services WASH doit être assuré pour contribuer à renforcer l'environnement protecteur.  Ce niveau de réponse fournira un cadre et une base pour une réponse plus intégrée par zone, à tous les niveaux.

Siguiendo un enfoque holístico de inclusión, se implementarán intervenciones adaptadas a la edad, el género, la discapacidad inclusiva, así como adaptadas a la identidad cultural de los pueblos indígenas (Warao, Amorua, Pemón), teniendo en cuenta las medidas de prevención de enfermedades, en línea con el enfoque de triple nexo, construyendo un puente hacia soluciones a largo plazo y fortaleciendo la coexistencia pacífica de los migrantes en tránsito y las comunidades de acogida. El proyecto beneficiará directamente a un total de 110,166 personas vulnerables, al apoyar las necesidades más críticas en las áreas WASH (acceso a agua potable, potabilización y dotación de instalaciones de saneamiento, así como kits de higiene, kits de dignidad y capacitación para la prevención de enfermedades endémicas, con especial énfasis en el lavado de manos), seguridad alimentaria (kits de alimentos o platos servidos) y salud (actividades de fortalecimiento y dotación de insumos básicos a establecimientos de salud cercanos a las comunidades seleccionadas y el entrenamiento y sensibilización a trabajadores del área, así como atención con consultas médicas básicas y medicación a los beneficiarios). En consecuencia, la protección se constituye en un eje transversal (apoyo psicosocial, a cargo de una Oficial, la entrega de dispositivos de asistencia, acceso a TICs y concientización en materia de riesgos). El enfoque inclusivo de poblaciones en los más altos niveles o riesgo de vulnerabilidad (personas mayores, personas con discapacidades, mujeres víctimas o en riesgo de violencia basada en género, mujeres gestantes o lactantes, con hijos menores de 5 años, cabezas de familia, otros grupos minoritarios incluyendo población LGBTIQ+, pero especialmente la población indígena) implica requerimientos de atención y protección diferencial, basada en las necesidades identificadas en terreno y la adaptación del contenido de la intervención. Esto es particularmente visible en los temas alimentarios, en las inversiones en infraestructura para agua y saneamiento básico y en la aplicación del enfoque de género intercultural con comunidades indígenas. La asistencia en áreas remotas requiriendo transporte fluvial y largos trayectos en carretera, elevan los costos de atención ligeramente sobre los estándares. Por ello, se realiza la cobertura de un número menos amplio de beneficiarios de la atención integral. Por último, el objetivo es cubrir una gran brecha humanitaria existente en áreas específicas, en 2 de los 8 estados priorizados del país. Basado en datos sólidos recopilados directamente durante los últimos dos años y alineado con las necesidades del HRP, los objetivos del Clúster de Protección y el Grupo de Trabajo de Edad y Discapacidad, así como también la sinergia generada con el sub-clúster de protección CCT Guayana y el Foro ONGI. Hemos desarrollado intervenciones exitosas en el área de protección junto a Convite y Kapé-Kapé, ambas reconocidas como especialistas en poblaciones indígenas, garantizando el respeto a la interculturalidad y una comunicación efectiva en idiomas autóctonos. El componente de género, a cargo de una Oficial, contempla no solo la sensibilización individual, comunitaria y a trabajadores del sector salud sino también la asistencia material y la orientación psicosocial

This project aims to implement the organization's response under its vision of the triple nexus, in the Colombian pacific coast, especially in Valle del Cauca, Choco, Cauca and Nariño Departments, where consolidated peace is at the center of the changes needed to allow communities to move from insecurity and lack of access to rights to a scenario of protection and development Respuesta integrada de servicios especializados de Protección de NRC que reducen y mitigan el impacto del conflicto armado colombiano sobre personas desplazadas internas y comunidades afectadas por el mismo, permitiéndoles satisfacer necesidades urgentes, acceder a mecanismos de protección, disfrutar de sus derechos básicos y alcanzar soluciones duraderas. Los proyectos de Protección de NRC involucran el trabajo de dos equipos, por un lado, servicios especializados de protección y, por el otro lado, servicios de asistencia legal. 

Los proyectos de Protección contra violencia de NRC buscan reducir y mitigar el impacto de la violencia y el conflicto sobre individuos y comunidades expuestas al conflicto armado interno colombiano; inclusive riesgos de protección como amenazas, asesinatos, desplazamiento forzado, confinamiento, explotación, extorsión, robo, violencia basada en género, riesgos de minas y reclutamiento, uso y utilización por grupos armados. 

Las actividades de Protección contra violencia miran a prevenir la violencia antes de que ocurra, mientras se contribuye a la restauración de la seguridad para comunidades e individuos en riesgo. Se logra este resultado asegurando que los individuos sobrevivientes de violencia tengan recursos y capacidades de enfrentamiento mejoradas, aumentando la resiliencia y capacidad de mitigación frente a los riesgos de comunidades expuestas, fortaleciendo políticas públicas que protejan los individuos más vulnerables, y mejorando las capacidades de respuestas de instituciones y autoridades. 

Las actividades incluyen servicios individuales especializados de protección como gestión de casos y asistencia inmediata de protección, acompañamiento protectivo y apoyo psicosocial individual estructurado; acciones de autoprotección civil que incluyen mapeo de los riesgos dirigidos por las comunidades, aumento de capacidad en protección para miembros de comunidades, diseño y fortalecimiento de estrategias de autoprotección civil, asesoría y acompañamiento a las comunidades; actividades de fortalecimiento de entornos, incluyendo monitoreo y análisis de protección, protección por incidencia, y fortalecimiento de los mecanismos de coordinación de protección. Las actividades incluyen también intervención en contextos de emergencias como desplazamientos masivos, confinamientos, desastres naturales e incluyen evaluación rápida de necesidades de protección, asistencias de protección inmediata, entrenamientos en protección para líderes y lideresas, campañas de comunicación y talleres de manejo de estrés durante emergencias. 

En línea con la Estrategia de Protección de NRC, y dentro del contexto de respuesta a las dinámicas del conflicto armado en Colombia , el programa de protección se enfocará en personas afectadas por violencia, coerción y deprivación deliberadas con un énfasis particular en líderes y lideresas comunitarias, sociales y ambientalistas; comunidades expuestas a riesgos de protección como desplazamiento forzado, restricción de movilidad, confinamientos, amenazas, homicidios, violencia física y psicológica; individuos sobrevivientes o en riesgo de violencia, abuso, explotación, deprivación. 

Las intervenciones de protección contra violencia se priorizarán para los grupos más vulnerables como líderes/as sociales y defensores de derechos humanos, miembros de comunidades rurales, comunidades afrocolombianas e indígenas, mujeres y comunidad LGBTQI+. 

Con respecto a la respuesta por parte de ICLA, las personas desplazadas internas recibirán gestión de casos legales a través de la información, orientación y asistencia legal para acceso al registro de víctimas, acceso a derechos y servicios esenciales como educación y salud, acceso a identidad legal y regularización migratoria en el caso de las personas refugiadas y migrantes afectadas por el conflicto armado, acceso a derechos de vivienda tierra y propiedad y acceso a derechos de empleo. Esto a través de los servicios implementados en territorio a través del Contact Centre, atención en oficinas, espacios protectores, clínicas móviles y actividades de intervención con enfoque comunitario. Adicional, facilitaremos asistencia técnica y capacitación a entidades públicas y otras organizaciones, para el fortalecimiento integral en el territorio.

Respuesta integrada de servicios especializados de Protección de NRC que reducen y mitigan el impacto del conflicto armado colombiano sobre personas desplazadas internas y comunidades afectadas por el mismo, permitiéndoles satisfacer necesidades urgentes, acceder a mecanismos de protección, disfrutar de sus derechos básicos y alcanzar soluciones duraderas. Los proyectos de Protección de NRC involucran el trabajo de dos equipos, por un lado, servicios especializados de protección y, por el otro lado, servicios de asistencia legal. 

Los proyectos de Protección contra violencia de NRC buscan reducir y mitigar el impacto de la violencia y el conflicto sobre individuos y comunidades expuestas al conflicto armado interno colombiano; inclusive riesgos de protección como amenazas, asesinatos, desplazamiento forzado, confinamiento, explotación, extorsión, robo, violencia basada en género, riesgos de minas y reclutamiento, uso y utilización por grupos armados. 

Las actividades de Protección contra violencia miran a prevenir la violencia antes de que ocurra, mientras se contribuye a la restauración de la seguridad para comunidades e individuos en riesgo. Se logra este resultado asegurando que los individuos sobrevivientes de violencia tengan recursos y capacidades de enfrentamiento mejoradas, aumentando la resiliencia y capacidad de mitigación frente a los riesgos de comunidades expuestas, fortaleciendo políticas públicas que protejan los individuos más vulnerables, y mejorando las capacidades de respuestas de instituciones y autoridades. 

Las actividades incluyen servicios individuales especializados de protección como gestión de casos y asistencia inmediata de protección, acompañamiento protectivo y apoyo psicosocial individual estructurado; acciones de autoprotección civil que incluyen mapeo de los riesgos dirigidos por las comunidades, aumento de capacidad en protección para miembros de comunidades, diseño y fortalecimiento de estrategias de autoprotección civil, asesoría y acompañamiento a las comunidades; actividades de fortalecimiento de entornos, incluyendo monitoreo y análisis de protección, protección por incidencia, y fortalecimiento de los mecanismos de coordinación de protección. Las actividades incluyen también intervención en contextos de emergencias como desplazamientos masivos, confinamientos, desastres naturales e incluyen evaluación rápida de necesidades de protección, asistencias de protección inmediata, entrenamientos en protección para líderes y lideresas, campañas de comunicación y talleres de manejo de estrés durante emergencias. 

En línea con la Estrategia de Protección de NRC, y dentro del contexto de respuesta a las dinámicas del conflicto armado en Colombia , el programa de protección se enfocará en personas afectadas por violencia, coerción y deprivación deliberadas con un énfasis particular en líderes y lideresas comunitarias, sociales y ambientalistas; comunidades expuestas a riesgos de protección como desplazamiento forzado, restricción de movilidad, confinamientos, amenazas, homicidios, violencia física y psicológica; individuos sobrevivientes o en riesgo de violencia, abuso, explotación, deprivación. 

Las intervenciones de protección contra violencia se priorizarán para los grupos más vulnerables como líderes/as sociales y defensores de derechos humanos, miembros de comunidades rurales, comunidades afrocolombianas e indígenas, mujeres y comunidad LGBTQI+. 

Con respecto a la respuesta por parte de ICLA, las personas desplazadas internas recibirán gestión de casos legales a través de la información, orientación y asistencia legal para acceso al registro de víctimas, acceso a derechos y servicios esenciales como educación y salud, acceso a identidad legal y regularización migratoria en el caso de las personas refugiadas y migrantes afectadas por el conflicto armado, acceso a derechos de vivienda tierra y propiedad y acceso a derechos de empleo. Esto a través de los servicios implementados en territorio a través del Contact Centre, atención en oficinas, espacios protectores, clínicas móviles y actividades de intervención con enfoque comunitario. Adicional, facilitaremos asistencia técnica y capacitación a entidades públicas y otras organizaciones, para el fortalecimiento integral en el territorio.

populations affected by conflict and displacement in Colombia. Provision of emergency humanitarian and protection assistance to 
populations affected by conflict and displacement in Colombia. Provisión de asistencia en el sector de WASH para la atención de emergencias humanitarias y contribución a soluciones duraderas para población afectada por el conflicto armado y comunidades anfitrionas vulnerables en Colombia NRC contribuirá para que las personas afectadas restauren y mantengan su salud, reduzcan su exposición a riesgos y protejan sus derechos al acceso a agua y saneamiento con respeto a su dignidad. NRC, especialmente en el marco del apoyo a soluciones duraderas, fortalecerá las capacidades de las comunidades afectadas e instituciones locales para mantener la salud, seguridad y dignidad para las personas afectadas por desastres y conflicto armado. Las actividades a realizar serán las siguientes: 1. Asistencia emergencial con NFIs de higiene con enfoque diferencial. 2. Construcción, mejoramiento o mantenimiento de sistemas de abastecimiento de agua a nivel individual y colectivo. 3. Mejoramiento o mantenimiento de sistemas de saneamiento colectivo. 4. Cambio comportamental enfocado en prácticas de higiene, a través de la sensibilización y la formación.

Protection and humanitarian multi-faceted needs of conflict -and displacement-affected communities in hard-to-reach areas of Nariño and NdS are addressed through a multisectoral response, encompassing emergency and protection assistance, including the strengthening of community protection strategies. Respuesta integral de emergencia en Nariño y Norte de Santander DRC brindará asistencia humanitaria de emergencia a las personas afectadas por el conflicto en los departamentos de Nariño y Norte de Santander, donde los ciclos persistentes de violencia desencadenan en situaciones de vulnerabilidad para la población como los desplazamientos internos, confinamientos masivos y necesidades específicas de protección sin atender. La presencia humanitaria e institucional es extremadamente limitada en ambas áreas de intervención debido al aislamiento geográfico y los desafíos logísticos, como la infraestructura vial deficiente, junto con los peligros relacionados con el conflicto armado que impiden el acceso humanitario seguro y permanente. DRC contribuirá a reducir los riesgos y vulnerabilidades de las poblaciones expuestas a estas dinámicas de conflicto, con énfasis en atender las necesidades de protección y fortalecer la respuesta a través de una coordinación efectiva y oportuna entre las partes interesadas relevantes. Teniendo en cuenta los desafíos de seguridad relacionados con el contexto relacionados con la prestación exclusiva de servicios de protección, DRC brindará protección por presencia en paralelo a la prestación de servicios y asistencia en especie. Esta modalidad de respuesta ha demostrado ser la modalidad más adecuada para ganar confianza e involucrar a las comunidades y obtener acceso inmediato a las personas que enfrentan necesidades urgentes. Las principales actividades de la intervención son: 
Monitoreo de protección (PM): asistencia legal, difusión de información legal y de protección, asistencia de protección individual (IPA), 
participación comunitaria: QUIP (proyectos de impacto rápido) a través de un enfoque basado en la comunidad.
Seguridad Alimentaria y Medios de Vida: Distribuciones de alimentos de emergencia (kits de alimentos familiares), Entrega de efectivo multipropósito para familias en condición de inseguridad alimentaria
WASH: Kits de emergencia (kits de higiene familiar, kits Dignidad, kits para bebés, filtros de agua portátiles), rehabilitaciones WASH

Thematic Cross Sectoral - Education Education support for Syria’s children and youth affected by crisis As per HNO 2024, the sector PIN indicates a 4% increase from the previous year for children and teachers in need of education assistance. Access to education remains a challenge for many children, as the numbers of Out of School Children remain high. The main barriers are related to the deteriorating economic situation and the ongoing protracted crisis. Even for children in school, learning spaces continue to be unconducive with overcrowded classrooms, limited number of teachers and limited availability of teaching and learning materials.
UNICEF proposes to provide 3,182,074 children and teachers with education services in areas of severity 3-5. This includes children from preprimary, primary and secondary school-aged girls and boys to enable them to develop foundational numeracy and literacy skills, as well as life and citizenship skills, in order to strengthen child, family and community resilience. Additionally, support to enhance the physical learning spaces as well as provision of psychosocial support for children and teachers. 
UNICEF will contribute to: 
A. Providing equitable access to education 
B. Supporting quality education in protective environment
C. Strengthening education systems 
Access will be promoted through Back-to-Learning Campaigns, Vouchers-for-Education, provision of non-formal education programs, school textbooks and school supplies, support to national exams to enhance access to accredited education as part of a multi-sector approach, rehabilitation of schools (formal and nonformal) and provision of temporary classrooms. Rehabilitation is also needed in lower severity areas, where displaced children and returnees as well as large numbers of host community children reside, to contribute to resilience and social cohesion. 
For school rehabilitation UNICEF coordinates with relevant authorities to identify schools in need. UNICEF conducts an assessment to confirm needs and works through vetted independent contractors to commence rehabilitation, including the improvement of WASH facilities, enhancing accessibility for children with disabilities. This is complemented by the provision of school furniture and supplies.
UNICEF will support the Self-learning program to ensure that OOSC have an opportunity to learn, this includes provision of materials, establishment of learning spaces, provision of supplies and support to teacher training. To improve the quality of education services, UNICEF will ensure schools are child-friendly, with teachers trained in child-centered pedagogy, and where children develop academic, cognitive, life and psychosocial skills that empower them to engage, relate, cope and contribute to community and family life. Due to the large number of children at different learning levels within grades, children will be provided with remedial learning support. To support system resilience, UNICEF will establish Parent Teacher Associations that cooperate with Headmasters, and train education staff on monitoring schools, staff performance and children’s learning. UNICEF monitors ongoing activities through staff and implementing partner visits, Third Partner Monitoring and through established feedback mechanisms. In NWS, TPMs provide on-site verification and beneficiary interviews.

Water sanitation Conflict-affected households in North Syria provided with access to sufficient and safe WASH services and improved hygiene conditions Mercy Corps (MC) will respond to priority needs with life-saving and life-sustaining WASH assistance across the governorates of Al-Hasakeh, Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa, Deir-ez-Zor and Idleb - Across both Northeast and Northwest Syria. 

Informed by a multi-sectoral needs assessment conducted in September in 2023 on WASH needs at WoS level, MC will work on improving access to basic Water and sanitation services through the delivery of water trucking, SWM, Desludging and the rehabilitation of water supply infrastructure in IDP locations and areas with a high number of IDPs and returnees, and areas we anticipate significant inward displacement (Ar-Raqqa and DEZ, Dana, Daret Azza and Atareb in Idleb and north Aleppo). OCHA Carry over from 2023 to 2024 Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre de son mandat et son rôle auprès des partenaires humanitaires et gouvernementaux au niveau des fonctions coordination, gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant un lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.
Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters, des groupes de travail et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.
Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires, catastrophes naturelles) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet.
OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

The nutrition sector estimates that 4.7 million children under five and pregnant and lactating women are acutely malnourished and in need humanitarian assistance in 2024.

Through this project, UNICEF aims to (1) increase equitable access to an integrated lifesaving and preventive nutrition services focusing more on the “1000- day window”- as a critical opportunity to prevent child wasting and stunting among under five children, (2) improve early detection of acute malnutrition (3) improve access to quality lifesaving nutrition services to treat severe acute malnutrition among under-five children. UNICEF will target all states in the country with more focus on hotspots and IDP hosting states through scaling up integrated lifesaving nutrition preventive and curative services.

The preventive package includes iron-folate supplementation for pregnant and lactating women, maternal, infant and young child feeding nutrition (MIYCN) counseling and support for pregnant and lactating women. The package for under five children includes the provision of micronutrient supplements, Growth Monitoring and Promotion, as well as deworming. Overall, 1.4 million pregnant and lactating women, and over 4.9 million under five will be targeted with the preventive package. UNICEF will work toward the expansion of the geographical coverage of the treatment programme for severe acute malnutrition through the establishment of fixed and mobile sites to reach the planned target of 539,858 children under five suffering from SAM, representing 75 per cent of children under five with SAM in 2024. •Secure the pipeline of all essential preventive and curative nutrition supplies to prevent and treat children with malnutrition.

Syria - Support access to education Education support for Syria’s children and youth affected by crisis As per HNO 2024, the sector PIN indicates a 4% increase from the previous year for children and teachers in need of education assistance. Access to education remains a challenge for many children, as the numbers of Out of School Children remain high. The main barriers are related to the deteriorating economic situation and the ongoing protracted crisis. Even for children in school, learning spaces continue to be unconducive with overcrowded classrooms, limited number of teachers and limited availability of teaching and learning materials.
UNICEF proposes to provide 3,182,074 children and teachers with education services in areas of severity 3-5. This includes children from preprimary, primary and secondary school-aged girls and boys to enable them to develop foundational numeracy and literacy skills, as well as life and citizenship skills, in order to strengthen child, family and community resilience. Additionally, support to enhance the physical learning spaces as well as provision of psychosocial support for children and teachers. 
UNICEF will contribute to: 
A. Providing equitable access to education 
B. Supporting quality education in protective environment
C. Strengthening education systems 
Access will be promoted through Back-to-Learning Campaigns, Vouchers-for-Education, provision of non-formal education programs, school textbooks and school supplies, support to national exams to enhance access to accredited education as part of a multi-sector approach, rehabilitation of schools (formal and nonformal) and provision of temporary classrooms. Rehabilitation is also needed in lower severity areas, where displaced children and returnees as well as large numbers of host community children reside, to contribute to resilience and social cohesion. 
For school rehabilitation UNICEF coordinates with relevant authorities to identify schools in need. UNICEF conducts an assessment to confirm needs and works through vetted independent contractors to commence rehabilitation, including the improvement of WASH facilities, enhancing accessibility for children with disabilities. This is complemented by the provision of school furniture and supplies.
UNICEF will support the Self-learning program to ensure that OOSC have an opportunity to learn, this includes provision of materials, establishment of learning spaces, provision of supplies and support to teacher training. To improve the quality of education services, UNICEF will ensure schools are child-friendly, with teachers trained in child-centered pedagogy, and where children develop academic, cognitive, life and psychosocial skills that empower them to engage, relate, cope and contribute to community and family life. Due to the large number of children at different learning levels within grades, children will be provided with remedial learning support. To support system resilience, UNICEF will establish Parent Teacher Associations that cooperate with Headmasters, and train education staff on monitoring schools, staff performance and children’s learning. UNICEF monitors ongoing activities through staff and implementing partner visits, Third Partner Monitoring and through established feedback mechanisms. In NWS, TPMs provide on-site verification and beneficiary interviews. 
PROTECTION RISK ANALYSIS
1. Attack on education and safety of children on their way to school 2.Increased risks of GBV if latrines are not separated or there are no locks on the doors and light. 3.Increased risk of host-community tension due to assistance packages given to IDPs, 4. Risk of sexual exploitation by Teacher education personnel, NGO staff (risk of harassment) of boys and girls 5. Teachers or other education personnel participate in physical punishment or bullying of students Or Students participate in bullying of students
PSEA policy will be respected as per UNICEF rules and mandate.
RISKS, ASSUMPTIONS AND MITIGATION MEASURES Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation Children working with contractors Zero tolerance

Capitalisant sur les acquis des pratiques éducatives le projet mettra en place une gamme variée d’offres éducatives non formelles en vue de lever les obstacles à la scolarisation des enfants et assurer leur enrôlement, maintien et transition vers d’autres opportunités d’éducation ou de formation. SHO funds for Social Protection Expanding Social, Civic and Economic Engagement and Social Cohesion Interventions for Conﬂict-Affected Adolescents and Youth in the Syrian Arab Republic Needs: Young people in Syria face a myriad of interrelated barriers that prevent their meaningful economic, social, and civic participation and engagement. They face stigma and discrimination regarding their capacities to lead positive change in their communities. Limited opportunities for economic, social, and civic engagement, particularly for the most marginalized adolescents and youth, contribute to their systematic exclusion and exacerbate feelings of isolation and disenfranchisement. However, experiences from other contexts of protracted crisis have shown that supporting young people’s social and civic engagement can have positive social outcomes and be conducive to increased community resilience and social cohesion.
Intervention: In support of the ERL Sector, UNICEF will further its support for the Generation Unlimited initiative and No Lost Generation Agenda by empowering vulnerable adolescents and youth, both female and male, as well as those with disabilities, to access social, civic, and economic opportunities for skill development and engagement (including participation in social cohesion initiatives) with the objective of contributing to enhancing resilience and social cohesion. UNICEF will build on strategic partnerships, integration, and at-scale programming focusing on the most vulnerable adolescents to strengthen skills development, employability, and meaningful engagement through friendly spaces and mobile teams. The proposed project will support 342,883 young women and men per year to have better access to civic, social, and economic opportunities for skill development and engagement, and to unleash their potentials and increase their learning, leadership, and employability opportunities. UNICEF will work in the following two pillars and related interventions: (1) Strengthen social, civic, and economic engagement of adolescents and youth and foster volunteerism and social cohesion-building. (2) Support young entrepreneurs to start their own projects through seed funding. UNICEF will continue strengthening the capacity of local partners, including services providers, youth workers, and young volunteers, to improve the quality of provided services and enhance evidence generation.
Protection Risk Analysis: After enduring 12 years of conflict and ongoing economic turmoil, young Syrians have faced devastating hardships that have eroded their resilience. This has particularly affected girls, who have resorted to harmful coping mechanisms such as dropping out of school, engaging in addictive behaviors, entering child labor, and marrying early. Social norms in many communities also hinder girls' and people with disabilities' participation in sports, cultural activities, and community engagement. The compounding effects of COVID-19, earthquakes, and economic challenges have exacerbated these risks. UNICEF will continue to mainstream the principles of safety, dignity, and do no harm, as well as the inclusive and meaningful access of the most marginalized boys and girls, especially those who live with disabilities, to ensure that no one is left behind. UNICEF will increase safe access to skills development, social cohesion, awareness-raising, and engagement opportunities. UNICEF will prioritize developing the capacity of the implementing partners through providing technical support in the fields of Child Safeguarding, Code of Conduct, and PSEA.
Risks: Economic deterioration and transportation barriers, along with potential conflicts between IDPs and host communities, as well as risks of exploitation or abuse. To address these risks, there will be capacity building for staff and volunteers, awareness campaigns on risks, mandatory screening during recruitment, establishing complaint mechanisms with adequate staff for follow-up, and ensuring data protection and confidentiality.

Assumptions: The project assumes support for integrated and joint approaches and the promotion of youth participation nationwide.
