Strengthening Child Protection interventions for girls and boys most at risk of violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation across whole of Syria In light of the devastating and long-term effects of earthquakes, ongoing armed conflict, limited livelihood opportunities, as well as new and old layers of explosive contamination in Syria, the ongoing hostilities, protracted displacement, and economic crisis highlighted
in the HNO 2024 have further weakened the protective environment and resilience of communities. This situation exposes children to greater risks of violence, abuse, exploitation, and neglect. Explosive hazard contamination not only poses severe socioeconomic implications for families and communities by depriving them of livelihoods and sources of income but also increases vulnerabilities. Insecurity and economic hardship persist, exacerbating child protection concerns and leading to harmful coping mechanisms such as the worst forms of labor and child marriage. Additionally, high levels of psychosocial distress prevail among children and caregivers due to multiple stresses, including the continued escalation of conflict, poverty, earthquakes, and restrictions on movement that limit access to social services.

In line with the CP AOR Strategy, UNICEF will enhance equitable access to quality CP services with a resilience focus, for prevention and response to CP risks, including for survivors of abuse, violence, neglect and exploitation, CWD, unaccompanied and separated children, targeting high severity sub-districts.

UNICEF will focus the intervention under this proposal on the following activities:
• The provision of structured MHPSS activities for 234,500 girls and boys through child-friendly spaces, mobile teams, and community structures.
• Engagement of 50,000 parents and caregivers in structured and sustained parenting programmes to facilitate the creation of a safe and enabling environment in families and communities free from violence against children.
• Implement EORE sessions for 653,600 children and parents/caregivers in communities including through using mobile teams.
• Provide integrated specialized child protection services, through case management, to 16,920 children, including family tracing and reunification for separated and unaccompanied children, children in contact with the law, violence against children, child marriage, child labour, and children with disabilities.
• Build technical capacity of 3,000 implementing partners' social workers on child protection/GBV services delivery and ensure regular monitoring of activities. In coordination with the GBV AoR UNICEF will build capacities on GBV risk mitigation.
• Elimination of VAC, including GBV prevention and empowerment for 120,550 girls, boys, and women, and prevention of violence in schools, homes, and communities through awareness-raising sessions.
• Awareness-raising on CP risks and SBC interventions on child protection issues for 200,000 girls, boys, women and men.

UNICEF will generate evidence to inform the humanitarian response and advocacy, including setting up an information management system for case management. UNICEF will also continue to support the Monitoring and Reporting Mechanism on grave violations against children.

Violence prevention is a key priority. UNICEF will work to protect children from violence and abuse through prevention activities in schools, homes, and communities and by providing survivors of violence with child-friendly and gender-sensitive services. Support will be provided for PSEA mechanisms to protect beneficiaries and build the capacity of humanitarian actors.

PSEA by humanitarian workers and service providers is high on the UNICEF agenda to ensure that no violations and abuse happen during implementation. UNICEF, as co-lead for the ICN on PSEA, will continue to support and work closely with other agencies to enhance the PSEA portfolio by building continuous capacity for humanitarian workers with zero tolerance for SEA. As a pre-condition for contracting implementing partners, PSEA assurance and capacity-building plans are guaranteed.

Au 28 septembre, plus de 420 834 réfugiés et 67 780 retournés, dont plus de 280 000 enfants, avaient cherché refuge au Tchad, via 32 points d’entrée le long de la frontière, dans les trois provinces du Ouaddaï, du Sila et de Wadi-Fira, qui comptent parmi les provinces les plus défavorisées du Tchad. Parmi les réfugiés, se trouvent 37 542 populations hotes qui ont aceptes d’accueillir ces derniers.  Parmi ces réfugiés et communautés hotes, figurent des personnes vulnérables ayant des besoins spéciaux, telles que les femmes chefs de famille, les personnes âgées et, surtout, les personnes traumatisées par leur expérience au Soudan et ayant besoin d’une assistance multiforme.
Ce présent projet vient compléter les efforts déployés par les autres partenaires de mise en œuvre (ONG nationales et internationales) et des agences UN en particulier UNICEF en vue de répondre aux besoins clés, parmi lesquels les besoins en WASH et de la response cholera.
La stratégie de réponse aux besoins vitaux se focalisera sur le renforcement de l’accès aux services EHA aux personnes déplacées, expulsées ou retournées et aux ménages d’accueil affectés par des mouvements de population a travers:
- Des programmes de réalisation et de réhabilitation des infrastructures hydrauliques, de renforcement de l’assainissement, d’appui au système de gestion des services d’eau,  des campagnes de sensibilisation aux pratiques d’hygiène, de distribution des kits WASH et de dignite et de l’éradication de la défécation à l’air libre, à travers l’approche ATPC (assainissement totalement piloté par la communauté) seront à promouvoir.

- Les interventions basées sur le marché seront considérées pour l'achat de l'eau et/ou aux items d’hygiène et/ou à la construction de latrines pour les populations vulnérables à travers un appui monétaire ou coupon, au courant de cette année
- Les activites et intervention de lute et de prevention contre le cholera.

Enhanced Humanitarian Assistance, Social Cohesion and Resilience for Crisis-Affected Populations in Niger Assistance d'urgence aux personnes déplacées dans les régions de Tahoua et Tillabéri Dans le cadre du HRP 2024, partant de la stratégie du Groupe de Travail Abris et Biens Non Alimentaires (GTABNA) et en étroite collaboration avec le Ministère de l’Action Humanitaire, l'OIM comme membre du cluster poursuit l'objectif général de contribuer à l'amélioration les conditions de vie des populations. En particulier des populations déplacées vulnérables victimes des crises armées du Mali, dans les régions de Tahoua et de Tillabéri, par la fourniture d'abris d'urgence et de Biens Non Alimentaires. En tant que Co-Lead du Cluster Abris et Biens Non Alimentaires,  l'OIM va contribuer au  renforcement de la coordination du Groupe de travail Abris et Biens Non Alimentaires, contribuer à renforcer la collecte des informations de façon régulière dans le souci d'informer les intervenants sur la localisation, la nature et l'ampleur des besoins exprimés, de continuer à appuyer les partenaires et membres du secteur à mener les activités dans le respect de la stratégie du Groupe de Travail et les principes humanitaires et d'appuyer les services étatiques locaux dans leurs rôles de coordination et suivi des activités du secteur. La situation sécuritaire dans les régions de Tahoua et Tillabéri étant toujours volatile, le GTABNA reste attentif à tout mouvement de population et suit la situation au travers des annonces de sécurité, les MSA de RRM et le monitoring de protection du cluster protection fournissant les informations indicatives à la réponse en abris d’urgence et Biens Non Alimentaires.  Partant de la cible du HRP 2023, le secteur abris et bien non alimentaire mettra à disposition 5000 kits abris d’urgence et 5000 kits BNA en vue de répondre aux nouveaux mouvements de population, aux mouvements secondaires ainsi qu'au renouvèlement des abris détériorés des ménages. L’assistance basée sur la vulnérabilité ciblera également les familles hôtes vulnérables. Sur base de la stratégie du Secteur abris/BNA et dépendamment de la faisabilité, les interventions pourront se faire en transfert monétaires conditionnels. Cette modalité offrira la réduction considérable des coûts logistiques qui sont très élevés en période hivernale à cause du mauvais état des routes et permettrade résoudre le problème d’accès lié à l'insécurité qui retarde les interventions. Les activités de la réponse d'urgence se conformeront aux Principes de Protection transversales et au Cadre institutionnel de l'OIM de lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre en situation de crise (GBV), intégrera des mesures visant à assurer la sécurité, la dignité et le bien-être de la population touchée. Ce projet s'inscrira dans le respect des principes humanitaires et portera une attention particulière au principe ne pas nuire, de sécurité et non-discrimination. Dans le cadre de la redevabilité des sessions d'information sur le projet seront organisées avec les bénéficiaires, la phase d'évaluation des besoins sera réalisée de commun accord avec les populations dans les communes ciblées, la communication avec les communautés et les autorités locales sur les critères de ciblage seront organisées et après intervention, les feedbacks de la communauté cible seront collectés à travers des évaluations post-distribution et des séances de discussion de groupe séparées par genre et âge avant et après l'assistance. Aussi, en tant qu’acteur humanitaire, l'OIM et ses partenaires de mise en œuvre s’assureront que les actions n’induisent aucune tension ou problème dans la zone et n’exposent pas les bénéficiaires en affichant les compositions de kits BNA et Abris. A cet effet. Une collaboration étroite sera faite avec les acteurs de protection pour un suivi de prêt de toute question de protection. Le coût total du projet sera de 3 045 000 USD.

Food Assistance Cash and Food assistance to 70 000 refugees in the Minawao Camp in the Far North Region, 39 200 in the East region and 31 200 in the North and Adamaoua Regions Through the project WFP will provide cash and food support to 140 400 refugees in the targeted regions of the Far North, East, North and Adamaoua, in line with WFP Cameroon Country Strategic Plan (CSP 2022-2026). Targeting will be refined alongside physical verifications to ensure that only the most extremely food insecure households will be assisted. The project proposes to continue providing lifesaving support to extremely vulnerable CAR refugees households to ensure they are able to meet their immediate food security and nutrition needs, as well as essential needs. 
The transfer modality of food assistance to the beneficiaries will be initially in-kind food through unconditional monthly food distributions to support refugees’ households’ access to adequate and nutritious food, therefore prevent them from adopting negative coping practices. The full ration of the in-kind distributions will provide 1, 095kcal energy per day per person for the beneficiaries who entirely rely on humanitarian food assistance. A minimum percentage of 50% of beneficiaries will be gradually moved to cash assistance at the end of 2024. Mechanisms will be put in place to evaluate the evolution of household’s needs to ensure a graduation approach from one form of assistance to the other.

The daily ration for the specialized nutritious foods per assisted child will be 100 g.
Communication activities will be intensified to inform on the temporal nature of food assistance and the need to graduate towards early recovery and resilience activities as well as SBCC messages formulated to accompany food security and nutrition activities.

To save lives and alleviate suffering Provision of Integrated Safe, Equitable, Protective and Inclusive Education to Conflict Affected Boys and Girls in South Sudan. In 2023 an estimated 9.4 million people, more than two thirds of the country’s population, are in need of humanitarian assistance – 53% of people in need are children. In this context, education plays a crucial role for South Sudan’s children. Education provides safety, keeping children and youth from physical harm, whilst also contributing to psychosocial wellbeing and health, when complemented by WASH and school feeding interventions. Schools provide safe spaces that also function as a platform to deliver lifesaving interventions, such as food, water, sanitation, mental and physical health services. Education programmes mitigate the impact of humanitarian crises by building resilience among children, young people and their communities. Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) programmes in education curricula and preparedness plans equip and strengthen children’s ability to deal with emergencies and mitigate the impact of future disasters. WV will implement EiE projects in the counties where it has a strong operational presence, characterized with very high needs, especially in education and other related sectors: CES (Juba) Upper Nile (Malakal, Melut, Renk), WES (Yambio, Nzara, Tambura), Warrap (Tonj North, Twic, Gogrial East, Gogrial West, Tonj South and Tonj East), Northern Bahr El Ghazal (Aweil North, Aweil South) targeting populations affected by conflict or disaster in 2023.

WV is currently implementing education programs in partnership with ECHO, Education Can't Wait, EMPOWER Irish Aid, UNHCR and GPE. To consolidate on current efforts while reaching further and deeper into the areas with dire needs, in hard-to-reach areas WV will continue to focus on emergency affected rural and urban areas. 

In line with the Education Cluster Response Plan, WV will ensure that through this project, 28,200 children will have access to safe and equitable quality education; 600 teachers, and 650 PTA’s will be trained and supported with supplies and materials; 1500 youth will be provided life skills and vocational training with starter kits. Out of the identified learners, the project will target about 400 children (200 boys, 200 girls) with disabilities. The learners will also be categorized under social/residential status as internally displaced, host community, or refugees during the actual enrolment in the project.

WV will also prioritize establishment of learning structures with gender-segregated WASH facilities, and other supplies/materials/kits that are supportive and enhance motivation of children to go to and remain in school with a particular emphasis on girl’s education. In addition, recreational opportunities will be established and implemented to support the recovery of children and youth and promote their overall wellbeing. All learners will be given equal access to education despite Gender, disability or ethnic background.

Humanitarian support 2024 DRC (Danish Refugee Council) 2024 Protection Response for Sudan DRC works alongside affected communities and local authorities to address protection issues and meet basic needs in food security and livelihoods (FSL), shelter and non-food items (SNFI), and humanitarian mine action (HMA) in Sudan. DRC has also started implementing activities within water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), site management support (SMS), and multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA) sectors to address the growing emergency needs and widening gaps in support to affected communities impacted by the war.

DRC will continue to target Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), host communities and returnees in Central Darfur, Khartoum, and South Kordofan as well as refugees in Gedaref along with other vulnerable groups in the state. Since the war broke out, DRC has also added two more operational bases: White Nile State and Al Jeziera, and will be expanding programmatic operations to Port Sudan within the coming months. In South Kordofan, DRC operates a non-technical Mine Action programme through two activities:  (1) providing EORE to vulnerable persons and (2) conducting non-technical surveys

DRC has grown its emergency response through several interventions such as intersectoral mobile response teams and cross border programming. For the former, these teams will be based in Port Sudan and Gedaref but able to be deployed throughout Red Sea State, Northern State, Gedaref, River Nile, Sennar and Kassala. Regarding the latter, DRC will work with its counterparts in South Sudan and Chad to support cross border populations. From Sudan, this programming will particularly focus on those located in Darfur and White Nile State with possible support in South Kordofan. Furthermore, DRC has been providing technical and financial support to a local partner in Khartoum. The partner has been providing emergency support since the start of the war in Khartoum to support life-saving self-relocations of highly vulnerable individuals.

In addition to direct and immediate assistance and despite the challenges due to the outbreak of the conflict in April 2023, DRC continues to engage in and implement programming to build resilience and support for vulnerable populations, particularly with displaced and returnee communities; to address their priority needs, reducing aid dependency, supporting early recovery and paving pathways to durable solutions. One key dimension to this work is through ensuring that all stakeholder groups’ needs and vulnerabilities are considered and accounted for in the project’s implementation; community engagement, mobilization, and feedback are also key to the approach, ensuring participation of all relevant stakeholder groups. DRC also focuses on partnership building to ensure complimentary and integrated response and programming.

Throughout its interventions, DRC works to secure government buy-in and ensure that coordination with relevant federal, state, and local authorities is continuous throughout all projects such as HAC and line ministries. DRC will also collaborate with local NGOs and representative community structures that already have an operational presence in the areas of intervention. This approach aims to increase the efficiency of community engagement while improving the ownership of the local community and actors in the response. The engagement of local actors will improve local acceptance and understanding of the activities and serve to ease the delivery of activities vis-à-vis communities and authorities, given that these stakeholders are already part of the community and are familiar with the social context and its internal dynamics.

Cycle IV of the MIRE Rapid Response Mechanism: front line protection and humanitarian assistance to conflict-affected communities in Colombia Respuesta integrada de servicios especializados de Protección de NRC que reducen y mitigan el impacto del conflicto armado colombiano sobre personas desplazadas internas y comunidades afectadas por el mismo, permitiéndoles satisfacer necesidades urgentes, acceder a mecanismos de protección, disfrutar de sus derechos básicos y alcanzar soluciones duraderas. Los proyectos de Protección de NRC involucran el trabajo de dos equipos, por un lado, servicios especializados de protección y, por el otro lado, servicios de asistencia legal. 

Los proyectos de Protección contra violencia de NRC buscan reducir y mitigar el impacto de la violencia y el conflicto sobre individuos y comunidades expuestas al conflicto armado interno colombiano; inclusive riesgos de protección como amenazas, asesinatos, desplazamiento forzado, confinamiento, explotación, extorsión, robo, violencia basada en género, riesgos de minas y reclutamiento, uso y utilización por grupos armados. 

Las actividades de Protección contra violencia miran a prevenir la violencia antes de que ocurra, mientras se contribuye a la restauración de la seguridad para comunidades e individuos en riesgo. Se logra este resultado asegurando que los individuos sobrevivientes de violencia tengan recursos y capacidades de enfrentamiento mejoradas, aumentando la resiliencia y capacidad de mitigación frente a los riesgos de comunidades expuestas, fortaleciendo políticas públicas que protejan los individuos más vulnerables, y mejorando las capacidades de respuestas de instituciones y autoridades. 

Las actividades incluyen servicios individuales especializados de protección como gestión de casos y asistencia inmediata de protección, acompañamiento protectivo y apoyo psicosocial individual estructurado; acciones de autoprotección civil que incluyen mapeo de los riesgos dirigidos por las comunidades, aumento de capacidad en protección para miembros de comunidades, diseño y fortalecimiento de estrategias de autoprotección civil, asesoría y acompañamiento a las comunidades; actividades de fortalecimiento de entornos, incluyendo monitoreo y análisis de protección, protección por incidencia, y fortalecimiento de los mecanismos de coordinación de protección. Las actividades incluyen también intervención en contextos de emergencias como desplazamientos masivos, confinamientos, desastres naturales e incluyen evaluación rápida de necesidades de protección, asistencias de protección inmediata, entrenamientos en protección para líderes y lideresas, campañas de comunicación y talleres de manejo de estrés durante emergencias. 

En línea con la Estrategia de Protección de NRC, y dentro del contexto de respuesta a las dinámicas del conflicto armado en Colombia , el programa de protección se enfocará en personas afectadas por violencia, coerción y deprivación deliberadas con un énfasis particular en líderes y lideresas comunitarias, sociales y ambientalistas; comunidades expuestas a riesgos de protección como desplazamiento forzado, restricción de movilidad, confinamientos, amenazas, homicidios, violencia física y psicológica; individuos sobrevivientes o en riesgo de violencia, abuso, explotación, deprivación. 

Las intervenciones de protección contra violencia se priorizarán para los grupos más vulnerables como líderes/as sociales y defensores de derechos humanos, miembros de comunidades rurales, comunidades afrocolombianas e indígenas, mujeres y comunidad LGBTQI+. 

Con respecto a la respuesta por parte de ICLA, las personas desplazadas internas recibirán gestión de casos legales a través de la información, orientación y asistencia legal para acceso al registro de víctimas, acceso a derechos y servicios esenciales como educación y salud, acceso a identidad legal y regularización migratoria en el caso de las personas refugiadas y migrantes afectadas por el conflicto armado, acceso a derechos de vivienda tierra y propiedad y acceso a derechos de empleo. Esto a través de los servicios implementados en territorio a través del Contact Centre, atención en oficinas, espacios protectores, clínicas móviles y actividades de intervención con enfoque comunitario. Adicional, facilitaremos asistencia técnica y capacitación a entidades públicas y otras organizaciones, para el fortalecimiento integral en el territorio.

Flexible humanitarian funding from Save the Children International's Humanitarian Fund Protection des enfants vulnérables affectés par les conflits dans les régions de Diffa et Tillabéry Ce projet vise à améliorer l'environnement protecteur des filles et garçons affectés par les conflits par les biais des mésures préventives, de l'accès inclusif aux services de prise en charge adapaté à leur besoins, ainsi que par le renforcement du système formel et informel de la protection de l'enfant dans les régions de Diffa et Tilabéry. A travers cette intervention, SCI va continuer à se concentrer à promouvoir le cadre politique de la centralité de la protection pour atteindre les enfants les plus touchés et leurs communautés afin que les risques de protection auxquels ils sont confrontés soient identifiés, signalés et prise en charge. Nous nous concentrerons également, sur les dommages causés par les violations des droits et leur impact sur les filles différemment des garçons en tenant compte de leur capacité pour une réponse individualisée de la gestion de cas intégrant le soutien psychosocial et la réintégration socioéconomique. Pour renforcer le système de protection, une cartographie des services et un circuit  de référencement harmonisé seront regulièment actualisés pour promouvoir l’accès aux services essentiels assurant un environnement protecteur. En outre, Les acteurs communautaires seront mobilisés et formés aux outils et approches d'information et de sensibilisation adaptés aux enfants, afin d'assurer un changement de comportement positif et l'adoption de mesures préventives contre les risques et les violations des droits dans les contextes humanitaires.  Les interventions seront orientées vers les enfants les plus vulnérables parmi les populations déplacées internes et les communautés hôtes avec un focus sur ceux difficilement accessible ou en mobilité fréquente en raison de la crise à travers l’approche mobile. Les enfants affectés directement par la crise humanitaire, notamment, les enfants non accompagnés /séparés, associés aux forces et groupes armés et les enfants à risque d’autres violations ou de violences physiques et sexuelles, bénéficieront d’un appui psychosociale individuel et de groupe dans les espaces amis d’enfants, qui soutiennent la protection, le bien-être et l'apprentissage des enfants dans les crises par le renforcement du système, de la qualité et des méthodologies des activités de SMSPS, garantissant l'amélioration du bien-être des enfants et de leur résilience. Le système de protection sera renforcé à travers les approches intégrée  du modèle socio-écologique et des approches communes de SCI. Notamment, le renforcement des capacités sur la manière dont l'assistance sous forme de transfert monétaire et de bons sera utilisée pour atténuer les risques pour les enfants et soutenir une réponse à leurs besoins.  Les familles les plus vulnérables et les familles d’accueil seront soutenus par le Cash à l'aide d'un plan d’action individuel « PAI » participatif afin de réduire les vulnérabilités et renforcer la capacité des familles. Pour les enfants touchés par les conflits armés, l'aide comprendra des services destinés aux enfants qui ont besoin d'une aide à la réunification familial, à la réintégration communautaire comme les EAFGA, une aide aux enfants survivants des VBG liées aux conflits, aux victimes d'engins explosifs, ainsi qu'une aide connexe. Afin de renforcer la gestion des cas individualisée pour tous les enfants ayant besoin des multiples services et ayant des risques élevés. Nous allons faire recours à l' approche commune ""Steps to Protect"" de SCI, pour assurer une réponse multisectorielle. Il sera aussi question de déployer le CPIMS+ pour renforcer  la mise en œuvre d'un système de gestion de l'information inter-agences. De monitoring de la situation de protection seront organisées. La collaboration avec les autre secteurs (éducation, santé…VBG) sera envisagée pour mettre en place une intervention multisectorielle et multi acteurs. ceci répondra aux sévérités liées aux incidents de protections aux quels un grand nombre des enfants IDP sont exposés

Syrian Arab Republic HRP 2024		Livelihoods	Emergency employment through rural road rehabilitation for decent jobs and livelihoods recovery (sub-objective 2) Decent Job Creation through Community Infrastructure Works Unemployment rate has continued to deteriorate over the past several years and remains high at 21.9% according to the latest official statistics. Even if a worker has a job, majority of economic activities are estimated to take place in the informal sector, where workers are exposed to decent work deficits such as in terms of lack of access to appropriate wages, social protection coverage, OSH, career development opportunities and prospects, to name but a few. 
Accordingly, ILO proposes to implement two-year employment-intensive infrastructure recovery works with the dual objective of decent job creation and community infrastructure rehabilitation. This approach maximizes the wages rate as percentage of the total expenditures for infrastructure works through alternative engineering solutions. It also promotes decent work principles throughout project lifecycle. The project although it will support the people to meet their immediate needs however, as ILO we do encourage our target groups to be productive, self-reliance and experience good exposure to the labour market especially for youth and women through providing decent employment.
This can be achieved through short-term jobs (3 months) through the community works, roads rehabilitation, and cultural heritage site maintenance. In addition, formal apprenticeship programmes will be implemented with the aim of increase the long-term employability by supporting skills development through on the job training in partnership with local enterprises. The estimated budget is USD 11,614,498 for two years implementation with the aim of creating 4,498 decent short term decent jobs with 323,820 workdays, and 900 beneficiaries enrolled in the apprenticeship programme, generating 93,600 workdays. The proposed interventions will be implemented in Aleppo, Homs, Hama, Lattakia, and Rural Damascus governorates based on the following criteria: number of people in need and target as set by ERL sector; high severity of needs; actual needs for infrastructure improvement for accessibility to basic services; and the presence of ILO and its partners in the targeted areas.
Protection risk 1: There is a risk of biased selection of community members (workers) who engage in the proposed infrastructure works and apprenticeship programmes, at the exclusion of others. Such a skewed selection does more harm than good in terms of social cohesion.(Likelihood: low, Impact: high).
Mitigation plan 1: The project will establish a local steering committee for each area with the equal representation of female, male, youth, people with disability, internally displaced persons, and other concerned parties, to give voices to all in an inclusive manner. Recruitment advertisement will be publicly announced, with an established and agreed upon quota for the particularly vulnerable categories, based on vulnerability assessment. 
Protection risk 2: Occupational injuries of workers at worksites due to exposure to biological, chemical and physical occupational hazards without control measures put in place.(Likelihood: High, Impact: High)
Mitigation plan 2: Occupational safety and health (OSH) training will be conducted prior to start of any worksite activities for infrastructure works, for both workers and employers. Safety managers will be recruited to ensure the safety of the works, while all workers will be covered by injury and health insurance. Targeted training and labour inspection will be conducted at factories for apprenticeship programmes to ensure the compliance of OSH measures by employers.
GBV Risk – Female workers may be exposed to worksite harassment by co-workers or employers during the activities’ execution.(Likelihood: medium, Impact: high).
Mitigation plan – GBV training will be conducted for each worksite to raise awareness in prevention of violence and harassment at work. Assign Female team leaders as a focal point. A help line will be established to receive complaints and provide necessary measures.

------  Sudan: Humanitarian thematic funding for Sudan 2024	Cross-Sectoral (two or more outcome areas)	THM HUMANITAR 2022-2025 UNICEF: Lifesaving nutrition preventive and curative interventions targeting most vulnerable population across Sudan The malnutrition situation in Sudan remains dire with an expected increase in the number of children with acute malnutrition due to the deteriorating nutrition determinants as result of the ongoing catastrophic humanitarian crisis. The nutrition sector estimates that 4.7 million children under five and pregnant and lactating women are acutely malnourished and in need humanitarian assistance in 2024.

Through this project, UNICEF aims to (1) increase equitable access to an integrated lifesaving and preventive nutrition services focusing more on the “1000- day window”- as a critical opportunity to prevent child wasting and stunting among under five children, (2) improve early detection of acute malnutrition (3) improve access to quality lifesaving nutrition services to treat severe acute malnutrition among under-five children. UNICEF will target all states in the country with more focus on hotspots and IDP hosting states through scaling up integrated lifesaving nutrition preventive and curative services.

The preventive package includes iron-folate supplementation for pregnant and lactating women, maternal, infant and young child feeding nutrition (MIYCN) counseling and support for pregnant and lactating women. The package for under five children includes the provision of micronutrient supplements, Growth Monitoring and Promotion, as well as deworming. Overall, 1.4 million pregnant and lactating women, and over 4.9 million under five will be targeted with the preventive package. Additionally, UNICEF will support the provision of cash transfers to 150,000 of the poorest pregnant women and caregivers of children under-two to help eliminate the financial barriers that women and children may experience in accessing nutritious diets and essential nutrition services. UNICEF will ensure more focus on IYCF-E interventions as part of emergency preparedness and response, with intensive advocacy and orientations to mobilize humanitarian partners to protect and support infant feeding in the emergency context.

UNICEF will strengthen early detection and referral of children suffering from wasting. The key strategy will be large-scale integrated nutrition campaigns through house-to-house modality to significantly scale up the early identification, referral, and management of acutely malnourished children, in addition to integrating it with other preventive services such as micronutrient supplementation for children and women. Through this, 4.9 million children under five will be targeted with early detection of wasting and referral activities. 

UNICEF will work toward the expansion of the geographical coverage of the treatment programme for severe acute malnutrition through the establishment of fixed and mobile sites to reach the planned target of 539,858 children under five suffering from SAM, representing 75 per cent of children under five with SAM in 2024. As part of this, UNICEF will continue working closely with WFP and WHO to ensure the complementarity and continuum of care among the three levels of management for acute malnutrition program. Different strategies will be implemented including (i) maintaining functionality and expanding coverage of OTPs to deliver lifesaving nutrition services and (ii) supporting mobile clinics to reach displaced, hard-to-reach communities with lifesaving nutrition services, and (iii) Expanding active case finding.  Additionally, UNICEF will support evidence generation through implementing SMART surveys.  

To support the implementation of integrated preventive and curative nutrition services UNICEF will:
•Secure the pipeline of all essential preventive and curative nutrition supplies to prevent and treat children with malnutrition. 
•Expand the partnerships with various stakeholders across the country.   
•Strengthen the health system through efforts to strengthen supply chain management, nutrition information systems, monitoring, frontline nutrition workers payment and capacity building.

The nutrition sector estimates that 4.7 million children under five and pregnant and lactating women are acutely malnourished and in need humanitarian assistance in 2024.

Through this project, UNICEF aims to (1) increase equitable access to an integrated lifesaving and preventive nutrition services focusing more on the “1000- day window”- as a critical opportunity to prevent child wasting and stunting among under five children, (2) improve early detection of acute malnutrition (3) improve access to quality lifesaving nutrition services to treat severe acute malnutrition among under-five children. UNICEF will target all states in the country with more focus on hotspots and IDP hosting states through scaling up integrated lifesaving nutrition preventive and curative services.

The preventive package includes iron-folate supplementation for pregnant and lactating women, maternal, infant and young child feeding nutrition (MIYCN) counseling and support for pregnant and lactating women. The package for under five children includes the provision of micronutrient supplements, Growth Monitoring and Promotion, as well as deworming. Overall, 1.4 million pregnant and lactating women, and over 4.9 million under five will be targeted with the preventive package. Additionally, UNICEF will support the provision of cash transfers to 150,000 of the poorest pregnant women and caregivers of children under-two to help eliminate the financial barriers that women and children may experience in accessing nutritious diets and essential nutrition services. UNICEF will ensure more focus on IYCF-E interventions as part of emergency preparedness and response, with intensive advocacy and orientations to mobilize humanitarian partners to protect and support infant feeding in the emergency context.

UNICEF will strengthen early detection and referral of children suffering from wasting. The key strategy will be large-scale integrated nutrition campaigns through house-to-house modality to significantly scale up the early identification, referral, and management of acutely malnourished children, in addition to integrating it with other preventive services such as micronutrient supplementation for children and women. Through this, 4.9 million children under five will be targeted with early detection of wasting and referral activities. 

UNICEF will work toward the expansion of the geographical coverage of the treatment programme for severe acute malnutrition through the establishment of fixed and mobile sites to reach the planned target of 539,858 children under five suffering from SAM, representing 75 per cent of children under five with SAM in 2024. As part of this, UNICEF will continue working closely with WFP and WHO to ensure the complementarity and continuum of care among the three levels of management for acute malnutrition program. Different strategies will be implemented including (i) maintaining functionality and expanding coverage of OTPs to deliver lifesaving nutrition services and (ii) supporting mobile clinics to reach displaced, hard-to-reach communities with lifesaving nutrition services, and (iii) Expanding active case finding.  Additionally, UNICEF will support evidence generation through implementing SMART surveys.

•Secure the pipeline of all essential preventive and curative nutrition supplies to prevent and treat children with malnutrition. 
•Expand the partnerships with various stakeholders across the country.   
•Strengthen the health system through efforts to strengthen supply chain management, nutrition information systems, monitoring, frontline nutrition workers payment and capacity building.

------ Support for Syria Emergency for learning after earthquake - RTL	Education Education support for Syria’s children and youth affected by crisis As per HNO 2024, the sector PIN indicates a 4% increase from the previous year for children and teachers in need of education assistance. Access to education remains a challenge for many children, as the numbers of Out of School Children remain high. The main barriers are related to the deteriorating economic situation and the ongoing protracted crisis. Even for children in school, learning spaces continue to be unconducive with overcrowded classrooms, limited number of teachers and limited availability of teaching and learning materials.
UNICEF proposes to provide 3,182,074 children and teachers with education services in areas of severity 3-5. This includes children from preprimary, primary and secondary school-aged girls and boys to enable them to develop foundational numeracy and literacy skills, as well as life and citizenship skills, in order to strengthen child, family and community resilience. Additionally, support to enhance the physical learning spaces as well as provision of psychosocial support for children and teachers. 
UNICEF will contribute to: 
A. Providing equitable access to education 
B. Supporting quality education in protective environment
C. Strengthening education systems 
Access will be promoted through Back-to-Learning Campaigns, Vouchers-for-Education, provision of non-formal education programs, school textbooks and school supplies, support to national exams to enhance access to accredited education as part of a multi-sector approach, rehabilitation of schools (formal and nonformal) and provision of temporary classrooms. Rehabilitation is also needed in lower severity areas, where displaced children and returnees as well as large numbers of host community children reside, to contribute to resilience and social cohesion. 
For school rehabilitation UNICEF coordinates with relevant authorities to identify schools in need. UNICEF conducts an assessment to confirm needs and works through vetted independent contractors to commence rehabilitation, including the improvement of WASH facilities, enhancing accessibility for children with disabilities. This is complemented by the provision of school furniture and supplies.
UNICEF will support the Self-learning program to ensure that OOSC have an opportunity to learn, this includes provision of materials, establishment of learning spaces, provision of supplies and support to teacher training. OCHA unearmarked allocation 2024 Renforcement des capacités de coordination, de gestion de l'information et de plaidoyer humanitaires au Burkina Faso •	Le Burkina Faso est en proie à une crise humanitaire sans précédent. Les mouvements de populations et les violations des droits humains s'intensifient, entraînant une détresse sans précédent pour les civils.

•	En 2023, comme lors des années précédentes, le pays a connu un grand nombre de chocs violents. Les mouvements de populations forcés, qui réduisent l’accès de la population aux services sociaux de base et aux moyens de subsistance, contribuant ainsi à l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, sont les principales conséquences. 

•	Il est probable que la situation politique et sécuritaire au Burkina Faso continue de se détériorer. En effet, plusieurs incidents de sécurité ont provoqué de nouveaux déplacements de population en 2023. Des déplacements forcés de plus en plus nombreux et prolongés. 2 062 534 de personnes se sont déplacées à l’intérieur du pays à la date du 31 mars 2023, selon le CONASUR (soit près de 10% de la population totale du pays). 

•	En 2024, plus de 6,3 millions de personnes au Burkina Faso auront besoin d'assistance humanitaire, dont 3,8 millions seront ciblées. Le bureau de pays d'OCHA au Burkina Faso soutiendra la mise en œuvre des activités prioritaires dans les cinq domaines d'intervention suivants : 

•	Améliorer la coordination des efforts humanitaires, à la fois au niveau stratégique et opérationnel. Cela comprend la coordination civilo-militaire, le suivi de l'accès humanitaire, l'engagement des communautés et la redevabilité envers les personnes touchées.

•	Intensifier les efforts de plaidoyer humanitaire, en particulier pour les personnes déplacées internes et les personnes non déplacées.
•	Assurer la mise en œuvre de la politique humanitaire et des bonnes pratiques, notamment la collaboration entre l'humanitaire, le développement et la consolidation de la paix, tout en respectant la distinction et l'intégrité de l'action humanitaire.
•	Faciliter la collecte et la répartition efficaces des fonds humanitaires.

•	Fournir des informations fiables et à jour pour aider les humanitaires à prendre des décisions éclairées.
2. Besoins, activités et résultats attendus : 
•	Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du plan de réponse humanitaire 2024, l’activité centrale de la coordination sera d’améliorer la réponse à la crise par une meilleure coordination de l’assistance humanitaire afin de préserver des vies et protéger les moyens de subsistance.
•	L’appui au Bureau du Coordonnateur Humanitaire dans la mise en place, la révision et le fonctionnement des structures de coordination au niveau national et régional.
•	L’organisation de réunions de coordination aux niveaux national et régional afin de garantir une réponse humanitaire efficace et dans les délais.
•	L’appui au Bureau du Coordonnateur Humanitaire et à l’Equipe humanitaire Pays dans la mise en œuvre des engagements relatifs au Sommet Humanitaire Mondial (WHS), Grand Bargain et du programme nexus humanitaire – développement-Paix.
•	La production et la diffusion de produits d’information de qualité sur les données et le contexte humanitaire.
•	L’appui à la gestion de sites web au profit de la communauté humanitaire et de leurs partenaires.
•	La coordination du groupe de coordination opérationnelle de la réponse rapide (GCORR).
•	La coordination des activités de transferts monétaires en tant que modalité de la réponse humanitaire globale.
•	La coordination du mécanisme d’Accès Humanitaire, de CMCOORD au niveau national et dans les régions touchées par les conflits.
•	Plaidera auprès des autorités compétentes pour garantir un accès humanitaire aux populations dans le besoin d’assistance et de protection.
•	Continuera de soutenir la vulgarisation des principes humanitaire à travers des activités de sensibilisation.
•	Poursuivra ses activités pour la mobilisation des fonds nécessaires à l’assistance et à la réponse humanitaires.
•	Organisera ou soutiendra des réunions de plaidoyer du coordonnateur humanitaire et du Gouvernement avec les donateurs.

OCHA unearmarked allocation 2024 Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre de son mandat et son rôle auprès des partenaires humanitaires et gouvernementaux au niveau des fonctions coordination, gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant un lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.
Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters, des groupes de travail et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.
Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires, catastrophes naturelles) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet.
OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

Camp Coordination / Management	Helping CBM support rehabilitation services, the provision of assistive devices, referrals, and installation of accessibility services, and promoting inclusion of individuals with disabilities in decision-making in the camps and host community. Mainstreaming disability inclusion in the shelter, settlements, camp coordination and camp management programme cycle. This project solely targets people with disabilities, including individuals with physical, visual, hearing, and psychosocial impairments. Individuals with disabilities will receive assistive devices, home, and shelter modifications, and benefit from accessible service centers in the community.

CBM and CDD’s current project takes place in the same geographical locations as the proposed project locations: camps 8W, 8E, 11, 13, 18, and 19 and Rajapalong, Ratanapalong, and Holdiapalong Unions in the host community. No other agencies provide the same/similar services in the proposed project locations.

Capacity building of Site Management and Site Development:  CBMG and CDD provided technical support to IOM and its implementing partners CARE and DRC on capacity building on inclusive Camp Coordination and Camp Management. The capacity-building support will extend in the proposed six camps. 

Home and community accessibility modifications:  The project will provide assistive devices and home/shelter modifications for 1,000 people with disabilities and will promote service center accessibility in the community. Providing this support will improve health for people living in already difficult conditions, in makeshift shelters, on rough terrain, and with limited healthcare services. Without these services, people with disabilities are unable to participate in their community and are a burden on family members who have become carers. These services will improve their functional abilities and allow for greater independence.     

Accessibility at the public and communal Facilities: To create access to different services for people with different types of disabilities, the project aims to conduct accessibility audits and install accessibility features (e.g., ramps with handrails, accessible WASH facility modifications) in three public offices, two health centers, six primary and secondary schools in the host community, and 12 communal facilities in the Rohingya Camps. 

Assistive Devices: A rehabilitation team will assess the clients to determine the types of assistive devices required. The project then will procure height-adjustable devices (e.g., crutches, walkers, toilet chairs) available in the local market and produce customized assistive devices (e.g., wheelchair, special seat chair, tricycle, prosthetic limbs) at CDD’s workshop and distribute to the clients. The materials of the assistive devices will consider the durability, cultural context, availability in the community, and appropriateness for the terrain. 

Ultimately, this project will facilitate clients' ability to move, see, and communicate, help reduce the risk of secondary complications, and provide require support to clients for overcome environmental barriers in certain situations to better engage in community life. Through the proposed interventions, people with disabilities in the camps and host community will have greater access to humanitarian and social protection services, improved quality of life, better functional independence in their daily regular and productive activities, and increased participation in the community.

Documentation: The project will develop some knowledge management documentation along with a video documentation of the accessibility modifications that will be produced to showcase the work and to be used in training and advocacy to present examples of good practice to other actors, who will improve facilities and services for more people with disabilities across the camps.

The project will be managed within CBMG and CDD’s current Inclusive Rohingya Response Program providing interventions in five camps and three Union Parishad in the host community. CDD’s office in Ukhia will monitor operations.

Alojamiento de Emergencias; Alojamiento de Emergencia para personas desplazadas y en riesgo de desplazamiento forzado, personas retornadas con necesidad de protección, solicitantes de asilo, refugiadas y afectados por desastres naturales en El Salvador ACNUR como líder del Sector Alojamientos de Emergencia en El Salvador, y como agencia humanitaria, implementará este proyecto para contribuir con el acceso a alojamiento de emergencia y la mejora de resiliencia en situaciones de crisis para personas afectadas por desplazamiento forzado y en riesgo de desplazamiento, personas retornadas con necesidad de protección, personas solicitantes de asilo y refugiadas, que hayan sido afectadas por efectos del cambio climático y/o desastres naturales.

El proyecto de ACNUR El Salvador para el HRP 2024 se alinea a los objetivos del Sector Alojamiento de Emergencias en el Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria, en el cual se proponen acciones para cubrir la necesidad de alojamientos transitorios dignos y seguros. El proyecto también se encuentra alineado con las prioridades nacionales y contribuye al Plan de Acción Nacional del Marco Integral Regional para la Protección y Soluciones (MIRPS). ACNUR brindará orientación y apoyo técnico a instituciones y partes interesadas para la inclusión de personas en situación de desplazamiento. Junto con contrapartes nacionales, ACNUR desarrollará procesos de capacitación y fortalecimiento técnico a instituciones estatales, actores humanitarios y actores comunitarios. 

Para el acceso a alojamiento de familias que no tienen donde pernoctar, se prevén modalidades transitorias como carpas, módulos temporales de vivienda, kits de materiales de construcción y kits de herramientas. En el caso de familias cuyas viviendas han sufrido afectación moderada, el proyecto prevé prestar apoyo bajo la modalidad de subsidios tanto para alquiler como para reparación de vivienda.

A su vez, el proyecto incluye la entrega de insumos no alimenticios de apoyo complementario a través de kits domésticos que pueden incluir colchonetas, lámparas, frazadas, menajes de cocina, mosquiteros, ropa, instrumentos de limpieza, entre otros, con el objeto de mitigar las carencias domésticas de las personas y/o comunidades que hayan sido forzadas a desplazarse a causa de un evento climático o un desastre natural. 

Sabiendo que las afectaciones en materia de alojamiento son diferenciadas según el edad, género y diversidad, la respuesta humanitaria que se implemente a través del proyecto debe considerar dichas necesidades diferenciadas, para tal efecto se mantendrá el enfoque de centralidad de protección y acción sin daño.

En cuanto a cobertura geográfica, el proyecto se implementará en todos los departamentos del país donde exista necesidad por las causas establecidas. Sin embargo, las acciones se enfocarán prioritariamente en los departamentos cuya necesidad de alojamiento fue expuesta como de alta severidad en el análisis del HNO 2023, a saber: Ahuachapán, Chalatenango, Cuscatlán, La Libertad, La Paz, La Unión, Morazán, Sonsonate y Usulután.

El Salvador	El Salvador Plan de Respuesta Humanitario 2024	- Atención integral de protección a la niñez en desplazamiento o en riesgo de desplazamiento en El Salvador ACNUR trabajará en el fortalecimiento del sistema Nacional de Protección de la Primera Infancia, Niñez y Adolescencia de El Salvador. La alianza con la autoridad nacional de protección de la niñez CONAPINA, y las unidades dedicadas de la Procuraduría General de la República (PGR) y la Procuraduría para la Defensa de los Derechos Humanos (PDDH), del Ministerio de Educación, Ciencia y Tecnología (MINEDUCYT), sustentarán y reforzarán acciones para la protección de la niñez desplazada por la fuerza.

ACNUR apoyará a las instituciones con recursos humanos para poder atender a niños, niñas y adolescentes que se encuentran desplazados o en riesgo de desplazamiento, buscando protección como refugiados y retornados con necesidades de protección.  Específicamente, ACNUR apoyará con profesionales de psicología que brindarán atención en los puntos de recepción, aeropuertos y fronteras; además de en comunidades donde había alto riesgo de violencia de pandillas en las que se implementarán espacios amigables para niños, niñas y adolescentes. Además, ACNUR fortalecerá capacidades y apoyará la adecuación de espacios para buscar soluciones para niños, niñas y adolescentes en situación de desplazamiento forzado.

ACNUR cooperará en apoyo a las comunidades históricamente afectadas por la violencia donde el Gobierno impulsará las respuestas a la niñez desplazada o en riesgo que requieren servicios básicos como educación y salud mental. ACNUR dará prioridad al trabajo en cinco comunidades para dar seguimiento a la situación de niñas, niños y adolescentes en mayor riesgo, trabajando con socios y el Gobierno en la identificación de casos y necesidades, y en la provisión de respuestas de protección.

Teniendo en cuenta los avances actuales en el entorno de seguridad, ACNUR impulsará soluciones a través de intervenciones dirigidas a la participación, el retorno a la educación y el bienestar de los niños, niñas y adolescentes. ACNUR adaptará espacios colectivos en cinco comunidades históricamente bajo control de pandillas como espacios amigables de estudio. Estas instalaciones contarán con una persona profesional en psicología y una persona promotora educativa. Trabajando juntos, ayudarán a los niños a recuperar las habilidades sociales y la autoestima afectadas por la violencia y las limitaciones de movilidad causadas por fronteras invisibles. Se guiará a niños, niñas y adolescentes en un proceso de reflexión y resiliencia. La persona promotora brindará apoyo para el retorno al sistema educativo en caso de deserción en coordinación con el Ministerio de Educación, Ciencia y Tecnología.

Dada la numerosa identificación de casos de niños, niñas y adolescentes en mayor riesgo, ACNUR creará un equipo especializado y dedicado a su gestión. La gestión y seguimiento de los casos incluirá el análisis y determinación del interés superior a la luz de sus necesidades de protección y posibles soluciones, incluido el reasentamiento.

Guatemala Plan de Respuesta Humanitario 2024 Proteccion integral a personas en situacion de movilidad humana en Guatemala A lo largo de 2022 e inicios de 2023, se ha notado un incremento en los impactos humanitarios y de necesidades de protección que dejan las diferentes crisis que afectan al país. Por un lado, la situación de violencia e inseguridad sigue impactando a miles de personas, evidenciado en el indicador de muertes violentas el cual registró un incremento de 6,7 por ciento con respecto al año anterior, llegando a una tasa de 17.3 por cada 100 mil habitantes, una de las más altas en Centro América. Los principales delitos denunciados son extorsión, hurto, robo, homicidios, lesiones, violencia sexual a NNA y mujeres adultas. A pesar de la mejora en ciertos indicadores de seguridad en el país, el alcance, control y violencia ejercida por grupos de delincuencia organizada continúa planteando serios desafíos a la protección de la población. Las pandillas poseen un amplio control en el país y están vinculadas a delitos violentos, extorsión, reclutamiento forzado y actividades relacionadas con el tráfico de drogas. Adicionalmente, las elecciones presidenciales y una transición política alterada, ha generado que los lideres indígenas se movilicen en protestas, generando varios bloqueos paralizando las principales rutas del país.  
Adicionalmente, las consecuencias del cambio climático en el área del corredor seco están provocando una crisis de inseguridad alimentaria, con cerca de 4.9 millones de personas afectadas, según el análisis del CIF (Clasificación Integrada en Fases) para el periodo junio/septiembre 2022; lo que representa un 25% del total de la población. Estas afectaciones incrementan situaciones de desigualdad, pobreza y de violencia, incluida la violencia basada en género (VBG) y vulneración de los derechos de los niños, niñas y adolescentes, así como a grupos especialmente marginalizados como la población LGBTIQ+, indígena, en condición de discapacidad, generando desplazamiento al interior del país y hacia los países del norte del continente. 

Se estima, por lo tanto, que hay más de 2.9 millones de personas con necesidades de protección en Guatemala. Aproximadamente 41% de las personas con necesidades son mujeres adultas y un 40% NNA. Hasta diciembre de 2024, el clúster de protección proyecta cubrir las necesidades de al menos 810.000 personas. 

A esto se suma, que durante 2023 se generó un aumento del número de personas en movilidad humana (personas solicitantes de la condición de refugiado y refugiados, retornadas, desplazadas y migrantes en tránsito) que atraviesan el país. Según el Servicio Nacional de Migración de Panamá más de 400,000 personas habían cruzado el Darién en septiembre 2023, con la cifra más alta registrada en agosto 2023 de 82,000 personas. Los anuncios y cambios en la política migratoria regional de los EE. UU, han generado incertidumbre frente al futuro inmediato de las personas en Movilidad Humana y reflejan los desafíos institucionales que tiene el país para asegurar una respuesta adecuada y acceso a medidas de protección frente a la agudización de las necesidades humanitarias y recrudecimiento de las condiciones en la ruta (extorsiones, robos, violencia sexual).  

ACNUR Guatemala continuará trabajando con el gobierno, la sociedad civil y las comunidades para fortalecer el espacio de protección para refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, personas en movimientos mixtos y guatemaltecos con necesidades de protección; mediante la consolidación de iniciativas emprendidas en años anteriores. Para lograr nuestros objetivos de una manera más eficiente, nuestro enfoque basado en áreas contempla intervenciones priorizadas en comunidades con alta presencia de personas a las que servimos, en todas las áreas de responsabilidad. 

ACNUR se compromete a fortalecer las capacidades de las instituciones estatales (incluyendo a las municipalidades) para proporcionar respuestas de prevención y protección para las personas a las que servimos para garantizar la sostenibilidad de las intervenciones.

Disasters Emergency Committee DEC Syria  Appeal Emergency humanitarian food aids response and livelihood support to empower resilience of Vulnerable communities in NW- Syria IR Syria's initiative aims to address critical food security needs in northern Syria, particularly among vulnerable populations affected by conflict and displacement. By providing essential food items, agricultural support, and livelihood assistance, the project seeks to mitigate escalating rates of malnutrition and food insecurity.


Key activities of the project include:

1. Provision of Daily Bread Bags:
Each day, 10,000 households receive bread bags weighing 750g. These are distributed to every 3 individuals in the family, with larger families receiving additional bags. Distribution occurs on 26 days per month.

2.Monthly Food Parcel Distribution:
10,000 households receive monthly food parcels.
The parcels contains:
- Rice, 1 kg pack
- Bulgur, 1 kg pack
- Red lentils, 1 kg pack
- Sugar, 1 kg pack
- IODIZED SALT, 1 kg pack
- Sunflower Cooking Oil, 1 Litre PET bottle
- Tomato Paste, 830 grams Tin
- Spaghetti, 400 grams
- Bottles of Margarine (Vegetable ghee), 750g
- Green lentils, 1 kg pack


3.Supply of Canned Meat and Adahi Meat:
27,378 households benefit from the supply of canned meat and Adahi meat.


4.Distribution of Agricultural Kits:
3,000 households receive agricultural kits tailored to support wheat cultivation, olive trees, and summer vegetables cultivation.


5.Livestock Income Generation Support:
Veterinary services and support for livestock income generation are provided to 5,000 households.


The agricultural component includes inputs tailored for three types of crops:

1.Wheat Cultivation: Inputs include wheat seed, urea fertilizers, herbicide, insecticide, foliar fertilizer, and harvest bags, sufficient for cultivating 10,000 m2 of wheat.


2.Olive Trees: Inputs include compound fertilizers NPK, insecticide, foliar fertilizer, and harvest bags.


3.Summer Vegetables Cultivation: Inputs include urea fertilizers, balanced fertilizer NPK, high phosphorus, high potash, foliar fertilizers (Boron and Amino acids), plastic packaging bags, and an agriculture voucher for redeeming pesticides and fungicides.

Needs:
Food insecurity in Syria is exacerbated by economic deterioration and prolonged conflict, necessitating urgent humanitarian support.

The project will execute a comprehensive response strategy in coordination with local stakeholders and humanitarian partners. Targeted assessments and community engagement will ensure effective implementation and mitigate potential tensions.

Dedicated monitoring staff oversee bread preparation, loading, distribution, and household delivery. Daily workers at bakeries provide reports on baking activities and bread quality. Additionally, daily monitoring in communities gathers feedback for prompt issue resolution.

The planned interventions will benefit 4,602085 females, 4,421,611 males and 3,609,478 children of which 1,804,769 girls (less than 18 year of age), and 1,804,769 boys. (less than 18 year of age). The project will also support 902,370 elderly (above 60) and 451,185 male and female people with disabilities. The proposed interventions are based on the basic and specific needs of the beneficiaries considering the factors of age and gender. FAO will coordinate with sector partners, government, and UN agencies to get actual information on numbers and locations of the people with disabilities to support them with suitable livelihoods interventions.

The project interventions under FSL SO1 (Improve the food security status of assessed severely food insecure people through emergency live-saving agriculture, livestock, emergency livelihood and social protection support through cash and in-kind transfers for 8,250,000 person (1,650,000 households). And 773,696 persons (154,739 households) under FSL SO2 (Strengthen affected food insecure households through live-sustaining and restoring food, agriculture, and livelihoods) to ensure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food from their own production to meet their family needs and sell the surplus in the local markets to generate income and avail diversified foods for others at their locations and at a reasonable price. During that process they will receive extension support to intensify their production and build their resilience to overcome natural or manmade risks and hazards. They will be encouraged to protect their natural resources to sustain their livelihoods base.
The FAO will collect information, conduct assessments, studies to better inform the decisions on the implementation of this project. Crop and Food Supply Assessment Mission (CFSAM) will be conducted during 2024/ 2025 to enhance the country planning and ensure that all Sudanese are food secure otherwise suitable interventions will be developed.
FAO will support coordination with FSL sector partners and harmonises the response to food chain threats including animal and plant pests specially locust and birds; in addition, communities will be involved in protecting and maintaining their productive assets through awareness raising. Accountability to affected populations and environmental concerns will be mainstreamed into the proposed activities, also risk to GBV will be taken into consideration and application of the PSEA measures will be applied in collaboration with sister UN agencies.

Syria, Arab Republic of: Education Education support for Syria’s children and youth affected by crisis As per HNO 2024, the sector PIN indicates a 4% increase from the previous year for children and teachers in need of education assistance. Access to education remains a challenge for many children, as the numbers of Out of School Children remain high. The main barriers are related to the deteriorating economic situation and the ongoing protracted crisis. Even for children in school, learning spaces continue to be unconducive with overcrowded classrooms, limited number of teachers and limited availability of teaching and learning materials.
UNICEF proposes to provide 3,182,074 children and teachers with education services in areas of severity 3-5. This includes children from preprimary, primary and secondary school-aged girls and boys to enable them to develop foundational numeracy and literacy skills, as well as life and citizenship skills, in order to strengthen child, family and community resilience. Additionally, support to enhance the physical learning spaces as well as provision of psychosocial support for children and teachers. 
UNICEF will contribute to: 
A. Providing equitable access to education 
B. Supporting quality education in protective environment
C. Strengthening education systems 
Access will be promoted through Back-to-Learning Campaigns, Vouchers-for-Education, provision of non-formal education programs, school textbooks and school supplies, support to national exams to enhance access to accredited education as part of a multi-sector approach, rehabilitation of schools (formal and nonformal) and provision of temporary classrooms. Rehabilitation is also needed in lower severity areas, where displaced children and returnees as well as large numbers of host community children reside, to contribute to resilience and social cohesion. 
For school rehabilitation UNICEF coordinates with relevant authorities to identify schools in need. UNICEF conducts an assessment to confirm needs and works through vetted independent contractors to commence rehabilitation, including the improvement of WASH facilities, enhancing accessibility for children with disabilities. This is complemented by the provision of school furniture and supplies.
UNICEF will support the Self-learning program to ensure that OOSC have an opportunity to learn, this includes provision of materials, establishment of learning spaces, provision of supplies and support to teacher training. To improve the quality of education services, UNICEF will ensure schools are child-friendly, with teachers trained in child-centered pedagogy, and where children develop academic, cognitive, life and psychosocial skills that empower them to engage, relate, cope and contribute to community and family life. Due to the large number of children at different learning levels within grades, children will be provided with remedial learning support. To support system resilience, UNICEF will establish Parent Teacher Associations that cooperate with Headmasters, and train education staff on monitoring schools, staff performance and children’s learning. UNICEF monitors ongoing activities through staff and implementing partner visits, Third Partner Monitoring and through established feedback mechanisms. In NWS, TPMs provide on-site verification and beneficiary interviews. 
PROTECTION RISK ANALYSIS
1. Attack on education and safety of children on their way to school 2.Increased risks of GBV if latrines are not separated or there are no locks on the doors and light. 3.Increased risk of host-community tension due to assistance packages given to IDPs, 4. Risk of sexual exploitation by Teacher education personnel, NGO staff (risk of harassment) of boys and girls 5. Teachers or other education personnel participate in physical punishment or bullying of students Or Students participate in bullying of students
PSEA policy will be respected as per UNICEF rules and mandate.
RISKS, ASSUMPTIONS AND MITIGATION MEASURES Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation Children working with contractors Zero tolerance

Access to education remains a challenge for many children, as the numbers of Out of School Children remain high. The main barriers are related to the deteriorating economic situation and the ongoing protracted crisis. Even for children in school, learning spaces continue to be unconducive with overcrowded classrooms, limited number of teachers and limited availability of teaching and learning materials.
UNICEF proposes to provide 3,182,074 children and teachers with education services in areas of severity 3-5. This includes children from preprimary, primary and secondary school-aged girls and boys to enable them to develop foundational numeracy and literacy skills, as well as life and citizenship skills, in order to strengthen child, family and community resilience. Additionally, support to enhance the physical learning spaces as well as provision of psychosocial support for children and teachers. 
UNICEF will contribute to: 
A. Providing equitable access to education 
B. Supporting quality education in protective environment
C. Strengthening education systems 
Access will be promoted through Back-to-Learning Campaigns, Vouchers-for-Education, provision of non-formal education programs, school textbooks and school supplies, support to national exams to enhance access to accredited education as part of a multi-sector approach, rehabilitation of schools (formal and nonformal) and provision of temporary classrooms. Rehabilitation is also needed in lower severity areas, where displaced children and returnees as well as large numbers of host community children reside, to contribute to resilience and social cohesion. 
For school rehabilitation UNICEF coordinates with relevant authorities to identify schools in need. UNICEF conducts an assessment to confirm needs and works through vetted independent contractors to commence rehabilitation, including the improvement of WASH facilities, enhancing accessibility for children with disabilities. This is complemented by the provision of school furniture and supplies.
UNICEF will support the Self-learning program to ensure that OOSC have an opportunity to learn, this includes provision of materials, establishment of learning spaces, provision of supplies and support to teacher training. To improve the quality of education services, UNICEF will ensure schools are child-friendly, with teachers trained in child-centered pedagogy, and where children develop academic, cognitive, life and psychosocial skills that empower them to engage, relate, cope and contribute to community and family life. Due to the large number of children at different learning levels within grades, children will be provided with remedial learning support. To support system resilience, UNICEF will establish Parent Teacher Associations that cooperate with Headmasters, and train education staff on monitoring schools, staff performance and children’s learning. UNICEF monitors ongoing activities through staff and implementing partner visits, Third Partner Monitoring and through established feedback mechanisms. In NWS, TPMs provide on-site verification and beneficiary interviews.

1. Attack on education and safety of children on their way to school 2.Increased risks of GBV if latrines are not separated or there are no locks on the doors and light. 3.Increased risk of host-community tension due to assistance packages given to IDPs, 4. Risk of sexual exploitation by Teacher education personnel, NGO staff (risk of harassment) of boys and girls 5. Teachers or other education personnel participate in physical punishment or bullying of students Or Students participate in bullying of students
PSEA policy will be respected as per UNICEF rules and mandate.

IOM’s plan for Ukraine targets 1,5 million people to provide critically needed assistance to internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and other affected populations. Thematic areas included are for example support for basic needs, including food and multi-purpose cash assistance, health and psychosocial health support, settlements, protection, WASH and socioeconomic inclusion.

Interventions in Ukraine are in line with and complementary to the Ukraine Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2024, which has a strong focus on gender equality. IOMs response focuses on vulnerable groups including persons with disabilities, children, as well as survivors of gender-based violence (GBV) and human trafficking.

UNHCR's appeal is part of the overarching 2024 Humanitarian Response Plan for Ukraine coordinated by OCHA, which has a strong focus on gender equality (disaggregated data, thorough gender analysis and a separate GBV cluster. The education and health clusters also explicitly point out the promotion of gender equality in their activities. Disability status is disaggregated in the response under all clusters and the inclusion of people with disabilities is integrated across project activities.
