----- USAID/BHA UNICEF: Lifesaving nutrition preventive and curative interventions targeting most vulnerable population across Sudan The malnutrition situation in Sudan remains dire with an expected increase in the number of children with acute malnutrition due to the deteriorating nutrition determinants as result of the ongoing catastrophic humanitarian crisis. The nutrition sector estimates that 4.7 million children under five and pregnant and lactating women are acutely malnourished and in need humanitarian assistance in 2024.

Through this project, UNICEF aims to (1) increase equitable access to an integrated lifesaving and preventive nutrition services focusing more on the “1000- day window”- as a critical opportunity to prevent child wasting and stunting among under five children, (2) improve early detection of acute malnutrition (3) improve access to quality lifesaving nutrition services to treat severe acute malnutrition among under-five children. UNICEF will target all states in the country with more focus on hotspots and IDP hosting states through scaling up integrated lifesaving nutrition preventive and curative services.

The preventive package includes iron-folate supplementation for pregnant and lactating women, maternal, infant and young child feeding nutrition (MIYCN) counseling and support for pregnant and lactating women. The package for under five children includes the provision of micronutrient supplements, Growth Monitoring and Promotion, as well as deworming. Overall, 1.4 million pregnant and lactating women, and over 4.9 million under five will be targeted with the preventive package. Additionally, UNICEF will support the provision of cash transfers to 150,000 of the poorest pregnant women and caregivers of children under-two to help eliminate the financial barriers that women and children may experience in accessing nutritious diets and essential nutrition services. UNICEF will ensure more focus on IYCF-E interventions as part of emergency preparedness and response, with intensive advocacy and orientations to mobilize humanitarian partners to protect and support infant feeding in the emergency context.

UNICEF will strengthen early detection and referral of children suffering from wasting. The key strategy will be large-scale integrated nutrition campaigns through house-to-house modality to significantly scale up the early identification, referral, and management of acutely malnourished children, in addition to integrating it with other preventive services such as micronutrient supplementation for children and women. Through this, 4.9 million children under five will be targeted with early detection of wasting and referral activities. 

UNICEF will work toward the expansion of the geographical coverage of the treatment programme for severe acute malnutrition through the establishment of fixed and mobile sites to reach the planned target of 539,858 children under five suffering from SAM, representing 75 per cent of children under five with SAM in 2024. As part of this, UNICEF will continue working closely with WFP and WHO to ensure the complementarity and continuum of care among the three levels of management for acute malnutrition program. Different strategies will be implemented including (i) maintaining functionality and expanding coverage of OTPs to deliver lifesaving nutrition services and (ii) supporting mobile clinics to reach displaced, hard-to-reach communities with lifesaving nutrition services, and (iii) Expanding active case finding.  Additionally, UNICEF will support evidence generation through implementing SMART surveys.  

To support the implementation of integrated preventive and curative nutrition services UNICEF will:
•Secure the pipeline of all essential preventive and curative nutrition supplies to prevent and treat children with malnutrition. 
•Expand the partnerships with various stakeholders across the country.   
•Strengthen the health system through efforts to strengthen supply chain management, nutrition information systems, monitoring, frontline nutrition workers payment and capacity building.

Le présent projet poursuit comme objectif d’atteindre 10 000 ménages soit 70 000 personnes à travers tout le Niger prioritairement dans les régions de Zinder, Diffa, Maradi et Tahoua. En coordination avec le MAH/GC et la Direction Générale de la Protection Civile (DGPC), l’OIM mettra à disposition 10 000 kits abris et 10 000 kits Biens non-alimentaires qui seront distribués aux ménages sinistrés. En plus des kits, l’OIM couvrira les coûts liés à la logistique et à la distribution des kits. Ce projet ne couvrira pas une zone ou région donnée mais permettra d’intervenir là où les besoins se présentent et aussi de pouvoir compléter les activités des autres acteurs en cas de besoin en tant que prestataire de dernier recours pour la réponse humanitaire en abri d'urgence et BNA. L’OIM en tant que Co-Lead du Groupe de Travail Abri et Bien non-alimentaire (GTABNA) avec le MAH/GC s'assurera que les activités sont menées en étroite coordination avec les autres partenaires humanitaires membres du GTABNA pour la réponse en abri et Biens non-alimentaires pour les ménages sinistrés des inondations au Niger. Conformément à la logique de la stratégie du Secteur abris/BNA et en fonction de la faisabilité, les interventions pourront se faire en transferts monétaires conditionnels. Cela réduirait considérablement les coûts logistiques qui sont très élevés en période hivernale à cause du mauvais état des routes mais aussi et permettrait aussi de résoudre en partie le problème d’accès lié à l'insécurité qui souvent retarde les interventions. Enfin, la mise en œuvre du présent projet fera l’objet d’un suivi régulier de la qualité des interventions réalisées mais aussi de l’implication des bénéficiaires et autorités locales. Pour cela, les feedbacks de la communauté cible seront collectés à travers des évaluations post-distribution et des séances de discussion de groupe séparées par genre et âge avant et après l'assistance. Aussi, en tant qu’acteur humanitaire, l'OIM et ses partenaires de mise en œuvre s’assureront que ses actions n’induisent aucune tension ou problème dans la zone et n’exposent pas les bénéficiaires. A cet effet la phase d'évaluation de besoins sera réalisée de commun accord avec les populations dans les communes ciblées, les sessions d'information sur le projet seront organisées à l'attention de communauté bénéficiaires, le mecanisme de ciblage de bénéficiaires sera réalisé en étroite collabation avec les autorités au niveau local (do no harm). Une collaboration étroite faite avec les acteurs de protection pour un suivi de près de toutes questions de protection et de LTB. Le cout total du projet sera de 6.090.000 USD.

-- USA / BPRM UNICEF: Lifesaving nutrition preventive and curative interventions targeting most vulnerable population across Sudan The malnutrition situation in Sudan remains dire with an expected increase in the number of children with acute malnutrition due to the deteriorating nutrition determinants as result of the ongoing catastrophic humanitarian crisis. The nutrition sector estimates that 4.7 million children under five and pregnant and lactating women are acutely malnourished and in need humanitarian assistance in 2024.

Through this project, UNICEF aims to (1) increase equitable access to an integrated lifesaving and preventive nutrition services focusing more on the “1000- day window”- as a critical opportunity to prevent child wasting and stunting among under five children, (2) improve early detection of acute malnutrition (3) improve access to quality lifesaving nutrition services to treat severe acute malnutrition among under-five children. UNICEF will target all states in the country with more focus on hotspots and IDP hosting states through scaling up integrated lifesaving nutrition preventive and curative services.

The preventive package includes iron-folate supplementation for pregnant and lactating women, maternal, infant and young child feeding nutrition (MIYCN) counseling and support for pregnant and lactating women. The package for under five children includes the provision of micronutrient supplements, Growth Monitoring and Promotion, as well as deworming. Overall, 1.4 million pregnant and lactating women, and over 4.9 million under five will be targeted with the preventive package. Additionally, UNICEF will support the provision of cash transfers to 150,000 of the poorest pregnant women and caregivers of children under-two to help eliminate the financial barriers that women and children may experience in accessing nutritious diets and essential nutrition services. UNICEF will ensure more focus on IYCF-E interventions as part of emergency preparedness and response, with intensive advocacy and orientations to mobilize humanitarian partners to protect and support infant feeding in the emergency context.

UNICEF will strengthen early detection and referral of children suffering from wasting. The key strategy will be large-scale integrated nutrition campaigns through house-to-house modality to significantly scale up the early identification, referral, and management of acutely malnourished children, in addition to integrating it with other preventive services such as micronutrient supplementation for children and women. Through this, 4.9 million children under five will be targeted with early detection of wasting and referral activities. 

UNICEF will work toward the expansion of the geographical coverage of the treatment programme for severe acute malnutrition through the establishment of fixed and mobile sites to reach the planned target of 539,858 children under five suffering from SAM, representing 75 per cent of children under five with SAM in 2024. As part of this, UNICEF will continue working closely with WFP and WHO to ensure the complementarity and continuum of care among the three levels of management for acute malnutrition program. Different strategies will be implemented including (i) maintaining functionality and expanding coverage of OTPs to deliver lifesaving nutrition services and (ii) supporting mobile clinics to reach displaced, hard-to-reach communities with lifesaving nutrition services, and (iii) Expanding active case finding.  Additionally, UNICEF will support evidence generation through implementing SMART surveys.  

To support the implementation of integrated preventive and curative nutrition services UNICEF will:
•Secure the pipeline of all essential preventive and curative nutrition supplies to prevent and treat children with malnutrition. 
•Expand the partnerships with various stakeholders across the country.   
•Strengthen the health system through efforts to strengthen supply chain management, nutrition information systems, monitoring, frontline nutrition workers payment and capacity building.

United States (USAID-BHA) Contribution to OCHA 2024 Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre de son mandat et son rôle auprès des partenaires humanitaires et gouvernementaux au niveau des fonctions coordination, gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant un lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.
Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters, des groupes de travail et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.
Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires, catastrophes naturelles) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet.
OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

El Salvador:Humanitarian assistance to children and youths	Child Protection Protección de niñez y adolescencia vulnerable en situación de movilidad y afectada por la sequía El Salvador enfrenta grandes retos asociados a la niñez y adolescencia en contexto de movilidad (desplazamiento forzado, flujos de salida del país, retornos, migrantes en tránsito hacia el norte del continente, refugiados y solicitantes de asilo). 
Los factores que subyacen a la movilidad humana en El Salvador son diversos y complejos e incluyen, entre otros: desigualdad social, brechas de acceso a servicios básicos, violencia en sus diversas formas y ámbitos, incluida la violencia basada en género (VBG), limitado acceso a empleo formal y oportunidades económicas, y pretensiones de reunificación familiar. 
Los desastres naturales y de origen humano, exacerbados por el cambio climático, agravan los factores subyacentes a la movilidad. 
La violencia basada en género también motiva a las niñas, adolescentes y mujeres a huir y recurrir al desplazamiento interno y a la migración en condición irregular como medidas de afrontamiento, que ponen en riesgo su vida y seguridad en tránsito y destino. 
Más de 70,000 niños y niñas viven en el país sin uno o ambos padres como resultado de la migración.
La ubicación de El Salvador en la ruta migratoria en el norte de Centroamérica, su economía dolarizada y una percepción de seguridad son factores que inciden en el incremento de personas en movimientos mixtos que atraviesan el país. 
La violencia generalizada que sufren los niños, niñas y adolescentes en sus hogares, comunidades o escuelas, siguen siendo un detonante para el desplazamiento y la migración. La violencia tiene impactos diferenciados; si bien los homicidios disminuyeron en los últimos cinco años, seis de cada diez víctimas son niños y hombres jóvenes (entre 13 y 35 años), y la violencia sexual afecta desproporcionadamente a niñas y mujeres jóvenes.
La Organización Meteorológica Mundial (OMM) declaró en julio de 2023 que se habían dado las condiciones para la aparición del fenómeno de El Niño.  También declaró que los efectos serían más notables a partir del segundo semestre de 2023, con una duración de 9 a 12 meses. Para la región centroamericana, la OMM informa que el fenómeno suele causar sequías severas.  
Se prevé que la sequía tenga graves repercusiones en los medios de subsistencia y la seguridad alimentaria de los hogares de las zonas más afectadas. Estos impactos pueden llevar a las personas a adoptar estrategias negativas para hacer frente a la situación, como el trabajo infantil, la discriminación en el reparto de alimentos dentro de la familia y el matrimonio precoz, entre otras. 
Con el presente proyecto, UNICEF tiene como objetivo brindar una respuesta humanitaria para que niñas, niños y adolescentes en contexto de movilidad o afectados por sequía, que están expuestos a violencia, abuso o explotación, incluyendo a población LGBTIQ+ o con discapacidad, accedan a servicios especializados e integrales de protección de la infancia. Ello orientado al fortalecimiento de su resiliencia, la reintegración en sus comunidades y la plena restitución de sus derechos. 
Las niñas, niños y adolescentes con necesidades de protección beneficiarios recibirán protección a través de albergues o acceso a espacios seguros, apoyo psicosocial y atención a la salud mental, asistencia legal y respuesta a otras necesidades humanitarias (asistencia humanitaria); junto con el desarrollo de habilidades para la vida para ellas y ellos, así como para las madres, padres o personas cuidadoras, fortaleciendo los lazos familiares. Para ello, se apoyarán servicios especializados de protección adecuados a la edad, género y diversidad, líneas de ayuda  mecanismos de denuncia, espacios amigables de apoyo psicosocial, mecanismos de referencia y gestión de casos, promoviendo entornos protectores a nivel familiar y comunitario. El proyecto se implementará bajo un enfoque inclusivo de género y discapacidad, promoviendo la continuidad de los servicios que puedan ser afectados.

Projet de Sécurisation des Ressources des Ménages déplacés, réfugiés et communautés hôtes dans la commune de chétimari, Région de Diffa (PSRM)
Project Start Date: 2024-08-01 - Project End Date: 2025-07-31
Project Code: CBPF-NER-24-R-NGO-32687
Emergency Type: Conflict - Displacement Projet de Sécurisation des Ressources des Ménages vulnérables  dans la commune de Chetimarie /Région de Diffa La Région de Diffa est une zone à vocation agro pastorale par excellence. Elle dispose d’énormes potentialités afin d’assurer sa propre souveraineté alimentaire (terres irrigables, un important capital bétail, ressources en eau, main d’œuvre, etc.). 
 Les communautés ont essentiellement des sources de revenus fondés sur l’agriculture de subsistance. Cependant, depuis la sécheresse de 2012 qui a touché les pays du sahel, les communautés de la zone d’intervention n’ont pas véritablement pu reconstituer leur potentiel de survie. Les campagnes hivernales qui ont suivi n’ont pas apporté de réponses efficaces au problème de retard de croissance des enfants de moins de 5 ans. Les pratiques culturales ne répondent pas convenablement aux attentes des ménages vulnérables. Ces derniers sont en effet obligés de faire le salariat agricole  pendant la période de culture pour pourvoir subvenir aux besoins alimentaires de leurs ménages au lieu de travailler dans leur propre champs. De toutes les façons, cette agriculture de subsistance sur laquelle repose l’espoir de tous les ménages reste le plus souvent confrontés aux caprices et défis du climat. Il faut souligner que les actions que compte impulser le projet  mettent l’accent sur des activités plus résilientes. En effet, les actions du projet tablent également sur la durabilité en faisant la promotion des activités qui renforcent les stratégies d’adaptation des ménages notamment l’introduction du moringa qui est déterminante dans la lutte contre les conséquences de la malnutrition et la lutte contre la paupérisation des ménages. Le choix du groupe cible reste sans doute motivé par le fait que les femmes et les enfants sont les plus touchés par les situations couplées de crises d'insécurités et alimentaires que connaissent les département  presque chaque année. Les attaques des groupes armées et la réduction des moyens d’existence poussent les hommes à partir en exode vers la Libye et l’extrême Est du Nigeria en laissant derrière eux femmes et enfants dans des besoins énormes. Les femmes n’ont pas assez de pouvoirs économiques pour supporter la charge du ménage. Les actions du projet notamment pour les transferts de Cash ,CFW et les AGR visent à apporter un soutien substantiel aux femmes et de facto aux enfants de moins de 5 ans de ces ménages vulnérables. Le soutien en semences de qualité va aider également le ménage dans son ensemble à mieux renforcer sa stratégie d’adaptation. L’introduction de la culture de moringa et les  Jardins Potagers du Ménage touchent directement les femmes car leurs permettant de produire de la feuille de moringa qui a une valeur nutritive démontrée par les scientifiques mais également produire des légumes avec les Key Hole Garden pour soutenir l’alimentation de tout le ménage. le projet  prévoit également la culture de case pour aider les ménages vulnérables à produire du gombo pour renforcer l’économie du ménage.
Au vue de tout ce qui précède que le projet qui concerne 15 000 participants, vise à contribuer à la réduction de l’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle des populations les plus vulnérables dans le département de Chétimari, Région de Diffa. Plus spécifiquement, il vise à augmenter la production alimentaire et les revenus des ménages vulnérables et à améliorer leur résilience face aux  changements climatiques.

Emergency Type: Climate / natural disaster - Flood Beyond Zero Maternal and Child Deaths: Provision of Lifesaving Primary Healthcare and Reproductive Health Services to Persons Most in Need in Leer, Mayendit, Koch, Panyijiar and Pariang Counties Through Primary Health Care Units and Mobile Clinics According to the Health Cluster Response Plan for 2024, 8.9 million South Sudanese are in need of Humanitarian Aid, with 6.3 million among them requiring essential lifesaving healthcare services. Insecurity, long distances, limited healthcare supplies, inaccessibility of healthcare facilities and inadequate healthcare workers have disproportionately affected access to healthcare, especially among women and children. Unity State counties such as Leer, Koch, Mayendit, Panyijiar and Pariang have been adversely affected by these emergencies and currently lie in severity 4. 

In Leer, Mayendit, Koch, Panyijiar and Pariang, an estimated 405,576 persons are in need of emergency life saving healthcare. The rates of immunization are extremely low, malaria cases remain high, while acute watery and acute bloody diarrhea are endemic in multiple counties. Thousands of hepatitis cases have been reported due to a dire WASH situation, while infectious diseases such as COVID-19 continue spreading, with significant portions of the population depending on traditional healers as a coping mechanism.  
The proposed project shall extend primary health care and reproductive health services to vulnerable persons, including IDPs, returnees and host populations in Leer, Mayendit, Koch, Panyijiar and Pariang. 

This project is in line with the health cluster objectives and the 2024 Humanitarian Response Plan which seek to:
1. Improve equitable access to life-saving essential comprehensive quality health care services including maternal, child and adolescent health, sexual and reproductive health, treatment common illnesses, disability, MHPSS and GBV health services to crisis affected populations.
2. Reduce excess morbidity and mortality by timely detection and coordinated response to epidemic prone diseases.
3. Enhance resilience and promote humanitarian-development linkages to strengthen health system recovery and coping mechanisms.
This project is targeting 45,400 beneficiaries and will support them with lifesaving emergency health care and reproductive healthcare services through 12 Primary Health Care Units (PHCUs), 3 Primary Health Care Centers and mobile clinics that CH has been supporting in the targeted counties. CH will work with the State Ministry of Health in Bentiu and the County Health Departments in Leer, Mayendit, Koch, Panyijiar and Pariang, as well as the nutrition cluster for nutritional supplies to PHCCs, Protection and GBV sub cluster for reproductive health supplies and clinical management of rape, and the WASH cluster for WASH in health facilities. CH is a strong member of these clusters.
The project requires USD 1,100,000 to reach 45,400 vulnerable individuals in Leer, Koch, Mayendit, Panyijiar and Pariang.

Emergency Type: Conflict - Violence/clashes Comprehensive humanitarian nutrition services for IDPs, returnees and vulnerable residents Sudan is among the top four countries globally with the highest prevalence of global acute malnutrition (GAM) estimated at 13.6 percent. Following the conflict in May 2023, the acute malnutrition People in Need (PIN) increased by over 13% from 4.0 M in January to over 4.5M in May.  The nutrition situation is projected to continue worsening in 2024 aggravated by the conflict, deterioration in food security, health and WASH services and the continuing displacement. As a result, the 2024 PIN is estimated to increase by between 10% and 30% in non-IDP and frontline localities respectively; with an overall additional 4.1% increase from 2023 PIN levels reaching over 4.7M in 2024, the highest PIN ever estimated in Sudan. 

 About, 76% acutely malnourished under-five children, pregnant and Lactating women in host and IDP settings live in 103 localities (54% of the total localities in Sudan). These localities are most affected, classified with severity scale 3-5 for WASH, Health, and Food Security; above national average acute malnutrition PIN and very high GAM prevalence of 15% and above- the WHO emergency threshold.  Micronutrient malnutrition among children is also very high with 48% of under-five children suffering from anaemia most of which is due to iron deficiency.  Minimum dietary diversity among under-five is one of the lowest trailing at 25% which is projected have deteriorated further following the ongoing massive displacement that has disrupted feeding and caring practices.  
The proposed nutrition project aim is to improve equitable access to quality lifesaving curative and preventive services through the systematic provision of nutrition services  that includes; Preventive nutrition interventions focusing on  Maternal and Young child Nutrition (MYCN) & Infant and young child feeding practices, detection, referral and treatment of severe acute malnutrition  with and without medical complications as well as supplementation of moderate acute malnutrition among under-fives, Pregnant and lactating women and girls , Management of Small and Nutritionally at risk infants under-six months and their mothers (MAMI) and Nutrition Impact and Positive Practice (NIPP).The action will implemented in South Kordofan, Central Darfur, North Darfur, Sennar, Blue Nile, River Nile and Al Gezira states in which 25 localities with severity scale 3-5 will be covered. Vulnerable children under-five and PLWs are the main target of the project. Through SC -Nutrition interventions, a total of 323,298beneficiaries will benefit from the services provided, among them (71,287boys, 87,129girls, 163,233 women, 1,649 men. To reach the estimated targets and planned response scale up, the nutrition sector will deploy integrated response modalities with health sector, WASH, FSL, protection, education at facility and community levels. SC will deliver nutrition services through existing health facilities and outreach teams and at community such as mother-to mother support groups activities including IDPs and hard to reach areas, use of cash based interventions in one prioritized location in SK  to increase access and utilization of nutrition services through FSL will be used for most cases in need. In term of emergency response, rapid response mechanisms for timely delivery of nutrition interventions in the onset emergencies will applied. Specific nutrition response strategies will include scaling up the minimum preventive and protection lifesaving intervention package for prevention of malnutrition, treatment, and geographical coverage of severe and moderate acute malnutrition among the under-fives, strengthening referrals for children suffering from SAM with medical complication through provision of transportation costs to and from the SC, nutrition system capacity strengthening (capacity and infrastructure) will be done to facilitate provision of quality and people centered life-saving nutrition responses, timely delivery of core nutrition supplies.

Emergency Type: Conflict - Violence/clashes Provision of Lifesaving Emergency Nutrition and Recovery Response to IDPs and Host Communities in North Darfur, Sennar, RiverNile, RedSea, Al Jazirah and Blue Nile states According to the 2024 humanitarian needs and response overview, the current conflict in Sudan has created massive displacement, with over 6.1 million people forced to leave their homes in search of safety. Of the 4.85 million people displaced internally, 54 percent are women and over half are children under 18 years of age .Sudan is among the top four countries in the world with the highest prevalence of global acute malnutrition (GAM), with an estimated 13.6 percent. The nutrition outlook is expected to deteriorate in 2024 due to ongoing conflict, food security decline, and compromised health and WASH services, and prolonged displacement.
Sudan is one of the top four hunger hotspots of highest concern globally with a third of the population soon becoming food insecure. Malnutrition rates among under-five children are among the highest in the world and are an increasing concern in all states for children and pregnant or lactating women, raising the risks of compromised immune systems, vulnerability to disease, and associated mortality.
A household survey conducted in El Fasher locality in North Darfur state in July 2023 revealed that 72% of the households struggled to access nutritious food for their consumption mainly due to lack of money and not having income sources and 93% of the households did not have diverse food intake (less than 4 food groups). Reasons given to explain difficulty in accessing food or difficulty in getting adequate and diverse diet included: lack of money (56%), insecurity due to the current conflict (28%), unavailable of food in the market (9%), and high food prices (7%). 69% of the households did not seek nutritional support or assistance for specific health conditions or deficiencies and 24% of household heads were not aware of the recommended breastfeeding practices for infants and young children. Malnutrition-related diagnosis mainly OTP/TSFP/SC accounted for only 6% among the different of diagnosis people sought at the health facilities.
RI will target and prioritize the 2024 nutrition response based on six areas: (i) Prioritizing the youngest and most vulnerable children with the highest mortality risk, (ii) Providing life-saving preventive and protective nutrition package, (iii) Treating SAM cases with medical complications, (iv) Treating SAM cases without medical complications among children under-five years, (v) Implementing non-food and food-based malnutrition prevention programs, and (iv) Generating evidence for planning, advocating for resources and decision-making. RI will improve access to nutrition care and services in 81 primary healthcare facilities (47 in ND, 12 in BN, 4 in Sennar, 4 in River Nile, 4 in Red Sea, and 10 in Al Jazirah). Through the proposed nutrition services, RI will build the capacity of 324 (M: 156 and F: 168) nutrition workers through formal and on-the-job training that will strengthen service delivery at both facility and community levels. Furthermore, RI will strengthen the referral mechanism and will ensure that complicated SAM have access to stabilization centers.
Through the proposed project, RI intends to reach 207,664 (M: 67,648 and F: 140,016) 7) and will provide quality nutrition lifesaving and recovery services to conflict- and natural disaster-affected IDPs and host communities in six localities in North Darfur (El Fasher - 52,539, Mellit - 19,225, El Tawisha – 7,886, Kalemindo– 3,094, Dar Al Salam – 5,757 and Al Malha – 27,575); four localities in Blue Nile (Al Rosaries - 5,620, Damazine - 4,794, Geissan – 5,720, Wad Almahi – 1,148); two localities in Al Jazirah (Wad Madani – 10,833 and South Al Jazirah – 11,176); two localities in Sennar (Sennar – 10,746 and Singa – 8,597), two localities in River Nile (Atbara – 5,970 and Shendi – 7,642) and two localities in Red Sea (Port Sudan – 10,985 and Suakin – 8,358).

Emergency Type: Conflict - Displacement Delivery of Life-saving Healthcare Services to Conflict-affected Communities in Gedaref, Khartoum, South Kordofan, Blue Nile, White Nile, Red Sea, and Jazira states The project aims to reduce excess morbidity and mortality through improving access to life-saving preventive and curative health services in Jezira, White Nile, Red Sea, Gedaref, Khartoum, South Kordofan, and Blue Nile states in Sudan. The main beneficiaries are persons affected by the recent crisis caused by armed conflicts between the Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) including internally displaced communities (IDPs), and vulnerable host communities targeting children under five years of age, adolescent girls, women, boys and men. The project will hotspot areas affected by the current crisis as well as IDP-receiving states and will support the existing Ministry of Health (MoH) capacity to deliver lifesaving primary health care services, including management of communicable and non-communicable diseases, support reproductive; maternal, and child health services including strengthening of expanded program for immunization; mental health and psychosocial support. The IRC will build the capacity of MoH staff, and provide essential drugs and medical supplies, including supplies for infection prevention and control, as well as infrastructure improvement and surge teams in the form of mobile medical teams (MMTs) to quickly respond to health emergencies. This is well aligned with the IRC’s Sudan Response Strategy. 
Protection services will also be integrated into the IRC’s health programming to achieve greater outcomes for women and girls, including prevention and response to Gender Based Violence (GBV). Through a community-based approach, the project will ensure equity by supporting community health volunteers to provide community health packages to hard-to-reach and underserved communities. The IRC WASH teams will closely support the HF teams to improve facility WASH infrastructures and practices including medical and non-medical waste management, hand washing stations, and hygiene promotion. 
The IRC has a strong capacity to deliver health services in Sudan with current support including strengthening the MoH capacity to deliver integrated health services in Gedaref, Khartoum, Jazira, and Blue Nile states, and currently expanding to White Nile and Red Sea states. Since 2019, the IRC has supported the delivery of integrated health, nutrition, protection, livelihoods, and WASH services providing a one-stop center to deliver life-saving interventions to beneficiaries in a safe way. The IRC health technical excellence unit at the headquarter in NY with regional representation in Nairobi provides technical oversight and guidance for the adaptation of quality health standards, training, and technical supervision including frequent field presence to support country teams. Even in the face of the current crisis, the IRC has maintained in-country capacity and regional support to continue to deliver essential health services.

Project Start Date: 2024-10-15 - Project End Date: 2026-01-14
Project Code: CBPF-SUD-24-R-INGO-33469
Emergency Type: Conflict - Displacement Provision of Lifesaving Emergency Nutrition and Recovery Response to IDPs and Host Communities in North Darfur, Sennar, RiverNile, RedSea, Al Jazirah and Blue Nile states According to the 2024 humanitarian needs and response overview, the current conflict in Sudan has created massive displacement, with over 6.1 million people forced to leave their homes in search of safety. Of the 4.85 million people displaced internally, 54 percent are women and over half are children under 18 years of age .Sudan is among the top four countries in the world with the highest prevalence of global acute malnutrition (GAM), with an estimated 13.6 percent. The nutrition outlook is expected to deteriorate in 2024 due to ongoing conflict, food security decline, and compromised health and WASH services, and prolonged displacement.
Sudan is one of the top four hunger hotspots of highest concern globally with a third of the population soon becoming food insecure. Malnutrition rates among under-five children are among the highest in the world and are an increasing concern in all states for children and pregnant or lactating women, raising the risks of compromised immune systems, vulnerability to disease, and associated mortality.
A household survey conducted in El Fasher locality in North Darfur state in July 2023 revealed that 72% of the households struggled to access nutritious food for their consumption mainly due to lack of money and not having income sources and 93% of the households did not have diverse food intake (less than 4 food groups). Reasons given to explain difficulty in accessing food or difficulty in getting adequate and diverse diet included: lack of money (56%), insecurity due to the current conflict (28%), unavailable of food in the market (9%), and high food prices (7%). 69% of the households did not seek nutritional support or assistance for specific health conditions or deficiencies and 24% of household heads were not aware of the recommended breastfeeding practices for infants and young children. Malnutrition-related diagnosis mainly OTP/TSFP/SC accounted for only 6% among the different of diagnosis people sought at the health facilities.
RI will target and prioritize the 2024 nutrition response based on six areas: (i) Prioritizing the youngest and most vulnerable children with the highest mortality risk, (ii) Providing life-saving preventive and protective nutrition package, (iii) Treating SAM cases with medical complications, (iv) Treating SAM cases without medical complications among children under-five years, (v) Implementing non-food and food-based malnutrition prevention programs, and (iv) Generating evidence for planning, advocating for resources and decision-making. RI will improve access to nutrition care and services in 81 primary healthcare facilities (47 in ND, 12 in BN, 4 in Sennar, 4 in River Nile, 4 in Red Sea, and 10 in Al Jazirah). Through the proposed nutrition services, RI will build the capacity of 324 (M: 156 and F: 168) nutrition workers through formal and on-the-job training that will strengthen service delivery at both facility and community levels. Furthermore, RI will strengthen the referral mechanism and will ensure that complicated SAM have access to stabilization centers.
Through the proposed project, RI intends to reach 207,664 (M: 67,648 and F: 140,016) 7) and will provide quality nutrition lifesaving and recovery services to conflict- and natural disaster-affected IDPs and host communities in six localities in North Darfur (El Fasher - 52,539, Mellit - 19,225, El Tawisha – 7,886, Kalemindo– 3,094, Dar Al Salam – 5,757 and Al Malha – 27,575); four localities in Blue Nile (Al Rosaries - 5,620, Damazine - 4,794, Geissan – 5,720, Wad Almahi – 1,148); two localities in Al Jazirah (Wad Madani – 10,833 and South Al Jazirah – 11,176); two localities in Sennar (Sennar – 10,746 and Singa – 8,597), two localities in River Nile (Atbara – 5,970 and Shendi – 7,642) and two localities in Red Sea (Port Sudan – 10,985 and Suakin – 8,358).

Emergency Type: Conflict - Violence/clashes Shelter /NFIs services for emergency affected people in, Khartoum, Al Jazeera, Kassala, Al Gedaref, Port Sudan, East Darfur, and South Darfur states Timely life-saving Shelter and NFI assistance is essential to prevent physical hazard and ensure safety, security, and dignity of IDPs and vulnerable residents. The purpose of the project is to contribute to improving protection, safety & security, and dignity of new IDPs through provision of life-saving assistance, and extremely vulnerable people as well as PWSNs living in protracted displacement with more sustainable, emergency-recovery type of interventions. The project targets localities in Khartoum, Al Jazeera, East and
South Darfur states that experienced several displacements in 2023 and are still hotspot areas. The project basically targets two groups; first new crises-affected people will be provided with emergency shelter making materials & NFI assistance. Second, people living in protracted displacement will be supported with replenishment of S/NFI and shelter upgrading solutions. Based on the experience, in this project we planned to support 79,765 people (about 15,953 HHs) by ES/NFIs. To achieve the above purposes Alight will monitor situations, preparing hotspot areas and identifying affected & vulnerable communities, and raising awareness of the communities on hazards. We regularly coordinate with HAC and UNHCR to exchange information on existing humanitarian situations. Whenever responses are required (suppose conditions
worsen or new humanitarian conditions emerge such as displacement of people due to conflict or extreme hazard (drought/flood)) then Alight will trigger joint need assessment (with state level stakeholders), conduct joint verification exercises and response plans. Any response prioritization will be done through cluster conventional processes. Activities that are in line with cluster objectives and relevant to the locality culture and traditions are carefully selected and will be implemented to deliver effective responses.
Wherever and whenever possible Cash Base intervention (CBI) (up to 20% of total budget) will be applied to help households fulfill their S/NFI needs. Alight will engage local authorities, COR, HAC, UNHCR and other key partners and jointly monitor and Supervise distributions and conduct Post distribution evaluation and document learnings.
To make this project a success, Alight uses its leverage of cumulated knowledge and experience. During implementation, Alight will work with the communities and local administrations, mobilize its potential suppliers and transporters, which will help to timely responses. Also, in case NFI gaps occur in the market Alight will utilize the Core Pipeline to respond to emergencies. As much as possible uniformity of responses will be respected by applying standardized NFI packages and Standard Operating Procedures
(SOPs) developed by the ES/NFI cluster. Wherever necessary to deliver holistic response,
Alight will combine WASH and protection responses with the S/NFI distribution. As much as possible Alight will respect and take care of the environment, culture, traditions and local businesses. We will use environmentally friendly and culturally appropriate shelter materials, most of the procurements will be locally sourced, which will help to activate local economies. Alight also provides on-the-job training in building techniques of shelters that will be useful for developing self-reliance and resilience. To improve accountability, transparency in programming, and adherence to “Do no harm principles,” Alight will strengthen the capacity of staff (men, women, and youth) and local national NGOs through training in the complete package of PSET for emergency response. Additionally, Alight will implement the project by considering protection and accountability to the community and to the donor. Our MEAL system will gather important data and produce information. Communities will be provided with information about our
complaints and feedback systems and Alight document complaints, refer and take corrective measures.

Allocation Type: Reserve - 2024 - SHF Reserve for Emergencies (Lifesaving response to displacement and famine in Sudan)
Life-Saving IDP and Famine Response in North Darfur State: Addressing Urgent Needs in Dar Al-Salam and Al-Fasher
Project Start Date: 2024-10-15 - Project End Date: 2025-10-14
Project Code: CBPF-SUD-24-R-INGO-33634
Emergency Type: Conflict - Displacement Provision of Lifesaving Emergency Nutrition and Recovery Response to IDPs and Host Communities in North Darfur, Sennar, RiverNile, RedSea, Al Jazirah and Blue Nile states According to the 2024 humanitarian needs and response overview, the current conflict in Sudan has created massive displacement, with over 6.1 million people forced to leave their homes in search of safety. Of the 4.85 million people displaced internally, 54 percent are women and over half are children under 18 years of age .Sudan is among the top four countries in the world with the highest prevalence of global acute malnutrition (GAM), with an estimated 13.6 percent. The nutrition outlook is expected to deteriorate in 2024 due to ongoing conflict, food security decline, and compromised health and WASH services, and prolonged displacement.
Sudan is one of the top four hunger hotspots of highest concern globally with a third of the population soon becoming food insecure. Malnutrition rates among under-five children are among the highest in the world and are an increasing concern in all states for children and pregnant or lactating women, raising the risks of compromised immune systems, vulnerability to disease, and associated mortality.
A household survey conducted in El Fasher locality in North Darfur state in July 2023 revealed that 72% of the households struggled to access nutritious food for their consumption mainly due to lack of money and not having income sources and 93% of the households did not have diverse food intake (less than 4 food groups). Reasons given to explain difficulty in accessing food or difficulty in getting adequate and diverse diet included: lack of money (56%), insecurity due to the current conflict (28%), unavailable of food in the market (9%), and high food prices (7%). 69% of the households did not seek nutritional support or assistance for specific health conditions or deficiencies and 24% of household heads were not aware of the recommended breastfeeding practices for infants and young children. Malnutrition-related diagnosis mainly OTP/TSFP/SC accounted for only 6% among the different of diagnosis people sought at the health facilities.
RI will target and prioritize the 2024 nutrition response based on six areas: (i) Prioritizing the youngest and most vulnerable children with the highest mortality risk, (ii) Providing life-saving preventive and protective nutrition package, (iii) Treating SAM cases with medical complications, (iv) Treating SAM cases without medical complications among children under-five years, (v) Implementing non-food and food-based malnutrition prevention programs, and (iv) Generating evidence for planning, advocating for resources and decision-making. RI will improve access to nutrition care and services in 81 primary healthcare facilities (47 in ND, 12 in BN, 4 in Sennar, 4 in River Nile, 4 in Red Sea, and 10 in Al Jazirah). Through the proposed nutrition services, RI will build the capacity of 324 (M: 156 and F: 168) nutrition workers through formal and on-the-job training that will strengthen service delivery at both facility and community levels. Furthermore, RI will strengthen the referral mechanism and will ensure that complicated SAM have access to stabilization centers.
Through the proposed project, RI intends to reach 207,664 (M: 67,648 and F: 140,016) 7) and will provide quality nutrition lifesaving and recovery services to conflict- and natural disaster-affected IDPs and host communities in six localities in North Darfur (El Fasher - 52,539, Mellit - 19,225, El Tawisha – 7,886, Kalemindo– 3,094, Dar Al Salam – 5,757 and Al Malha – 27,575); four localities in Blue Nile (Al Rosaries - 5,620, Damazine - 4,794, Geissan – 5,720, Wad Almahi – 1,148); two localities in Al Jazirah (Wad Madani – 10,833 and South Al Jazirah – 11,176); two localities in Sennar (Sennar – 10,746 and Singa – 8,597), two localities in River Nile (Atbara – 5,970 and Shendi – 7,642) and two localities in Red Sea (Port Sudan – 10,985 and Suakin – 8,358).

•	Assurer un ciblage géographique en coordination et en synergie avec le cluster nutrition et la section nutrition de l’UNICEF en vue de toucher les poches de malnutrition aigüe sévère, particulièrement dans les zones impactées par l’insécurité

Renforcer des capacités des mères /accompagnant - enfant malnutri  pour une meilleure connaissance et adoption des pratiques d'hyygiène

Emergency Type: Climate / natural disaster - Flood Appui à la qualité et à l'inclusion de l’éducation dans un environnement sûr pour les enfants filles et garçons impactés par les crises humanitaires  dans les régions de Tillabéry, Tahoua , Maradi et Diffa, La présente réponse éducation de l’Unicef contribuera à la  la prise en charge d'une proportion d'enfants et adolescents non scolarisés et/ou déscolarisés  dans le contexte d'EiE. La vision est d’assurer la continuité educative perturbée par la fermeture de nombreuses écoles, le mariage des enfants et la paupérisation des communautés, qui constituent des privations d' accès à des opportunités d'apprentissage alternatives et flexibles   
L’intervention sera menée de façon coordonnée avec les autorités éducatives et les communautés. L’objectif est de mobiliser les communautés autour de l’école en y incluant les enfants qui n’ont pas intégré le système éducatif, ou qui l’ont quitté précocement, et en mobilisant la communauté autour des thématiques essentielles en matière de droits à l’éducation. Capitalisant sur les acquis des pratiques éducatives le projet mettra en place une gamme variée d’offres éducatives non formelles en vue de lever les obstacles à la scolarisation des enfants et assurer leur enrôlement, maintien et transition vers d’autres opportunités d’éducation ou de formation. Le segment formel sera soutenu et appuyé pour accroitre les capacités d’accueil, en équipement, matériels et fournitures scolaires pour répondre au reversement des formules SSAP et CEA et à la demande. Un accent sera mis sur le développement professionnel des enseignants et des appuis matériels pédagogiques conséquents en vue d’asseoir la qualité des interventions développées et stimuler la rétention des enfants au sein de ces programmes.  Cette intervention contribuera également à une meilleure protection des enfants en veillant à ce qu'ils ne soient pas exposés à des risques de protection (VBG, exploitation sociale…). Un accent particulier sera mis sur la protection des écoles dans une approche contextualisée à travers la mise à jour et ou la mise en place des plans de préparation et réponses aux urgences dans les écoles de concert avec les communautés.
Il sera fait usage du transfert monétaire conditionnel pour briser la barrière économique au retour et ou inscription des populations les plus vulnérables ou encore pour le maintien des filles et enfants handicapés.
Le projet s’aligne sur les objectifs ci-dessous du Cluster.
1. OSS 2.1.1 : Accès à des offres éducatives inclusives et de qualité pour les enfants déplacés, les réfugiés et la communauté d'accueil  pour les  enfants de 6 à 17 ans touchés par les crises humanitaires,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      2. OSS 2.1.2 : Assurer un environnement d'apprentissage sûr pour les enfants déplacés, réfugiés et de la communauté d'accueil,                                                                
3. OSS 3.3.1 : Les enfants et le personnel scolaire des écoles vulnérables sont soutenus dans la préparation et la réponse aux urgences

Allocation Type: Rapid Response - CERF Rapid Response: Niger Jul 2024 (Anticipatory Action - Floods)
Actions anticipatoires face aux inondations  du Fleuve Niger
Project Start Date: 2024-12-03 - Project End Date: 2025-06-02
Project Code: CERF-NER-24-RR-FAO-33347
Emergency Type: Climate / natural disaster - Flood Assistance  agricole d'urgence pour soutenir les moyens d'existence des populations vulnérables dans les 7 régions du Niger. Le projet vise à contribuer à l'amélioration des moyens d'existence des populations affectées par les chocs  naturelles et anthropiques dans 7 régions du Niger notamment les  régionss de Diffa, Tillabéri, Tahoua, Maradi, Zindier, Dosso et Agadez. Le projet touchera 84 009 ménages  en semence pluviale et outils agricoles, la  réhabilitaion de 4500 ha, l'appui en semence de contre saison de 30 ménages et l'appui en AGR pour transformation agro alimentaire des 4000 femmes.  D'après les analyses de la campagne pluviale 2023, la production  céréalière 2023 est  en baisse de 14% par rapport à l’année 2022 et de 4% par rapport à la moyenne des cinq dernières années. Selon les données d'analyse du cadre harmonisé de novembre 2023, pendant la période d'octobre à décembre 2023, 2.318.639 personnes, soit 8,87% de la population du Niger (contre 1.044.331 personnes en  Novembre 2022) seront en insécurité alimentaire sévère (crise et plus) dont 42 921 personnes en urgence alimentaire. Cette situation se déteriorerait en période de soudure 2024 pour atteindre 3 231 825 personnes qui seraient en insécurité alimentaire sévère soit 12,36% de la population totale (crise et plus) contre 2 872 278 personnes pour la soudure 2023 . 
Les ménages seront appuyés en semences de mil et niébé pour la saison pluviale, et en semences irriguées pour la contresaison. Chaque ménage recevra en cultures pluviales 10 kg de mil et 5 kg de niébé  et en cultures irriguées 40 g de semences potagères (tomate, chou, laitue, carotte) et 5 kg de maïs. Pour la contre-saison des appuis en intrants agricoles  pour les cultures irriguées seront distribués à 30 000 ménages. Au moins 10 % des bénéficiaires d’intrants agricoles pour la campagne hivernale seront les femmes cheffes de ménages. Les  femmes seront concernées par les activités génératrices des revenus.

Allocation Type: Rapid Response - CERF Rapid Response: Niger Jul 2024 (Anticipatory Action - Floods)
Mitiger l'impact des inondations sur le bien être des femmes et des filles en garantissant l'accès aux services de Santé de la Reproduction et des biens de première nécessité pour la dignité.
Project Start Date: 2024-12-03 - Project End Date: 2025-06-02
Project Code: CERF-NER-24-RR-FPA-33348
Emergency Type: Climate / natural disaster - Flood Interventions vitales en Santé Sexuelle et Reproductive dans les régions affectées par la crise L’offre de soins complets de santé sexuelle et reproductive (SSR) à tous les membres d’une population affectée par une crise constitue un objectif global du secteur de la santé. Au Niger nous assistons à une complexité des crises affectant tous les secteurs et une raréfaction des ressources financières et la prise en compte des interventions sur la santé sexuelle et reproductive est souvent négligée ou n'est pas considéré comme prioritaire. Cette situation à des conséquences dramatiques en termes de morbidité et mortalité maternelles et néonatales: les conséquences évitables de la grossesse non désirée comme l’avortement à risques; et les conséquences évitables de la violence sexuelle comme les grossesses non désirées, la contamination accrue par les infections sexuellement transmissibles (IST), la transmission accrue du VIH, les problèmes de santé mentale ; les complications obstétricales sont autant des causes fréquentes de mortalité maternelle et des morbidités graves comme la dépression, des séquelles post traumatique ou la fistule obstétricale. Pour éviter d'aboutir à toutes ces conséquences potentiellement meurtrières pour les femmes et les filles, l'UNFPA propose des interventions qui sauvent la vie des femmes et des filles selon un dispositif minimum d'urgence en santé de la reproduction et dont les objectifs s'articulent en 6 points: (i) la mise en place d'une coordination des interventions SR aussi bien dans les régions affectées qu'au niveau national, il s'agira de faire une cartographie exhaustive des organisations mettant en œuvre des activités SR et s'assurer d'une bonne répartition géographique des intervenants. (ii) Prévenir la violence sexuelle et répondre aux besoins des survivantes, il s'agit d'assurer la disponibilité des kits et former les prestataires des services dans les zones affectées à la prise en charge clinique des viols sans oublier l'aspect prévention par des sensibilisation en communauté mais aussi s'assurer que les installations des sites d'accueil des personnes déplacées ou des réfugiées ne comportent pas des risques des violences sexuelles. Prévenir la transmission et réduire la morbidité et la mortalité en raison du VIH et d’autres IST. Prévenir la surmorbidité et la surmortalité maternelle et néonatale en assurant les fonctions des soins obstétricaux et néonataux d'urgence (SONU) des zones affectées mais aussi en assurant un système de référencement efficace pour la gestion des complications obstétricales. Prévenir les grossesses non désirées par la distribution des préservatifs et la mise à disposition de la contraception d'urgence. Les principaux bénéficiaires sont les femmes et les filles les nouveaux nés, mais le projet cible aussi les hommes dans son aspect prévention

Allocation Type: Rapid Response - CERF Rapid Response: Niger Jul 2024 (Anticipatory Action - Floods)
Assistance humanitaire anticipatoire pou les populations affectées pour faire face aux inondations dans les régions de Dosso et de Tillabéri
Project Start Date: 2024-12-03 - Project End Date: 2025-06-02
Project Code: CERF-NER-24-RR-IOM-33353
Emergency Type: Climate / natural disaster - Flood Assistance humanitaire en abri et en Biens non-alimentaires (BNA) pour les sinistrés d'inondation au Niger Dans le cadre de HRP 2023 au travers de ce projet, l'OIM vise à apporter un appui au gouvernement du Niger dans le cadre de la réponse d'urgence aux personnes sinistrées des inondations. Ce projet propose de répondre aux besoins des ménages sinistrés à travers les requêtes qui seront exprimées par le Gouvernement au travers du Ministère de l’Action Humanitaire et de la Gestion des Catastrophes (MAH/GC). Cette réponse s’adressera uniquement aux ménages vulnérables victimes d’inondations dont les abris ou cases auront été effondrées et/ou ceux dont les Biens non-alimentaires (BNA) auront été emportés par les eaux. Le présent projet poursuit comme objectif d’atteindre 10 000 ménages soit 70 000 personnes à travers tout le Niger prioritairement dans les régions de Zinder, Diffa, Maradi et Tahoua. En coordination avec le MAH/GC et la Direction Générale de la Protection Civile (DGPC), l’OIM mettra à disposition 10 000 kits abris et 10 000 kits Biens non-alimentaires qui seront distribués aux ménages sinistrés. En plus des kits, l’OIM couvrira les coûts liés à la logistique et à la distribution des kits. Ce projet ne couvrira pas une zone ou région donnée mais permettra d’intervenir là où les besoins se présentent et aussi de pouvoir compléter les activités des autres acteurs en cas de besoin en tant que prestataire de dernier recours pour la réponse humanitaire en abri d'urgence et BNA. L’OIM en tant que Co-Lead du Groupe de Travail Abri et Bien non-alimentaire (GTABNA) avec le MAH/GC s'assurera que les activités sont menées en étroite coordination avec les autres partenaires humanitaires membres du GTABNA pour la réponse en abri et Biens non-alimentaires pour les ménages sinistrés des inondations au Niger. Conformément à la logique de la stratégie du Secteur abris/BNA et en fonction de la faisabilité, les interventions pourront se faire en transferts monétaires conditionnels. Cela réduirait considérablement les coûts logistiques qui sont très élevés en période hivernale à cause du mauvais état des routes mais aussi et permettrait aussi de résoudre en partie le problème d’accès lié à l'insécurité qui souvent retarde les interventions. Enfin, la mise en œuvre du présent projet fera l’objet d’un suivi régulier de la qualité des interventions réalisées mais aussi de l’implication des bénéficiaires et autorités locales. Pour cela, les feedbacks de la communauté cible seront collectés à travers des évaluations post-distribution et des séances de discussion de groupe séparées par genre et âge avant et après l'assistance. Aussi, en tant qu’acteur humanitaire, l'OIM et ses partenaires de mise en œuvre s’assureront que ses actions n’induisent aucune tension ou problème dans la zone et n’exposent pas les bénéficiaires. A cet effet la phase d'évaluation de besoins sera réalisée de commun accord avec les populations dans les communes ciblées, les sessions d'information sur le projet seront organisées à l'attention de communauté bénéficiaires, le mecanisme de ciblage de bénéficiaires sera réalisé en étroite collabation avec les autorités au niveau local (do no harm). Une collaboration étroite faite avec les acteurs de protection pour un suivi de près de toutes questions de protection et de LTB. Le cout total du projet sera de 6.090.000 USD.

Allocation Type: Rapid Response - CERF Rapid Response: Sudan 2024 (Famine)
Provision of integrated nutrition, health, and WASH services to the 19 localities at the highest risk of famine.
Project Start Date: 2024-10-15 - Project End Date: 2025-04-14
Project Code: CERF-SDN-24-RR-CEF-33778
Emergency Type: Conflict - Displacement UNICEF: Lifesaving nutrition preventive and curative interventions targeting most vulnerable population across Sudan The malnutrition situation in Sudan remains dire with an expected increase in the number of children with acute malnutrition due to the deteriorating nutrition determinants as result of the ongoing catastrophic humanitarian crisis. The nutrition sector estimates that 4.7 million children under five and pregnant and lactating women are acutely malnourished and in need humanitarian assistance in 2024.

Through this project, UNICEF aims to (1) increase equitable access to an integrated lifesaving and preventive nutrition services focusing more on the “1000- day window”- as a critical opportunity to prevent child wasting and stunting among under five children, (2) improve early detection of acute malnutrition (3) improve access to quality lifesaving nutrition services to treat severe acute malnutrition among under-five children. UNICEF will target all states in the country with more focus on hotspots and IDP hosting states through scaling up integrated lifesaving nutrition preventive and curative services.

The preventive package includes iron-folate supplementation for pregnant and lactating women, maternal, infant and young child feeding nutrition (MIYCN) counseling and support for pregnant and lactating women. The package for under five children includes the provision of micronutrient supplements, Growth Monitoring and Promotion, as well as deworming. Overall, 1.4 million pregnant and lactating women, and over 4.9 million under five will be targeted with the preventive package. Additionally, UNICEF will support the provision of cash transfers to 150,000 of the poorest pregnant women and caregivers of children under-two to help eliminate the financial barriers that women and children may experience in accessing nutritious diets and essential nutrition services. UNICEF will ensure more focus on IYCF-E interventions as part of emergency preparedness and response, with intensive advocacy and orientations to mobilize humanitarian partners to protect and support infant feeding in the emergency context.

The armed conflict that began on 15 April 2023, between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) led to an overall increase in WASH needs, affecting approximately 18.9 million individuals, with the cluster targeting 8.9 million people. The primary focus of the relief effort is to assist those who are recently displaced, individuals stranded in certain areas, and families congregating at designated points. Assistance is particularly aimed at vulnerable groups such as women, children, the elderly, persons with disabilities or other vulnerabilities. Additionally, efforts are being made to address the needs of individuals affected by epidemics, natural disasters, and the consequences of climate change, notably water scarcity and floods. This project aims to provide humanitarian WASH assistance to 900,000 beneficiaries including 183,600 women, 176,400 men, 275,400 girls, and 264,600 boys with approximately 12 per cent of the target population estimated to be either elderly, people with disabilities, or individuals with other vulnerabilities. IOM aims to assist approximately 450,000 internally displaced persons (IDPs) newly displaced by conflict or disasters related to natural hazards with WASH services and improve and sustain access to safe water for approximately 400,000 individuals including returnees and crisis-affected communities. The project will focus on crisis impacted communities in various states primarily in areas where water infrastructure is damaged or available capacity is unable to meet the critical needs stretched by the influx of the displaced. IOM will also support communities to improve hygiene through sustaining access to safe water and sanitation facilities and promoting hygiene messages to address and increase community resilience to malnutrition, disease outbreaks, and other public health related risks targeting approximately 50,000 individuals. IOM will provide emergency water assistance through the establishment and rehabilitation of water points, access to proper sanitation facilities and hygiene items and campaigns. This will include environmental impact mitigation such as the provision of solar technology to power water points and monitoring ground water to moderate depletion levels. Food Assistance Programme Niger Country Strategic Plan La vision de la réponse aux urgences dans le cadre du Plan Stratégique Pays (PSP) 2020-2024 du PAM Niger est la réduction de l’empreinte humanitaire dans la mise en oeuvre de l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences du PSP à travers la promotion de l’approche NEXUS. Cette réponse s’inscrit dans la Stratégie de Prévention et de Gestion des Crises Alimentaires 2021 – 2025 du Dispositif National de Prévention et de Gestion de Crises Alimentaires (DNPGCA). Ce plan s’inscrit également dans le Plan d’Action 2021-2024 du Comité Technique Tripartite sur le Nexus Urgence-Développement (CTTNUD), en vue d’une mobilisation des ressources fi nancières pour une planification et une mise en œuvre concertée des activités relatives à la promotion du NEXUS. Dans le cas spécifique de l’assistance aux retournés dans leurs villages d’origine, qui est envisagée depuis 2022, la Loi 2018-74, relative à la protection et à l’assistance aux Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI) cadrera le processus. Rappelons que l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences s’inscrit dans l’effet direct stratégique 1 du CSP (2020-2024) du PAM Niger « Les populations affectées, y compris les réfugiés, les personnes déplacées internes, les communautés hôtes et les retournés dans les zones ciblées sont en mesure de répondre aux besoins alimentaires minimums pendant et après la crise ». La réponse aux urgences du PAM concernant la SECAL, basée sur une approche flexible, concernera toutes les trois (3) composantes de cette réponse en 2023 :
• Le Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM)
• La réponse aux crises prolongées.
• La réponse à la soudure agricole et pastorale.
Par ailleurs la prévention de la malnutrition aux enfants 6-23 mois est combinée aux trois composantes ci-dessus.

Emergency Type: Conflict - Violence/clashes Comprehensive humanitarian nutrition services for IDPs, returnees and vulnerable residents Sudan is among the top four countries globally with the highest prevalence of global acute malnutrition (GAM) estimated at 13.6 percent. Following the conflict in May 2023, the acute malnutrition People in Need (PIN) increased by over 13% from 4.0 M in January to over 4.5M in May.  The nutrition situation is projected to continue worsening in 2024 aggravated by the conflict, deterioration in food security, health and WASH services and the continuing displacement. As a result, the 2024 PIN is estimated to increase by between 10% and 30% in non-IDP and frontline localities respectively; with an overall additional 4.1% increase from 2023 PIN levels reaching over 4.7M in 2024, the highest PIN ever estimated in Sudan. 

 About, 76% acutely malnourished under-five children, pregnant and Lactating women in host and IDP settings live in 103 localities (54% of the total localities in Sudan). These localities are most affected, classified with severity scale 3-5 for WASH, Health, and Food Security; above national average acute malnutrition PIN and very high GAM prevalence of 15% and above- the WHO emergency threshold.  Micronutrient malnutrition among children is also very high with 48% of under-five children suffering from anaemia most of which is due to iron deficiency.  Minimum dietary diversity among under-five is one of the lowest trailing at 25% which is projected have deteriorated further following the ongoing massive displacement that has disrupted feeding and caring practices.  
The proposed nutrition project aim is to improve equitable access to quality lifesaving curative and preventive services through the systematic provision of nutrition services  that includes; Preventive nutrition interventions focusing on  Maternal and Young child Nutrition (MYCN) & Infant and young child feeding practices, detection, referral and treatment of severe acute malnutrition  with and without medical complications as well as supplementation of moderate acute malnutrition among under-fives, Pregnant and lactating women and girls , Management of Small and Nutritionally at risk infants under-six months and their mothers (MAMI) and Nutrition Impact and Positive Practice (NIPP).The action will implemented in South Kordofan, Central Darfur, North Darfur, Sennar, Blue Nile, River Nile and Al Gezira states in which 25 localities with severity scale 3-5 will be covered. Vulnerable children under-five and PLWs are the main target of the project. Through SC -Nutrition interventions, a total of 323,298beneficiaries will benefit from the services provided, among them (71,287boys, 87,129girls, 163,233 women, 1,649 men. To reach the estimated targets and planned response scale up, the nutrition sector will deploy integrated response modalities with health sector, WASH, FSL, protection, education at facility and community levels. SC will deliver nutrition services through existing health facilities and outreach teams and at community such as mother-to mother support groups activities including IDPs and hard to reach areas, use of cash based interventions in one prioritized location in SK  to increase access and utilization of nutrition services through FSL will be used for most cases in need. In term of emergency response, rapid response mechanisms for timely delivery of nutrition interventions in the onset emergencies will applied. Specific nutrition response strategies will include scaling up the minimum preventive and protection lifesaving intervention package for prevention of malnutrition, treatment, and geographical coverage of severe and moderate acute malnutrition among the under-fives, strengthening referrals for children suffering from SAM with medical complication through provision of transportation costs to and from the SC, nutrition system capacity strengthening (capacity and infrastructure) will be done to facilitate provision of quality and people centered life-saving nutrition responses, timely delivery of core nutrition supplies.
